title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on work extraction from finite-time closed quantum dynamics, establishing a trade-off between power and efficiency.
motivation: Rapid quantum protocols are often desired, but the trade-off between power and efficiency in work extraction from closed quantum systems was not well understood.
method: The authors use optimal control theory and quantum thermodynamic principles to analyze work extraction under finite-time constraints, deriving bounds based on quantum speed limits.
result: They obtain a general bound relating the maximum extractable work to the protocol duration and the quantum Fisher information, revealing a power-efficiency trade-off.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits on work extraction in finite-time quantum processes, guiding the design of fast and efficient quantum engines.

title: Shake Before Use: Universal Enhancement Of Quantum Thermometry By Unitary Driving
authors: Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, And Giacomo Guarnieri
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, and Giacomo Guarnieri

Quantum thermometry aims at determining temperature with ultimate precision in the quantum regime. Standard equilibrium approaches, limited by the quantum Fisher information given by static energy fluctuations, lose sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window. Nonequilibrium strategies have there…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Universal enhancement of quantum thermometry precision via unitary driving, overcoming equilibrium limitations.
motivation: Standard equilibrium quantum thermometry loses sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window; nonequilibrium strategies can improve precision.
method: The authors propose a universal unitary driving protocol that enhances the quantum Fisher information for temperature estimation, applicable to any quantum probe.
result: The protocol achieves a significant improvement in thermometric precision, independent of the specific system or temperature range.
conclusion: Unitary driving provides a universal and practical method to enhance quantum thermometry, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and sensing.

title: Enhanced Performance Of Sudden-quench Quantum Otto Cycles Via Multiparameter Control
authors: R. S. Watson And K. V. Kheruntsyan
abstract:
Author(s): R. S. Watson and K. V. Kheruntsyan

The authors present a theoretical framework to investigate quantum thermodynamic Otto cycles operating under the simultaneous sudden quench of multiple externally tunable control parameters. Applying this formalism to both a harmonically trapped one-dimensional Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model, they demonstrate that multiparameter control yields a significant cooperative enhancement to net work and efficiency, dramatically outperforming the combined output of individual single-parameter cycles.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063319] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Multiparameter control in sudden-quench quantum Otto cycles enhances work output and efficiency beyond single-parameter cycles.
motivation: To explore whether simultaneously quenching multiple control parameters can improve the performance of quantum thermodynamic cycles beyond what is achievable with individual quenches.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for quantum Otto cycles with multiple sudden quenches and apply it to a harmonically trapped 1D Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model.
result: Multiparameter control yields a cooperative enhancement in net work and efficiency, significantly outperforming the sum of individual single-parameter cycles.
conclusion: Multiparameter control is a promising strategy for optimizing quantum heat engines and refrigerators.

title: Power Of Quantum Catalytic Local Operations
authors: Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, And Pavel Sekatski
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, and Pavel Sekatski

A key result in entanglement theory is that the addition of a catalyst dramatically enlarges the set of possible state transformations via local operations and classical communication (LOCC). However, it remains unclear what is the interplay between classical communication and quantum catalysis. Her…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062216] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum catalysis, using a catalyst that is returned unchanged, can enhance the power of local operations without classical communication, enabling transformations that are impossible with LOCC alone.
motivation: Understanding the role of classical communication in entanglement transformations is fundamental; previous work showed catalysts enlarge the set of achievable states under LOCC, but the interplay between catalysis and communication was unclear.
method: The authors develop a resource-theoretic framework for catalytic local operations (without classical communication) and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for state transformations using a catalyst, employing techniques from entanglement theory and convex optimization.
result: They prove that catalytic local operations can achieve transformations that are impossible with LOCC, even with unlimited classical communication, and provide explicit examples and a complete characterization for pure states.
conclusion: Quantum catalysis provides a genuine advantage over LOCC, revealing that the power of local operations is significantly enhanced by catalysts, independent of classical communication.

title: Response Kinetic Uncertainty Relation For Markovian Open Quantum Systems
authors: Kangqiao Liu And Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Kangqiao Liu and Jie Gu

Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics extend precision bounds to the sensitivity of observables under external perturbations. Here we derive a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for continuously monitored Markovian open quantum systems in the steady state of the Lind…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062443] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for Markovian open quantum systems, extending precision bounds to sensitivity under perturbations.
motivation: Extend classical response uncertainty relations to the quantum domain, providing fundamental bounds on the precision of observables in open quantum systems.
method: Uses Lindblad master equation formalism and continuously monitored quantum trajectories to derive a kinetic uncertainty relation for response coefficients.
result: Establishes a trade-off between the sensitivity of an observable to perturbations and the dynamical activity or entropy production rate.
conclusion: The quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation provides a thermodynamic bound on precision in quantum sensing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum f-divergences, linking distinguishability to thermodynamic cost.
motivation: To establish a general bound on the distinguishability of quantum states in terms of thermodynamic quantities, extending classical thermodynamic uncertainty relations to the quantum regime.
method: The author shows that any Petz f-divergence (with operator convex f) can be expressed as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts, and then derives a universal inequality relating the divergence to the average of a thermodynamic cost function.
result: A universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum f-divergences is obtained, which generalizes previous results and provides a unified framework for thermodynamic bounds on state distinguishability.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental link between quantum information measures and thermodynamics, with implications for understanding the thermodynamic cost of quantum information processing.

title: Autonomous Quantum Thermodynamics With A Quantum Kicked Top Reservoir
authors: Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, And You-Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, and You-Yang Xu

We develop an operational framework to characterize energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite, dynamically tunable environment modeled by a quantum kicked top. Instead of relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, heat and work are defined through a weighted decomposition of…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an operational framework for autonomous quantum thermodynamics using a quantum kicked top as a finite, tunable reservoir, defining heat and work via weighted decomposition of energy changes.
motivation: Standard quantum thermodynamics often assumes large equilibrium reservoirs or external driving; this work aims to model energy exchange with a finite, dynamically controllable environment without those assumptions.
method: The authors model the reservoir as a quantum kicked top, a chaotic many-body system, and define heat and work through a weighted decomposition of the system's energy change, using the framework of autonomous quantum thermodynamics.
result: They demonstrate that the kicked top reservoir can simulate thermalization and work extraction, with the ability to tune the effective temperature and coupling strength, enabling controlled thermodynamic processes.
conclusion: The quantum kicked top provides a versatile platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics in a finite, controllable setting, bridging quantum chaos and thermodynamics.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system using nonreciprocal and chiral magnons in a magnet to mediate dissipative, unidirectional coupling of spin qubits, achieving steady-state Bell state entanglement.
motivation: To generate steady-state entanglement between spin qubits without active feedback or fine-tuning, leveraging the unique properties of magnons in magnetic systems.
method: The system consists of spin qubits coupled to a magnet that supports nonreciprocal or chiral magnons; driving the qubits leads to dissipative coupling mediated by the magnons, resulting in a steady-state Bell state.
result: The steady state of the qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state, enabled by the nonreciprocal or chiral nature of the magnons.
conclusion: This hybrid platform offers a robust method for generating entanglement in quantum networks, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Probing Many-body Phenomena With Atomically Thin Nuclear Spin Layers In Diamond
authors: Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, And Fedor Jelezko
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, and Fedor Jelezko

Quantum simulation aims to recreate complex many-body phenomena in controlled environments, offering insights into dynamics that are otherwise difficult to model. Existing platforms, however, are often complex and costly to scale, typically requiring ultrapure vacuum or low temperatures. Here, we in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum simulator using atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond to probe many-body phenomena at room temperature.
motivation: Existing quantum simulation platforms are complex and costly; a simpler, scalable platform operating at ambient conditions is needed.
method: The authors use shallow nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond to control and read out a two-dimensional layer of 13C nuclear spins via dynamical decoupling sequences.
result: They observe coherent dynamics of up to 10 nuclear spins and simulate many-body Hamiltonians, including the formation of spin clusters and quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: This platform offers a scalable, room-temperature quantum simulator for studying many-body physics, with potential for integration into quantum networks.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic role of information flow in autonomous bipartite systems beyond the conventional decomposition of entropy production.
method: Uses geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to derive the decomposition, and applies it to a bipartite Markov jump process model.
result: The housekeeping information flow is linked to the breakdown of detailed balance, while the excess part captures the non-steady-state contribution; the decomposition provides a clear interpretation of information-thermodynamic quantities.
conclusion: The geometric decomposition offers new insights into the interplay between information and thermodynamics in autonomous systems, potentially applicable to biological and nanoscale information processing.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI-QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling over long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; this work aims to make DI-QKD practical over long ranges.
method: The schemes use spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics, with a focus on achieving key rates that scale proportionally to the channel transmittance.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rate scaling proportional to the channel transmittance, enabling long-distance DI-QKD with current technology.
conclusion: Long-distance DI-QKD is feasible with SPDC sources and linear optics, paving the way for practical secure quantum communication.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear operational boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, which is fundamental for understanding quantum resources and their applications.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and generalized probabilistic theories to classify processes as classical or quantum.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures and identifies new nonclassical features in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: Many processes considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantumness, which could be harnessed for quantum technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn cavity noise, typically detrimental, into a tool for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme, leveraging collective decay to stabilize desired entangled states. The reconfigurability is achieved by tuning external drives.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can produce steady-state entanglement with high fidelity, and demonstrate its application for ultraprecise sensing beyond the standard quantum limit and for engineering topological many-body states.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable and robust platform for generating multipartite entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and simulation.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit encoded in a bosonic mode against photon loss, without active syndrome measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the unprotected mode, reaching the breakeven point where the error-corrected lifetime equals the best possible without correction.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, suggesting a path toward simpler and more efficient quantum error correction for bosonic codes.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, revealing scaling laws for information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information is crucial for quantum computing and error correction; the paper aims to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size in certain measurement regimes, contrasting with the typical exponential decay of entanglement.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy for improving near-term quantum computers and algorithms.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with minimal experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to entangle spin ensembles, leveraging inhomogeneous broadening as a resource rather than a nuisance.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with overhead scaling favorably for 10–100 qubits, validated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking and computation.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum error-correcting codes, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding and revealing new insights into stability under partial measurement.
motivation: Understanding how random measurements affect quantum error-correcting codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum information theory.
method: The authors analyze monitored dynamics of quantum codes, deriving conditions for decodability based on measurement statistics and partial measurement stability.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and characterize logical measurement statistics that enable efficient decoding.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, offering new perspectives on code performance under realistic noise and measurement conditions.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a hierarchical method for generating tree-codes and optimizing asymmetric code geometries to improve quantum repeater performance and resource efficiency.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs often suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance. The authors aim to design more efficient codes that are practical for near-term implementations.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation algorithm and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage. They analyze the performance using numerical simulations.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve higher loss tolerance and lower resource requirements compared to symmetric codes, enabling more efficient quantum repeater architectures.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes significantly enhance the feasibility of quantum repeaters, bringing practical quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections. A method to integrate realistic device models into security proofs is needed for practical certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that incorporates device characterization data into composable security proofs, using entropy accumulation and smooth min-entropy techniques.
result: The framework yields tight security bounds that account for device imperfections, enabling rigorous certification of QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, providing a path to standardized security certification for quantum key distribution systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors limit qubit coherence; converting them to erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times compared to standard qubit operation.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling over Abelian groups to solve the state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian symmetries, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to states, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, addressing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity enhancement are promising for quantum computing but limited by serial addressing; multiplexing allows parallel operations to scale.
method: Uses multiple cavity modes (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian modes) to simultaneously address different atoms in the array, with each mode coupled to a distinct atom.
result: Demonstrates that mode multiplexing can achieve high-fidelity parallel operations without crosstalk, significantly increasing the number of atoms that can be processed.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing is a viable path to scalable quantum computing with neutral-atom arrays, combining cavity enhancement with parallelism.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous single-qubit, two-qubit gates, and readout with >99.9% fidelity in a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing; simultaneous operation is challenging due to crosstalk.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol to mitigate crosstalk and optimize gate performance.
result: Achieved >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device.
conclusion: The results show that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, advancing toward practical quantum computing.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics methods, mapping the decoding problem to a statistical mechanics model and studying its phase transitions.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases as a function of noise rate, with the transition point determined by the code's spectral properties.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical error-correcting codes.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using Clifford circuits doped with non-Clifford gates requires extensive T-gate doping, establishing a fundamental resource bound.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to achieve pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and cryptography.
method: The authors derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates (e.g., T gates) required for a Clifford circuit to approximate random unitaries, using techniques from quantum resource theory and circuit complexity.
result: They show that the number of non-Clifford gates must scale extensively with the number of qubits, implying that shallow doping is insufficient for pseudorandomness.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental limit on the efficiency of generating pseudorandom unitaries, with implications for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage experiments.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium where traditional Langevin approaches fail.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, and applies the framework to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent description of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production across scales, challenging Langevin-based approaches.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena in diverse systems, with implications for information thermodynamics and physical constraints on computation.

title: Entropic Limitations On Fixed Causal Order
authors: Matheus Capela And Kaumudibikash Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus Capela and Kaumudibikash Goswami

Quantum processes can exhibit scenarios beyond a fixed order of events. We propose information inequalities that, when violated, constitute sufficient conditions to certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order—either a classical mixture or a quantum superposition of causal orders. The ineq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062217] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives information inequalities that certify non-fixed causal order in quantum processes, linking causal structure to entropy constraints.
motivation: Understanding and certifying indefinite causal order is a fundamental question in quantum information, with implications for quantum computation and foundations.
method: The authors propose information inequalities based on entropy measures that, when violated, indicate the presence of a classical mixture or quantum superposition of causal orders.
result: They establish sufficient conditions for certifying processes without fixed causal order using information-theoretic criteria.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for detecting and characterizing indefinite causal order, advancing the theory of quantum causal structures.

title: Resource Theory Of Interactive Quantum Instruments
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Quantum instruments describe both the classical outcome and the updated quantum state in a measurement process. To do this in a nontrivial way, instruments must have the capability to interact coherently with the state that they measure. Here we develop a resource theory for instruments. We consider…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062445] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops a resource theory for quantum instruments, characterizing their ability to interact coherently with measured states.
motivation: Quantum instruments are fundamental in measurement theory, but their non-classical capabilities lack a unified resource-theoretic framework.
method: Defines free operations and resources for instruments, using concepts from quantum resource theories and channel theory.
result: Identifies a hierarchy of instrument resources, including coherence and entanglement, and provides monotones and conversion conditions.
conclusion: The resource theory offers a new perspective on quantum measurements and their operational power, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of quantum shadow enumerators in terms of two-copy Bell measurements and demonstrates their efficient experimental measurement on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for analyzing quantum error-correcting codes, but they lack a direct physical interpretation and are difficult to measure experimentally.
method: The authors show that Rains' quantum shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling efficient learning protocols. They implement these measurements on a trapped-ion device.
result: They experimentally extract shadow enumerators for small error-correcting codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the feasibility of the approach.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract enumerator theory and experimental quantum error correction, providing a practical tool for characterizing code performance.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories without assuming a specific quantum gravity framework.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several feasible experimental setups are identified that could detect gravitationally induced entanglement, providing a test of the quantum nature of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with near-term tabletop experiments being potentially viable.

title: Squeezing-Enhanced Sensing At An Exceptional Point
authors: Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, And Zheshen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, and Zheshen Zhang

Pushing the boundaries of measurement precision is central for sensing and metrology, pursued by nonclassical resources such as squeezing, as well as non-Hermitian degeneracies with distinct spectral response. Their convergence, however, remains challenging. We find extraordinary enhancement of sens…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250801] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Combining squeezing and exceptional points in a non-Hermitian system yields extraordinary enhancement of sensing precision.
motivation: Pushing measurement precision limits is central for sensing; both squeezing and exceptional points offer distinct advantages, but their convergence has been challenging.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a hybrid system where squeezed light interacts with a non-Hermitian resonator operating at an exceptional point.
result: They find that the combination leads to a sensitivity scaling beyond the standard quantum limit and beyond what either squeezing or exceptional points alone can achieve.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new paradigm for quantum-enhanced sensing by synergizing nonclassical resources with non-Hermitian degeneracies.

title: Clifford Hierarchy Stabilizer Codes: Transversal Non-Clifford Gates And Magic States
authors: Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, And Po-Shen Hsin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, and Po-Shen Hsin

A fundamental problem in fault-tolerant quantum computation is the tradeoff between universality and dimensionality, exemplified by the Bravyi-König bound for [MATH]-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. In this Letter, we extend topological Pauli stabilizer codes to a broad class of [MATH]-dimensiona…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends topological stabilizer codes to higher dimensions to achieve transversal non-Clifford gates and magic state distillation, circumventing the Bravyi-König bound.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires universal gate sets, but transversal gates are limited by the Bravyi-König bound for 2D topological codes. This work aims to overcome that limitation by considering higher-dimensional codes.
method: The authors construct a family of Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes in arbitrary dimensions, leveraging the structure of the Clifford hierarchy to design codes with transversal non-Clifford gates.
result: They demonstrate that these codes support transversal implementations of gates from the third level of the Clifford hierarchy and enable efficient magic state distillation.
conclusion: Higher-dimensional topological codes can provide a pathway to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with transversal gates, relaxing the constraints of the Bravyi-König bound.

title: Crosstalk Insensitive Trapped-Ion Entanglement Through Coupling Matrix Engineering
authors: Vikram Kashyap, Caleb Walton, And Sara Mouradian
abstract:
Author(s): Vikram Kashyap, Caleb Walton, and Sara Mouradian

Optical crosstalk due to imperfect addressing in trapped-ion entangling gates generates unwanted nonlocal entanglement between target ions and their combined set of neighbors that is difficult to mitigate using standard quantum error correction. We present a method to design entangling operations th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253601] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A method to design crosstalk-insensitive entangling gates in trapped-ion systems by engineering the coupling matrix.
motivation: Optical crosstalk in trapped-ion gates creates unwanted nonlocal entanglement that is hard to correct; existing methods are insufficient.
method: The authors engineer the coupling matrix of the entangling operation to suppress crosstalk to neighboring ions while maintaining gate fidelity.
result: They demonstrate that the engineered gates achieve high-fidelity entanglement with significantly reduced crosstalk compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical path to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing by mitigating a key error source.

title: Nonstabilizerness And Error Resilience In Noisy Quantum Circuits
authors: Fabian Ballar Trigueros And José Antonio Marín Guzmán
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Ballar Trigueros and José Antonio Marín Guzmán

We investigate how noise impacts nonstabilizerness—a key resource for quantum advantage—in many-body qubit systems. While noise typically degrades quantum resources, we show that amplitude damping, a nonunital channel, can generate or enhance nonstabilizerness, whereas depolarizing noise provably ca…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240602] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how noise affects nonstabilizerness (magic) in many-body qubit systems, finding that amplitude damping can generate or enhance it while depolarizing noise cannot.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its behavior under noise is poorly understood; understanding this is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: Analytical and numerical study of nonstabilizerness measures (e.g., stabilizer Rényi entropy) under amplitude damping and depolarizing noise in many-body qubit systems.
result: Amplitude damping, a nonunital channel, can generate or enhance nonstabilizerness, whereas depolarizing noise provably cannot; the effect is linked to the nonunital nature of the channel.
conclusion: Noise is not always detrimental to quantum resources; nonunital noise can actually boost magic, which has implications for error mitigation and resource theory.

title: Observing Fundamental Triple Uncertainty Relations
authors: Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

The uncertainty principle, arising from the incompatibility of noncommuting observables, constitutes one of the cornerstones of quantum mechanics. While uncertainty relations involving pairs of observables have been extensively investigated, experimentally accessible tight uncertainty relations for …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062447] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of tight triple uncertainty relations for three incompatible observables using photonic systems.
motivation: To test fundamental quantum uncertainty relations beyond pairwise ones, which are crucial for understanding quantum mechanics and applications in quantum information.
method: Implemented a photonic experiment with polarization and path qubits to measure triple uncertainty relations based on sum of variances and entropic measures.
result: Observed tight triple uncertainty relations that are stronger than those derived from pairwise relations, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence for fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing the understanding of quantum uncertainty and its information-theoretic implications.

title: Equilibrium Thermometry In The Multilevel Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, and Gerardo Adesso

The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the temperature sensitivity of a quantum probe in equilibrium using the quantum Rabi model, showing that degeneracy and spectral uniformity affect thermometric precision.
motivation: Quantum thermometry at the nanoscale is important for sensing and thermodynamics; understanding how probe structure limits sensitivity is key.
method: The authors compute the thermal quantum Fisher information for the multilevel quantum Rabi model, analyzing how energy-level degeneracy and spectral uniformity influence the achievable precision.
result: They find that degeneracy can enhance sensitivity, while a more uniform spectrum extends the range of temperatures over which the probe remains sensitive.
conclusion: The quantum Rabi model offers a tunable platform for equilibrium thermometry, with trade-offs between peak sensitivity and operational bandwidth.

title: Magnetometry With Broadband Microwave Fields In Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Diamond
authors: Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, And Khabat Heshami
abstract:
Author(s): Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, and Khabat Heshami

Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are optically addressable and versatile light-matter interfaces with practical application in magnetic-field sensing, offering the ability to operate at room temperature and reach sensitivities below pT/[MATH]. We propose an approach to simultan…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063113] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a magnetometry scheme using broadband microwave fields in NV centers to improve sensitivity and bandwidth.
motivation: NV centers are promising for magnetic sensing but conventional narrowband microwave excitation limits sensitivity and dynamic range.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a protocol using broadband microwave fields to simultaneously address multiple NV spin transitions, enhancing signal-to-noise ratio.
result: The broadband approach achieves higher sensitivity and faster acquisition compared to standard continuous-wave or pulsed methods.
conclusion: Broadband microwave excitation is a practical way to improve NV magnetometry performance without complex hardware.

title: Anticoncentration And State Design Of Doped Real Clifford Circuits And Tensor Networks
authors: Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, And Xhek Turkeshi
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, and Xhek Turkeshi

We investigate the statistical properties of orthogonal, or real, Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources. By developing the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, we derive the exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states, identifying a different universality cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062446] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops Weingarten calculus for real Clifford group to study anticoncentration and state design properties of doped real Clifford circuits and tensor networks.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of quantum circuits with magic resources is crucial for quantum computing and information theory, particularly for random circuit sampling and benchmarking.
method: Derives exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states using Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, and analyzes anticoncentration and state design properties of doped circuits.
result: Identifies a different universality class for real Clifford circuits compared to standard Clifford circuits, with implications for anticoncentration and approximate state designs.
conclusion: Doped real Clifford circuits exhibit distinct statistical behavior, which may affect their use in quantum information protocols and tensor network simulations.

title: Remote Nonreciprocal Optical-microwave Entanglement And One-way Steering Via Parametric Amplification
authors: Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, And Hao Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, and Hao Xiong

We propose a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between spatially separated optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification. Both entanglement and one-way steering emerge when the system is driven from a specific direction, while being fully suppressed…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063730] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification in a hybrid system.
motivation: To achieve directional quantum correlations between disparate frequency modes, which is crucial for quantum networks and hybrid quantum information processing.
method: Uses parametric amplification in a cavity optomechanical system with a nonlinear crystal to create nonreciprocal entanglement and steering between optical and microwave fields.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement and one-way steering can be generated when driven from a specific direction, and suppressed in the opposite direction, enabling remote nonreciprocal quantum correlations.
conclusion: The scheme provides a way to realize directional quantum interfaces between optical and microwave domains, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Almost Sure Minimality Of The Set Of Experiments With Classical Kirkwood-Dirac Representations
authors: Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan de Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, And David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan De Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, and David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

A central problem in quantum information is determining quantum-classical boundaries. In the quasiprobability framework, a state is called classical if it is represented by a quasiprobability distribution that is positive, and thus a probability distribution. In recent years, the Kirkwood-Dirac (KD)…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062215] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the set of quantum experiments with classical Kirkwood-Dirac representations is almost surely minimal, establishing a sharp quantum-classical boundary.
motivation: Determining when a quantum state admits a classical (positive) quasiprobability representation is a central problem in quantum information. The Kirkwood-Dirac distribution offers a framework to study this boundary.
method: The authors use measure-theoretic arguments and properties of the Kirkwood-Dirac distribution to characterize the set of experiments (POVMs and states) that yield positive KD distributions, showing that this set is meager (topologically small) in the space of all experiments.
result: The set of experiments with classical KD representations is almost surely minimal: it is a countable union of nowhere dense sets, meaning that almost all experiments are non-classical in this sense.
conclusion: The result sharpens the quantum-classical divide, indicating that classicality in the KD sense is extremely rare, which has implications for quantum foundations and resource theories.

title: Bootstrapping The Stationary State Of Bosonic Open Quantum Systems
authors: Gustave Robichon And Antoine Tilloy
abstract:
Author(s): Gustave Robichon and Antoine Tilloy

We propose a method to compute expectation values of observables in the stationary state of a (Markovian) bosonic open quantum system. Using a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations, we obtain finer and finer upper and lower bounds to any expectation value of interest. The bounds are rigorous, robust…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062440] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A method to compute stationary-state expectation values of bosonic open quantum systems using semidefinite relaxations, providing rigorous bounds.
motivation: Computing stationary states of open quantum systems is challenging; existing methods lack rigorous error bounds.
method: Uses a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations to obtain converging upper and lower bounds on expectation values.
result: The method yields rigorous, robust bounds for bosonic systems, demonstrated on examples.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for analyzing stationary states of bosonic open quantum systems with guaranteed accuracy.

title: Tighter Asymptotic Key Rates For Intensity-correlated Decoy-state Quantum Key Distribution Via Nonlinear Programming
authors: Matej Pivoluska And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Matej Pivoluska and Mateus Araújo

Decoy-state QKD with phase-randomized weak coherent pulses is typically analyzed assuming independent, precisely prepared intensities. Real sources, however, can exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, potentially leaking intensity information and breaking the standard decoy-state reductio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062441] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves asymptotic key rate bounds for decoy-state QKD with intensity-correlated sources using nonlinear programming.
motivation: Real QKD sources exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, which can leak intensity information and compromise standard decoy-state security proofs.
method: The authors formulate the key rate optimization as a nonlinear programming problem that accounts for intensity correlations, and solve it to obtain tighter bounds.
result: They derive significantly higher asymptotic key rates compared to previous analyses that assumed independent intensities, demonstrating the impact of properly modeling correlations.
conclusion: Accounting for intensity correlations in decoy-state QKD is crucial for accurate security analysis, and nonlinear programming provides a practical tool to compute tighter key rates.

title: Edge State Effects In Quantum Work Statistics
authors: Moallison F. Cavalcante
abstract:
Author(s): Moallison F. Cavalcante

Motivated by the objective of quantifying the energetic cost of accessing boundary phases through local control, we investigate here a simple, analytically tractable quantum impurity model. This model exhibits a rich boundary phase diagram, characterized by phases with different numbers of edge stat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the energetic cost of accessing boundary phases in a quantum impurity model by analyzing work statistics.
motivation: To quantify the thermodynamic cost of controlling edge states in quantum systems with boundary phases.
method: The authors use an analytically tractable quantum impurity model and compute work distribution statistics via full counting statistics or similar techniques.
result: They find that the work statistics are sensitive to the number of edge states, revealing distinct thermodynamic signatures for different boundary phases.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding the energetic implications of edge state manipulation, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Topological And Nontopological Defects From Quantum Reset Dynamics
authors: R. Jafari, Henrik Johannesson, And Sebastian Eggert
abstract:
Author(s): R. Jafari, Henrik Johannesson, and Sebastian Eggert

We analyze mechanisms for universal out-of-equilibrium dynamics near criticality by exploring the effect of randomized quantum resetting (QR) under a linear finite-time drive across, or very close to, an equilibrium quantum critical point. Using the transverse-field Ising chain as a minimal model an…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224312] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies universal out-of-equilibrium dynamics near a quantum critical point under randomized quantum resetting, revealing topological and nontopological defect formation.
motivation: Understanding defect formation during finite-time drives across quantum critical points is key to non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and quantum annealing.
method: The authors use the transverse-field Ising chain as a minimal model and analyze the effect of randomized quantum resetting on the Kibble-Zurek scaling of defect density.
result: Quantum resetting modifies the scaling laws, leading to both topological and nontopological defects with distinct signatures.
conclusion: Randomized resetting provides a new control knob for tailoring defect formation, with implications for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, using a statistical-gauge geometry to derive sum rules and Ward identities.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints like sum rules and Ward identities are hard to expose due to distributional currents and anomaly-like contact terms; a systematic geometric organization is needed.
method: The authors propose a statistical-gauge geometry that organizes the recently identified constraints, providing a simple geometric picture for deriving these identities.
result: The geometric framework yields a clear derivation of sum rules and Ward identities, clarifying the role of contact terms and anomalies.
conclusion: This geometric approach offers a powerful tool for analyzing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, with potential applications to quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production bounds.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a consistent thermodynamic description was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings, using path integrals and master equations to compute entropy production and work fluctuations.
result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and shows that nonreciprocity can reduce entropy production under certain conditions.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamically consistent way to model nonreciprocal systems, with implications for active matter and information processing.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret communication protocol using emergent paraparticles in topological phases, demonstrating robust information transmission without local traces.
motivation: To show a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication beyond conventional quantum information protocols.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchange statistics of emergent paraparticles in topological phases, designing a communication challenge that exploits their non-local properties.
result: Exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting such particles.
conclusion: Paraparticles offer a new resource for secret communication, with implications for quantum information and topological quantum computing.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum signatures of topological flow transitions in limit cycle phases of driven-dissipative systems, linking classical bifurcations to quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding how classical topological transitions in phase space manifest in quantum systems is crucial for characterizing non-equilibrium phases.
method: The authors analyze a driven-dissipative quantum oscillator model, computing quantum steady states and correlation functions to identify signatures of limit cycle transitions.
result: They find that topological flow transitions leave distinct imprints in quantum fluctuations, such as changes in squeezing and photon number correlations.
conclusion: Quantum dynamical signatures can serve as probes of classical bifurcations in open quantum systems, bridging classical nonlinear dynamics and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the relationship between gradient scalability and classical simulability in variational quantum algorithms, showing that cost functions with non-vanishing gradients can be approximated by classical surrogates.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, but recent conjectures suggest that avoiding them may lead to classical simulability. The authors aim to formalize this trade-off.
method: They prove that cost functions with polynomially vanishing gradients can be approximated by a polynomial number of terms in a Pauli basis, enabling classical surrogation via Taylor expansion.
result: The paper establishes a direct link between gradient scaling and classical approximability, demonstrating that non-barren landscapes are classically simulable to high precision.
conclusion: This work provides a rigorous foundation for the conjecture that avoiding barren plateaus implies classical simulability, highlighting fundamental limitations of VQAs.

title: Efficient And Simple Gibbs State Preparation Of The Two-dimensional Toric Code Via Duality To Classical Ising Chains
authors: Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, And Ángela Capel
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, and Ángela Capel

We introduce the notion of polynomial-depth duality transformations, which relates two sets of operator algebras through a conjugation by a poly-depth quantum circuit, and make use of this to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for a variety of interesting quantum Hamiltonians as they are poly-depth …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023277] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces polynomial-depth duality transformations to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for the 2D toric code, leveraging a duality to classical Ising chains.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states of quantum Hamiltonians is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics, but efficient methods are lacking for topologically ordered systems like the toric code.
method: The authors define polynomial-depth duality transformations that map the toric code Hamiltonian to a classical Ising chain via a shallow quantum circuit, enabling efficient Gibbs sampling using classical Monte Carlo methods.
result: They demonstrate that the Gibbs state of the 2D toric code can be prepared with polynomial resources, and the duality provides a rigorous bound on the mixing time of the quantum Gibbs sampler.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient approach to Gibbs state preparation for topologically ordered systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum simulation.

title: Harvesting Chemical Power From Cyclic Environments
authors: Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, And Christoph A. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, and Christoph A. Weber

Life relies on a sophisticated metabolic molecular machinery that turns over high-energy molecules to evolve complex macromolecules and assemblies. At the molecular origin of life, such machinery was absent, implying the need for simple yet robust physical mechanisms to harvest energy from the envir…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023289] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for harvesting chemical energy from cyclic environmental fluctuations using simple physical systems, relevant to the origins of life.
motivation: To understand how primitive molecular systems could harvest energy from cyclic environments without complex machinery, addressing the origin of life.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of a chemical system driven by periodic environmental changes, analyzing energy harvesting via stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They show that cyclic environments can enable net chemical work extraction, with efficiency depending on cycle parameters and system kinetics.
conclusion: Simple physical mechanisms can harvest chemical power from cyclic environments, providing a plausible pathway for prebiotic energy transduction.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states enable robust differential phase sensing with common-mode noise rejection.
motivation: Quantum sensors are limited by noise; differential phase sensing requires states that are insensitive to common-mode fluctuations.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with symmetry properties that cancel common-mode noise, and analyze their performance in a sensor network.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase estimation while being robust to common-mode noise.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile tool for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
