motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom infrastructure but suffers from low secret key rates and security proofs that are not composable. The authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: They combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization of the secret key rate.
result: The protocol achieves record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: This work brings CV-QKD closer to practical deployment by providing both high rates and rigorous security guarantees.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for quantum networking and computing.
conclusion: This technique advances the use of circular Rydberg atoms in hybrid quantum systems, enabling new quantum information protocols.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization by studying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, likely using experimental measurements and theoretical modeling.
result: They reveal the dynamics of transmon ionization, identifying key mechanisms that lead to qubit leakage.
conclusion: These insights can inform the design of more robust readout protocols and improve qubit fidelity.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in superconducting qubit platforms.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts induced by ionizing radiation in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, using state-of-the-art radiation protection.
result: They identify a new type of correlated error—phase error bursts—that persist even with advanced shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Correlated phase errors from ionizing radiation pose a significant challenge for scalable quantum computing, requiring novel mitigation strategies.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, especially for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze the shadowing time and thermalization time in many-body chaotic quantum circuits.
result: The shadowing time is found to be finite, and the Trotterization transition is shown to be a finite-size effect, not a true phase transition.
conclusion: The results clarify the nature of prethermalization and shadowing in quantum circuits, with implications for the validity of Trotterization in quantum simulations.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining that captures observable dynamics at the resolution of measurement channels.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are difficult to simulate due to many degrees of freedom; a reduced model that preserves relevant dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce a coarse-graining procedure that adapts to the time resolution of measurement channels, effectively discarding fast degrees of freedom that are not observed.
result: The method yields accurate reduced models for various open quantum systems, demonstrating significant computational savings while preserving key dynamical features.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems, bridging microscopic dynamics and observable phenomena.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform for generating and exploiting spin-dependent squeezed states.
method: The authors theoretically propose and experimentally realize a protocol using trapped ions to create spin-dependent squeezed states via spin-motion coupling, then apply them to displacement sensing.
result: They achieve near-Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for displacement measurements, outperforming standard quantum limit approaches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is crucial for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, performing spectroscopy and noise characterization to identify mechanisms causing spectral diffusion and linewidth broadening.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability, including charge noise and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can mitigate some decoherence effects.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon can achieve improved spectral stability, making them viable for quantum networking and computation applications.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model classes, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The method accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, outperforming standard approaches in efficiency and accuracy.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a practical tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay of long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel phases in driven-dissipative systems.
conclusion: The work establishes a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum many-body physics with cavity QED, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates, enabling the implementation of quantum error correction codes with improved performance.
conclusion: The optimized multiqubit gates bring neutral-atom platforms closer to practical quantum error correction, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum computing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and not scalable. An integrated photonic chip solution is needed for practical, production-scale quantum security.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated photon sources, detectors, and control electronics on a single chip.
result: The chip achieves real-time randomness generation with a certified min-entropy rate, demonstrating the first fully integrated self-testing QRNG on a photonic platform.
conclusion: This work paves the way for miniaturized, scalable quantum security devices that can be mass-produced, advancing practical quantum networks and cryptography.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high readout fidelity are characterized, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform with properties suitable for scalable quantum technologies, addressing the need for high-fidelity single-shot readout and long coherence times.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical spin selectivity.
result: A deep defect in ZnO exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance for spin qubits and quantum networking applications.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, achieving stronger antibunching and higher transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve blockade via collective effects in an ensemble, relaxing the requirement.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and single-photon sources.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving enables fast quantum state preparation but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from low fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to optimize the control fields, enhancing the approximation of the exact counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method achieves significantly higher fidelity for quantum control tasks compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods often scale poorly with system size or are not tailored to correlated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of sequences that cancel k-local noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and are device-tailored, offering efficient suppression of spatially correlated errors.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, providing a practical tool for improving coherence in multi-qubit systems.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and randomized Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation error bounds and phase estimation theory.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation, with rigorous error guarantees.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, bringing quantum chemistry simulations closer to feasibility.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics in confining systems.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in quantum systems is important for probing confinement and non-equilibrium dynamics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum simulation.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and experimental demonstrations with trapped ions to study string-breaking dynamics under adiabatic and diabatic conditions.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits complex quantum dynamics beyond simple breaking, including oscillatory and multi-particle effects.
conclusion: The work provides new probes of string breaking and demonstrates that confining strings can show rich quantum dynamics, relevant for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause backaction that destroys quantum information; a nondemolition readout is needed for high-fidelity quantum control and error correction.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize disturbance, using real-time feedback on a silicon spin qudit.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique for improving nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qudit platforms.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, likely using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical modeling.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: The proposed noise model significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations, enabling better prediction and optimization of transmon-based quantum computations.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and complexity in many-body systems, but existing probes often require full state tomography or are limited to specific settings.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the effect of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and then construct projected ensembles from these process tensors to extract signatures of chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensemble of process tensors can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics, and that its properties relate to out-of-time-order correlators and operator spreading.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and unified framework for diagnosing chaos in many-body quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and practical implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer conceptual and practical advantages over discrete-variable methods for quantum communication, including compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.
method: The paper surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, reconciliation) and experimental progress in CV-QKD, CV quantum networks, and related protocols.
result: CV quantum communication is now as mature as discrete-variable approaches, with high-rate QKD demonstrations and emerging network architectures.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising path for scalable quantum networks, with ongoing challenges in long-distance transmission and security proofs.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universality classes based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies distinct types of universal behavior in driven open matter, linking to known equilibrium and nonequilibrium critical phenomena.
conclusion: Provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory in driven quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting coherence times is crucial for developing solid-state spin qubits for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming reliable, aiding the design of long-coherence spin qubits.

title: Quantum State Preparation Without Coherent Arithmetic
authors: Sam Mcardle, András Gilyén, And Mario Berta
abstract:
Author(s): Sam McArdle, András Gilyén, and Mario Berta

We introduce a versatile method for preparing a quantum state whose amplitudes are given by some known function. Unlike existing approaches, our method does not require handcrafted reversible arithmetic circuits, or quantum table reads, to encode the function values. Instead, we use a template quant…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240603] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing quantum states with amplitudes given by a known function without coherent arithmetic, using a template quantum circuit and classical optimization.
motivation: Existing state preparation methods require handcrafted reversible arithmetic circuits or quantum table lookups, which are resource-intensive. This work aims to simplify state preparation by avoiding coherent arithmetic.
method: The authors propose a template quantum circuit with adjustable parameters, and use classical optimization to minimize the distance between the prepared state and the target state, leveraging the ability to compute function values classically.
result: The method achieves high-fidelity state preparation for various functions (e.g., polynomial, trigonometric) with significantly fewer quantum resources than previous approaches, as demonstrated numerically.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical and resource-efficient alternative for quantum state preparation, particularly useful for quantum algorithms that require loading classical data into quantum states.

title: Universal Two-Excitation Scattering In Two-Dimensional Subwavelength Atomic Arrays
authors: Yidan Wang (王艺丹), Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, Valentin Walther, And Susanne F. Yelin
abstract:
Author(s): Yidan Wang (王艺丹), Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, Valentin Walther, and Susanne F. Yelin

Subwavelength atomic arrays are a leading platform for engineering strong light-matter interactions, presenting exciting opportunities for quantum science. However, a full understanding of their multiexcitation dynamics remains a significant challenge. In this Letter, we uncover a remarkable univers…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243603] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals universal behavior in two-excitation scattering from subwavelength atomic arrays, showing that the scattering matrix depends only on the number of atoms and the array's lattice constant.
motivation: Understanding multiexcitation dynamics in subwavelength atomic arrays is crucial for quantum science applications, but a full theoretical description has been lacking.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the coupled-dipole model and analyze two-excitation scattering processes, deriving universal properties of the scattering matrix.
result: They find that the two-excitation scattering matrix is universal, depending only on the number of atoms and lattice constant, independent of other microscopic details.
conclusion: This universality simplifies the description of nonlinear light-matter interactions in atomic arrays and may enable robust quantum nonlinear optical devices.

title: Microwave-enabled Continuous-variable Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution In Free Space
authors: Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, And Ying Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, and Ying Guo

Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) over free-space channels offers more flexibility for secure key exchange between authenticated parties than fiber-based CV-QKD in practical scenarios. However, traditional CV-QKD systems use 1550-nm optical signals as the quantum source, which ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062450] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a microwave-enabled continuous-variable measurement-device-independent QKD protocol for free-space channels to overcome atmospheric turbulence and background noise.
motivation: Free-space CV-QKD is flexible but suffers from atmospheric turbulence and background noise; using microwave signals instead of optical can mitigate these issues.
method: The protocol uses microwave signals as the quantum source, employs continuous-variable encoding, and implements measurement-device-independent detection to eliminate detector side-channel attacks.
result: Simulations show that the microwave-based protocol achieves higher secret key rates over longer distances compared to optical CV-QKD under realistic atmospheric conditions.
conclusion: Microwave-enabled CV-MDI-QKD is a viable approach for secure free-space quantum communication, especially in adverse weather or high-noise environments.

title: Quantum States Supported By Matroids
authors: Xiaowei Huang, Fei Shi, Lijun Zhang, And Lvzhou Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaowei Huang, Fei Shi, Lijun Zhang, and Lvzhou Li

In this work, we establish a structural correspondence between quantum states and matroid theory. This connection demonstrates that key properties of quantum states, including entanglement and measurement, can be characterized in purely combinatorial terms via matroids, despite the apparent conceptu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062452] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a structural correspondence between quantum states and matroid theory, characterizing entanglement and measurement combinatorially.
motivation: To provide a combinatorial framework for understanding quantum state properties, potentially simplifying analysis of entanglement and measurement.
method: Develops a mapping from quantum states to matroids and proves that key properties like entanglement and measurement outcomes correspond to matroid invariants.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement and measurement can be characterized purely in terms of matroid theory, offering new combinatorial tools.
conclusion: Matroid theory provides a novel perspective on quantum states, with potential applications in quantum information theory.

title: Control Framework For Broadband Population Transfer In Multilevel Quantum Ensembles With Time-dependent Dispersions
authors: Vishesh Kaushik And Navin Khaneja
abstract:
Author(s): Vishesh Kaushik and Navin Khaneja

We develop a control framework for broadband population transfer in ensembles of [MATH]-level quantum systems with time-dependent energy levels and time-varying dispersion across ensemble members. Ensemble inhomogeneity is modeled through time-varying dispersion functions that capture Hamiltonian varia…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062620] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops a control framework for broadband population transfer in multilevel quantum ensembles with time-dependent dispersions.
motivation: Ensemble inhomogeneities, such as time-dependent energy level dispersions, hinder precise quantum control; a robust framework is needed to achieve high-fidelity population transfer across all ensemble members.
method: The authors model ensemble inhomogeneity via time-varying dispersion functions and design control pulses using optimal control theory to achieve broadband population transfer.
result: The framework enables efficient population transfer in multilevel systems despite time-dependent dispersions, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This control approach is promising for quantum information processing with inhomogeneous ensembles, such as those used in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Intercavity Phonons And Dynamics In Coupled Polariton Cavities
authors: Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, And Arturo Camacho-Guardian
abstract:
Author(s): Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, and Arturo Camacho-Guardian

Intercavity polaritons, hybrid quasiparticles with spatially separated photonic and excitonic components, provide a platform to engineer structured light-matter states. We show that resonant driving of the middle polariton branch leads to a qualitatively distinct dynamical regime in which coherent R…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062814] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies intercavity phonons and dynamics in coupled polariton cavities, revealing a regime of coherent Rabi-like oscillations between spatially separated photonic and excitonic components.
motivation: To understand and control the dynamics of intercavity polaritons, which are hybrid quasiparticles with spatially separated photonic and excitonic components, for engineering structured light-matter states.
method: The authors use resonant driving of the middle polariton branch in a coupled cavity system and analyze the resulting dynamics theoretically, likely using a master equation or Hamiltonian approach.
result: They find a qualitatively distinct dynamical regime with coherent Rabi-like oscillations between the photonic and excitonic parts, mediated by intercavity phonons.
conclusion: Intercavity phonons play a key role in the dynamics, offering a new way to control polariton states in coupled cavities.

title: Phonon Scattering From Spatial Relaxation Of One-dimensional Bose Gases
authors: Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, And Nicolas Cherroret
abstract:
Author(s): Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, and Nicolas Cherroret

We theoretically investigate the nonequilibrium relaxation of a spatial density modulation in a one-dimensional nonintegrable Bose gas and its connection to the equilibrium scattering rate [MATH] of the system's phononic excitations. We show that the density relaxation is generically go…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies nonequilibrium relaxation of density modulations in 1D Bose gases and connects it to phonon scattering rates.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in low-dimensional quantum systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the relaxation of a spatial density modulation in a nonintegrable 1D Bose gas using a hydrodynamic approach and relate it to the equilibrium phonon scattering rate.
result: They find that density relaxation is generically governed by the phonon scattering rate, providing a direct link between non-equilibrium dynamics and equilibrium properties.
conclusion: The work establishes a connection between spatial relaxation and phonon scattering, offering insights into thermalization and transport in one-dimensional quantum gases.

title: Non-Hermitian Cavity Magnomechanics With $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry-related Asymmetric Transparency
authors: Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, And Kashif Ammar Yasir
abstract:
Author(s): Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, and Kashif Ammar Yasir

We investigate magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling. The setup consists of a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere, where the magnon mode is further hybridized w…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063522] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with non-Hermitian coupling and PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian physics and PT-symmetry in hybrid magnomechanical systems, which could lead to novel control of light-matter interactions.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling, using input-output formalism and solving for transmission spectra.
result: Demonstrates asymmetric transparency windows and PT-symmetry-related effects in the magnomechanically induced transparency spectrum.
conclusion: The work reveals new phenomena in non-Hermitian hybrid systems, relevant for quantum information processing and sensing.

title: Nonreciprocal Universal Photon Blockade In An Asymmetrical Cavity
authors: Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, And Yaping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, and Yaping Yang

Inspired by the distinctive properties of universal photon blockade (UPB), we propose a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve quantum nonreciprocity. Through theoretical analysis, we establish direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect UPB in weak-driving limita…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063729] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve nonreciprocal universal photon blockade.
motivation: To realize quantum nonreciprocity using photon blockade effects, which are important for quantum information processing and networking.
method: Theoretical analysis of a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity, deriving direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect universal photon blockade in the weak-driving limit.
result: Establishes conditions for nonreciprocal photon blockade, enabling direction-dependent control of photon transmission.
conclusion: The asymmetric cavity design provides a platform for quantum nonreciprocal devices, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Effects Of Static Dc Electric-field Orientation On Two-photon Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas Destefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, And Irina Novikova
abstract:
Author(s): Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas DeStefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, and Irina Novikova

We examine the influence of a static dc electric field on electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances that involve highly excited Rydberg states. Our focus is on how these resonances are altered when the relative orientation between the laser polarization and the external electric-fiel…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062619] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the orientation of a static DC electric field relative to laser polarization affects two-photon Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances.
motivation: Understanding the influence of electric fields on Rydberg EIT is important for applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems where Rydberg atoms are coupled to other platforms.
method: The authors experimentally measure EIT spectra in a rubidium vapor cell with Rydberg states, varying the angle between the DC field and laser polarization, and compare with theoretical models.
result: They find that the EIT resonance amplitude and linewidth depend strongly on the field orientation, consistent with Stark shifts and mixing of Rydberg states.
conclusion: Controlling the DC field orientation is crucial for optimizing Rydberg EIT-based devices, and the results provide guidelines for designing hybrid quantum systems involving Rydberg atoms.

title: Application And Quantum Properties Of Superpositions Of Oppositely Squeezed States
authors: Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, And Kae Nemoto
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, and Kae Nemoto

We show that superpositions of oppositely squeezed states—non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states—exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime. These states possess photon-number structures distinct from conventional coherent-state cat s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063728] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are shown to exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime.
motivation: To explore non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states that may offer advantages for quantum information processing, particularly in continuous-variable systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the photon-number statistics, Wigner functions, and entanglement properties of superpositions of oppositely squeezed states, comparing them to conventional coherent-state cat states.
result: These states display distinct nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime, with potential applications in quantum communication and computation.
conclusion: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are promising non-Gaussian resources for continuous-variable quantum information tasks.

title: Giant Bubbles Of Fisher Zeros In The Quantum Xy Chain
authors: Songtai Lv, Yang Liu, Erhai Zhao, Haiyuan Zou, And Tao Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Songtai Lv, Yang Liu, Erhai Zhao, Haiyuan Zou, and Tao Xiang

We demonstrate an alternative approach based on a complex-valued inverse temperature and partition function to probe quantum phases of matter with nontrivial spectra and dynamics. It leverages thermofield dynamics (TFD) to quantitatively characterize quantum and thermal fluctuations, and exploit the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241117] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses complex-valued inverse temperature and thermofield dynamics to study Fisher zeros in the quantum XY chain, revealing giant bubble structures that characterize quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To develop a new approach for probing quantum phases of matter by analyzing the partition function zeros in the complex temperature plane, which can capture nontrivial spectra and dynamics.
method: The authors employ thermofield dynamics (TFD) to map the quantum XY chain to a classical system with complex temperature, then compute the Fisher zeros (partition function zeros) to identify phase boundaries and critical behavior.
result: They discover giant bubble-like structures of Fisher zeros that encode information about quantum and thermal fluctuations, providing a quantitative characterization of the phase diagram.
conclusion: The complex-temperature approach offers a powerful tool for studying quantum phase transitions and may be extended to other many-body systems.

title: Emergence Of Prethermal Time-quasicrystalline Order In A Quasiperiodically Driven Noninteracting Spin Chain
authors: Davood Marripour And Jahanfar Abouie
abstract:
Author(s): Davood Marripour and Jahanfar Abouie

We study prethermal time quasicrystalline (TQC) order in a quasiperiodically driven chain of noninteracting spin-1/2 particles. The drive consists of two parts, switched on and off periodically with frequency [MATH]: (i) disordered Ising interactions, with exchange couplings chosen from a symmetr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214318] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies prethermal time-quasicrystalline order in a quasiperiodically driven noninteracting spin chain, focusing on the interplay between driving and disorder.
motivation: Understanding prethermalization and time-crystalline order in driven systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors consider a quasiperiodically driven chain of noninteracting spin-1/2 particles with disordered Ising interactions and analyze the emergence of prethermal time-quasicrystalline order.
result: They find that prethermal TQC order can persist for long times even in noninteracting systems, protected by the quasiperiodic drive and disorder.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that prethermal time-quasicrystalline order is not exclusive to interacting systems, expanding the scope of such phenomena.

title: Open-system Dynamics In Local Lindbladians With Chaotic Spectra
authors: Sanket Chirame And Fiona J. Burnell
abstract:
Author(s): Sanket Chirame and Fiona J. Burnell

We investigate the physical consequences of having a spectrum that satisfies random matrix theory (RMT) for generic Lindbladians, and compare its implications for spatially local and completely random Lindblad dynamics in one spatial dimension. We find that Lindbladians whose spectrum is described b…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224314] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies open quantum systems with Lindbladians whose spectra follow random matrix theory, comparing spatially local and completely random dynamics in 1D.
motivation: Understanding the physical consequences of chaotic spectra in Lindbladians is important for characterizing thermalization and dynamics in open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze spectral properties of local and random Lindbladians using random matrix theory and compare their implications for dynamics in one spatial dimension.
result: They find that Lindbladians with RMT spectra exhibit distinct dynamical features depending on spatial locality, with implications for thermalization and chaos.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of chaos in open quantum systems, connecting spectral statistics to physical dynamics.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Optimal navigation strategy for a small swimmer in a flow trades off accuracy and cost, revealing thermodynamic constraints on information processing.
motivation: To understand how a microscopic swimmer can localize near a target despite environmental noise and flow, and to quantify the fundamental trade-off between accuracy and energetic cost.
method: The authors model a swimmer with active control in a stochastic environment with drift, and derive optimal strategies using stochastic control theory and thermodynamic cost functions.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a clear trade-off: higher accuracy requires more work, and the minimal cost scales with the desired precision.
conclusion: The work establishes a thermodynamic bound on localization accuracy, linking information-theoretic limits to physical energy dissipation, relevant for active matter and biological navigation.

title: Minimal-dissipation Learning For Energy-based Models
authors: Jeff Hnybida And Simon Verret
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Hnybida and Simon Verret

We show that the bias of the approximate maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) objective of a persistent chain energy-based model (EBM) is precisely equal to the thermodynamic excess work of an overdamped Langevin dynamical system. We then answer the question of whether such a model can be trained wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065306] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the bias in maximum-likelihood estimation for energy-based models equals thermodynamic excess work, and explores minimal-dissipation training.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of training energy-based models and to find training protocols that minimize dissipation.
method: The authors map the persistent chain EBM training to an overdamped Langevin dynamics and derive the bias as excess work, then propose a minimal-dissipation learning approach.
result: The bias of approximate MLE is exactly the thermodynamic excess work, and minimal-dissipation learning can reduce this dissipation.
conclusion: Energy-based model training can be understood and optimized using thermodynamic principles, linking machine learning to information thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves dynamical typicality for classical lattice systems, showing that macroscopic observables evolve typically under independent initial conditions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of thermodynamic behavior from microscopic dynamics is a fundamental question in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors consider deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous variables and sample initial conditions from a product distribution, then analyze the temporal evolution of macroscopic observables.
result: They show that for any macroscopic observable, its time evolution is typical (i.e., close to the ensemble average) for most initial conditions, with rigorous bounds on fluctuations.
conclusion: Dynamical typicality holds in classical lattice systems, providing a foundation for the emergence of irreversible thermodynamic behavior from reversible dynamics.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory to characterize non-Markovian dynamics in a collision model, demonstrating parameter estimation and detection of memory effects.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important in open quantum systems but challenging to characterize; machine learning offers a data-driven approach to extract parameters and detect memory effects.
method: The authors implement a QELM where the reservoir is a quantum system with memory, processing sequential quantum states from a collision model to learn and estimate parameters of the non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The QELM successfully estimates system-environment coupling strengths and detects non-Markovianity, outperforming standard QELMs without memory.
conclusion: Memory-enhanced QELMs provide an effective tool for characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum thermometry and sensing.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system, showing that ICO can be realized in this platform and may serve as a resource for quantum information processing.
motivation: ICO is a potential resource for quantum information tasks, but most experiments have been photonic; exploring ICO in cavity QED could enable new applications and more robust implementations.
method: The authors propose a cavity QED setup with two cavities and analyze the conditions for achieving ICO using the quantum switch formalism, modeling the interaction with atoms and cavities.
result: They demonstrate that ICO can be realized in cavity QED, with the ability to control the causal order via atomic states and cavity parameters.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO, potentially enabling new quantum information protocols that leverage indefinite causal order.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A review of the process tensor framework for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics using tensor networks.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging.
method: The paper reviews the process tensor formalism and demonstrates how tensor-network representations (e.g., MPS, MPO) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is applied to several examples, showing that tensor-network methods can capture memory effects and non-Markovianity in diverse physical systems.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor networks, provides a practical and scalable tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing connections to diffusion processes via continuum limits.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables across jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework enhances the theoretical toolkit for studying stochastic thermodynamics and may facilitate new results in fluctuation theorems and work relations.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular circuits may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework drawing on phase separation, multi-component condensates, and non-equilibrium thermodynamics to model information processing.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable cells to classify signals, perform logical operations, and adapt to noise, with potential for energy-efficient computation.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a novel paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for synthetic biology and understanding biological computation.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry reveals a two-step thermalization process in mesoscopic metallic islands at high magnetic field, involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the electron temperature in mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse, analyzing the relaxation dynamics.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: a fast electronic relaxation followed by a slower process involving nuclear spins, indicating a coupling between electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins governs the heating dynamics, which has implications for thermal management in quantum devices and understanding non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for assessing the computational power of near-term quantum devices and for benchmarking random circuit sampling experiments.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods to analyze the anticoncentration properties of random circuits under various noise models and circuit architectures.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth-dependent noise threshold, with a universal scaling that is independent of the specific circuit architecture, and identify distinct regimes based on depth and noise strength.
conclusion: The results provide a unified understanding of anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, which has implications for quantum supremacy experiments and the design of fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function negativity. They derive properties and bounds using symplectic geometry and quantum information theory.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a valid resource monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and the compression cost of non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a unified framework for quantifying non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theories and practical tasks in continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging with high fidelity and low atom loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to perform nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to image atoms with minimal scattering, and use a continuously operated loading scheme to maintain high array occupancy. The experiment is performed in a finite magnetic field to enable EIT.
result: They achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and demonstrate continuous loading of atom arrays, significantly improving array preparation and readout.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading is a powerful technique for neutral-atom quantum computing platforms, enabling higher performance and scalability.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation approach that uses a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice to represent ancillary degrees of freedom, combined with moment-matching techniques to approximate the target nonunitary evolution.
