result: The framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, overcoming traditional connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise correlations in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle at intermediate frequencies.
method: The authors develop a technique that leverages single-shot readout data to compute noise cross-correlations, enabling spectroscopy in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method on a semiconductor spin qubit platform, extracting noise cross-correlation spectra and revealing correlated noise sources.
conclusion: This approach provides a powerful tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, aiding in the development of more coherent quantum processors.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to overcome hardware noise, but existing architectures incur high space and time overhead.
method: The authors design a transversal logical gate set tailored to neutral-atom hardware, combining small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: The proposed architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit count, and runtime compared to conventional approaches.
conclusion: Neutral-atom platforms, combined with transversal error correction, offer a promising path toward practical large-scale quantum simulation.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function under noise, relating it to the expressivity of the circuit measured by the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra.
result: They show that noise can actually help by reducing the effective expressivity, leading to a concentration of the loss function that is less severe than in the noiseless case, and provide explicit estimates for various noise models.
conclusion: Noise, typically detrimental, can be beneficial for trainability by suppressing barren plateaus, offering a principled way to design noise-resilient variational algorithms.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally observe suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method for leakage protection in exchange-only spin qubits, enhancing their viability for quantum computing.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for choosing appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between different non-Markovian simulation methods, aiding researchers in selecting and developing tools for open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in circuit depth and resource efficiency.
motivation: Qudits offer potential advantages over qubits in reducing gate complexity and resource requirements for quantum algorithms, but their role in quantum computing is not yet fully explored.
method: The paper surveys qudit-based decompositions of standard multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate) and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Using a single qutrit can drastically simplify the Toffoli gate; qudit embeddings can reduce circuit depth and qubit count for certain algorithms.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, especially for near-term devices, but further development in qudit control and error correction is needed.

title: Dissipation Due To Bulk Localized Low-Energy Modes In Strongly Disordered Superconductors
authors: Anton V. Khvalyuk And Mikhail V. Feigel’man
abstract:
Author(s): Anton V. Khvalyuk and Mikhail V. Feigel’man

Microwave dissipation in strongly disordered superconductors is driven by localized collective modes within rare weak spots, a theoretical insight which provides a fresh strategy to enhance coherence times in quantum devices.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256001] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies localized collective modes in weak spots of disordered superconductors as a source of microwave dissipation, offering a strategy to improve coherence times in quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating microwave dissipation in superconducting qubits is crucial for improving coherence times, which are limited by material defects and disorder.
method: The authors theoretically analyze strongly disordered superconductors, focusing on rare weak spots that host localized low-energy collective modes, and compute their contribution to microwave dissipation.
result: They find that these localized modes cause significant dissipation, and propose that engineering the disorder landscape can reduce this loss.
conclusion: The work provides a fresh theoretical insight into dissipation mechanisms in disordered superconductors, with potential implications for enhancing qubit coherence in quantum devices.

title: Tripartite Kerr Soliton Ising Machine For Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Nitesh Chauhan, Yan Jin, Jizhao Zang, And Scott B. Papp
abstract:
Author(s): Nitesh Chauhan, Yan Jin, Jizhao Zang, and Scott B. Papp

We introduce and explore a Kerr soliton Ising machine with all-to-all connectivity and up to tripartite (cubic) interactions, unlocking efficient approaches for combinatorial optimization. The machine is an ensemble of solitons in a Kerr resonator, where a programmable optoelectronic feedback circui…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257301] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr soliton Ising machine with tripartite interactions is proposed for combinatorial optimization.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization problems are hard; Ising machines offer a physical approach but typically only support pairwise interactions, limiting their expressiveness.
method: The machine uses an ensemble of Kerr solitons in a resonator with programmable optoelectronic feedback to implement all-to-all couplings and tripartite (cubic) interactions.
result: The tripartite interactions enable solving problems with higher-order constraints, potentially improving performance on certain optimization tasks.
conclusion: This work extends Ising machines to higher-order interactions, but its primary application is optimization rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Mechanics Based On Real Numbers: A Consistent Description
authors: Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, And Dagmar Bruß
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, and Dagmar Bruß

By exploiting a physically motivated principle, rather than a mathematical postulate, researchers offer a new perspective on how a real-valued quantum theory can be constructed.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240202] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs a consistent real-valued quantum theory based on a physically motivated principle rather than a mathematical postulate.
motivation: Standard quantum mechanics uses complex numbers, but real-valued formulations have been proposed; the authors aim to provide a physically consistent real-valued theory.
method: They derive a real-valued quantum theory by imposing a physically motivated principle (e.g., no-signaling or causality) instead of assuming complex numbers a priori.
result: They show that a consistent real-valued quantum theory can be constructed, which reproduces many features of standard quantum mechanics.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on the foundations of quantum mechanics, suggesting that complex numbers may not be essential for a consistent theory.

title: Quantum Semiconductor Heterostructures For meV Axion Dark Matter Detection
authors: Jaanita Mehrani, Tao Xu, Andrey Baydin, Michael J. Manfra, Henry O. Everitt, Andrew J. Long, Kuver Sinha, Junichiro Kono, And Shengxi Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Jaanita Mehrani, Tao Xu, Andrey Baydin, Michael J. Manfra, Henry O. Everitt, Andrew J. Long, Kuver Sinha, Junichiro Kono, and Shengxi Huang

We propose a novel strategy and a new class of detectors for the direct detection of axion dark matter in the meV mass range, based on resonantly enhanced axion-photon conversion through the inverse Primakoff effect in engineered radiometers composed of quantum semiconductor heterostructures. Semico…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241001] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes quantum semiconductor heterostructures as detectors for meV axion dark matter via resonantly enhanced axion-photon conversion.
motivation: Axion dark matter in the meV mass range is a compelling candidate, but direct detection requires sensitive detectors operating at low energies.
method: Engineered radiometers using quantum semiconductor heterostructures exploit the inverse Primakoff effect for resonantly enhanced axion-photon conversion.
result: The proposed detector design achieves sensitivity to meV axions through material and structural engineering.
conclusion: Quantum semiconductor heterostructures offer a new platform for axion dark matter detection, bridging quantum materials and particle physics.

title: Identifying The Three-qubit $w$ State With The Quantum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, And Jing-Ling Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, and Jing-Ling Chen

The [MATH] state, a canonical representative of multipartite quantum entanglement, plays a crucial role in quantum information science due to its robust entanglement properties. Quantum uncertainty relations, on the other hand, form a fundamental cornerstone of quantum mechanics. This work introduces a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062451] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum uncertainty relations to identify the three-qubit W state, a canonical entangled state.
motivation: The W state is important for quantum information tasks, and uncertainty relations provide a way to characterize entanglement.
method: The authors derive an uncertainty relation based on local observables and show that the W state saturates it uniquely.
result: They obtain a criterion that distinguishes the W state from other three-qubit states using the uncertainty relation.
conclusion: The work offers a new method to identify the W state, but the contribution is incremental and not directly aligned with core interests.

title: Incoherent Repumping Scheme In The $^{88}\mathrm{Sr}^{+}$ Five-level Manifold
authors: Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, And Jean-Pierre Likforman
abstract:
Author(s): Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, and Jean-Pierre Likforman

Laser-cooled trapped ions are at the heart of modern quantum technologies and their cooling dynamics often deviate from the simplified two-level atom model. Doppler cooling of the [MATH] ion involves several electronic levels and repumping channels that strongly influence fluorescenc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063109] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an incoherent repumping scheme for Doppler cooling of Sr+ ions, analyzing its effect on fluorescence and cooling dynamics.
motivation: Doppler cooling of trapped ions involves multiple electronic levels and repumping channels, and simplified two-level models are insufficient for accurate description.
method: The authors model the five-level manifold of Sr+ and propose an incoherent repumping scheme, studying its impact on fluorescence and cooling via rate equations or master equation simulations.
result: The incoherent repumping scheme modifies the fluorescence spectrum and cooling efficiency compared to coherent repumping.
conclusion: The scheme provides a practical approach for optimizing laser cooling of Sr+ ions, relevant for quantum information platforms.

title: Microwave-free Vector Magnetic-field Measurement Using A Single Nitrogen-vacancy-center Spin In Diamond
authors: Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, And Lumin Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, and Lumin Ji

Magnetic field sensors based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers have attracted considerable attention due to their high sensitivity and spatial resolution. However, conventional vector magnetometry typically relies on either the four axes of ensemble NV centers or three orthogonal reference magnetic f…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062618] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A microwave-free vector magnetometry method using a single NV center in diamond is demonstrated.
motivation: Conventional NV-based vector magnetometry requires microwave fields or multiple NV axes, which can be limiting; a simpler, microwave-free approach using a single NV center is desired.
method: The authors use a single NV center and measure the Zeeman shifts of the spin sublevels via optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) without microwaves, employing a bias magnetic field and analyzing the fluorescence intensity as a function of field direction.
result: They achieve vector magnetic field measurement with high sensitivity and spatial resolution using only a single NV center, eliminating the need for microwave fields or multiple sensors.
conclusion: This work provides a simplified method for vector magnetometry that could be useful for applications where microwave fields are undesirable.

title: Optimal Control Of Open-quantum-system Dynamics Predicted By Long Short-term Memory
authors: Jun-Dong Zhong And Zhao-Ming Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Dong Zhong and Zhao-Ming Wang

The realization of high-fidelity quantum control is crucial for quantum information processing, particularly in noisy environments where control strategies must simultaneously achieve precise manipulation and effective noise suppression. Conventional optimal control designs typically require numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062442] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Uses LSTM neural networks to predict optimal control pulses for open quantum systems, achieving high-fidelity state preparation under noise.
motivation: Conventional optimal control for open quantum systems is computationally expensive; machine learning offers a faster alternative.
method: Trains a long short-term memory (LSTM) network on optimal control solutions from GRAPE to predict control pulses for Lindblad dynamics.
result: The LSTM predicts control pulses with fidelities above 0.99 for various target states and noise parameters, with orders of magnitude speedup.
conclusion: Machine learning can efficiently generate high-fidelity quantum control for open systems, aiding practical quantum information processing.

title: Three-qubit-state Preparation: Classification And Explicit Circuits
authors: Yonghae Lee And Taewan Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Yonghae Lee and Taewan Kim

We develop a deterministic and fully explicit framework for preparing an arbitrary three-qubit pure state from its computational-basis amplitudes. Our approach exploits bipartite Schmidt structure: we classify three-qubit states into five types with respect to a [MATH] bipartition and provide concret…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062444] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A deterministic framework for preparing arbitrary three-qubit pure states using bipartite Schmidt decomposition and explicit quantum circuits.
motivation: Efficient state preparation is crucial for quantum information processing, but explicit circuits for arbitrary three-qubit states are lacking.
method: Classifies three-qubit states into five types based on Schmidt rank across bipartitions and provides explicit circuit constructions for each type.
result: Complete classification and explicit circuits for preparing any three-qubit pure state from computational basis amplitudes.
conclusion: The framework offers a systematic and resource-efficient approach to three-qubit state preparation, useful for quantum computing experiments.

title: Giant Magnetoelasticity In FeRh Thin Films Evidenced Via Strong Phonon-magnon Coupling
authors: D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, And L. Thevenard
abstract:
Author(s): D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard

FeRh is best known for its metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction. Here, the authors reveal remarkably strong phonon–magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh. Combining Brillouin light scattering experiments with magnetoacoustic modeling, they demonstrate giant magnetoelasticity and show that Love surface acoustic waves provide an efficient mechanism for coherent magnon-polaron formation in magnetic thin films, highlighting FeRh as a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214450] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates strong phonon-magnon coupling in FeRh thin films, revealing giant magnetoelasticity and potential for spin-acoustic information processing.
motivation: FeRh exhibits a metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction, but its phonon-magnon coupling was unexplored; understanding this coupling could enable new hybrid quantum systems for information processing.
method: Brillouin light scattering experiments combined with magnetoacoustic modeling were used to study phonon-magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh thin films.
result: The authors observed remarkably strong phonon-magnon coupling and giant magnetoelasticity, with Love surface acoustic waves enabling coherent magnon-polaron formation.
conclusion: FeRh is a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing, relevant to hybrid quantum systems that couple spin and mechanical degrees of freedom.

title: Optimal Parametric Control Of Transport Across A Josephson Junction
authors: Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, and Ludwig Mathey

We present optimal control strategies for the dc transport across a Josephson junction. Specifically, we consider a junction in which the Josephson coupling is driven parametrically, with either a bichromatic or a trichromatic driving protocol, and optimize the prefactor of the [MATH] divergence of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023313] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Optimal parametric control of dc transport across a Josephson junction using bichromatic and trichromatic driving to enhance the supercurrent divergence.
motivation: To achieve high dc currents in Josephson junctions by optimizing parametric driving protocols, which is relevant for quantum device performance.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to bichromatic and trichromatic driving of the Josephson coupling, optimizing the prefactor of the current divergence.
result: They find that optimized driving protocols can significantly enhance the supercurrent, with trichromatic driving outperforming bichromatic.
conclusion: Parametric control offers a viable route to boost transport in Josephson junctions, with potential applications in quantum circuits.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity
authors: Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, And Georgia T. Papadakis
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, and Georgia T. Papadakis

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023293] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies far-field heat transfer and monochromatic thermal currents in cylindrical nonreciprocal cavities, focusing on breaking Kirchhoff's law.
motivation: To explore consequences of nonreciprocal thermal radiation for one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry.
method: Uses a specular ray-tracing algorithm to compute heat transfer in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Demonstrates violation of Kirchhoff's law and generation of monochromatic thermal currents in the far-field regime.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal cavities enable directional thermal transport, which may have applications in thermal management and energy conversion.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to optimize generation of non-Gaussian quantum states of light, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to provide systematic optimization.
method: The authors propose new control parameters beyond the stellar rank and develop a theoretical framework for optimizing optical state generation.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for scalable generation of non-Gaussian optical states, advancing quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for characterizing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a two-dimensional electron gas in a high-quality GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure, varying temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the extraction of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a thermodynamic probe of topological order, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high encoding rate and constant-depth encoding circuits for magic state distillation.
result: Demonstrates that tricycle codes enable magic state generation with lower overhead and higher noise thresholds compared to existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward efficient magic state generation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces twisted color circuits for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, enabling universal quantum computing with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates is essential for universal quantum computing, but existing schemes often require non-planar layouts or high overhead.
method: The authors design planar circuits using the 2D color code and a twisted lattice geometry, combined with a just-in-time decoder to handle errors during gate execution.
result: The proposed circuits achieve fault tolerance with reduced overhead compared to previous methods, and are compatible with nearest-neighbor couplings on a planar chip.
conclusion: Twisted color circuits provide a scalable and practical approach to universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical simulation method for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, leveraging initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum expectation landscapes is generally hard, but for small subregions it may be tractable, enabling hybrid quantum-classical algorithms.
method: The authors develop a classical surrogate model that uses a limited number of quantum measurements to predict expectation values in a local patch of the landscape.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately approximate the landscape with significantly fewer quantum resources than full simulation.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to reduce quantum resource requirements in variational quantum algorithms and other quantum-classical workflows.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing methods are limited by circuit size and structure.
method: The authors use strong and weak symmetry reductions to optimize stabilizer decompositions, enabling efficient simulation of multiqubit unitaries with dominant Clifford components.
result: The proposed techniques render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for circuits beyond previous limits, significantly extending the reach of classical simulation.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated methods provide a practical tool for simulating Clifford-dominated circuits, with potential applications in quantum circuit verification and quantum advantage studies.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in sensing.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling of quantum Fisher information near critical points.
result: Shows how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for high-precision metrology, but practical challenges remain.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T-gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T-gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant T-count reduction compared to standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-gate optimization, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to learn and extrapolate dynamics.
method: Applies Fourier neural operators to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables in frequency space, capturing temporal correlations.
result: The method accurately predicts Floquet Hamiltonians, observable dynamics, and operator growth beyond training data.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the end, allowing the simulation to be performed with reduced overhead. This likely involves tracking Pauli errors and using stabilizer formalism.
result: The method achieves efficient classical simulation for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, enabling analysis of larger systems than previously possible.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for evaluating magic state preparation protocols, which is important for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but the contribution is more computational than information-theoretic.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Abelian multi-cycle codes, a family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot error correction with improved pseudothreshold and shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires multiple rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead, but existing codes have large block lengths or low thresholds.
method: Constructs codes that are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, leveraging abelian groups and multi-cycle structure to enable single-shot correction.
result: Achieves a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous single-shot codes.
conclusion: Abelian multi-cycle codes offer a practical path toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computing with single-shot error correction.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code parameters.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes by carefully designing measurement sequences and exploiting code structure.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements while maintaining the code's distance and rate, and is compatible with common LDPC code families.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel operations on low-overhead quantum codes.

title: Temporal Signature Of Bosonic Stimulation Induced By Dark Exciton In A Two-Photon-Pumped Polariton Condensate
authors: Nadav Landau, Dmitry Panna, Sarit Feldman, Sebastian Brodbeck, Christian Schneider, Sven Höfling, And Alex Hayat
abstract:
Author(s): Nadav Landau, Dmitry Panna, Sarit Feldman, Sebastian Brodbeck, Christian Schneider, Sven Höfling, and Alex Hayat

Strongly coupled light-matter exciton-polaritons constitute an on-chip solid-state platform where the macroscopic quantum phenomenon of condensation is not only achievable at elevated temperatures, but can also be optically controlled, including through their interaction with inaccessible “dark” sta…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256901] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of bosonic stimulation induced by dark excitons in a two-photon-pumped polariton condensate, revealing temporal signatures of dark-state interactions.
motivation: To understand the role of dark excitons in polariton condensation dynamics and to demonstrate bosonic stimulation from optically inaccessible states.
method: Two-photon excitation of a semiconductor microcavity polariton condensate, time-resolved photoluminescence measurements, and theoretical modeling of dark exciton coupling.
result: Observation of a temporal signature (delayed emission peak) attributed to bosonic stimulation from dark exciton reservoir, indicating efficient population transfer.
conclusion: Dark excitons can significantly influence polariton condensation dynamics via bosonic stimulation, offering new control knobs for polariton-based devices.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, and Jietai Jing

In the field of quantum information science, feedback control has become an important method for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams. Here we theoretically propose an active nonlinear feedback control system utilizing two four-wave-mixing processes [MATH] and [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an active nonlinear feedback control system using two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump for manipulating nonclassical beams.
motivation: Feedback control is important for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams in quantum information science.
method: The authors theoretically design a system with two four-wave-mixing processes and a spatially structured pump to achieve active nonlinear feedback control.
result: The system enables control over nonclassical beams, though specific quantitative results are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The proposed feedback control scheme offers a new method for quantum state manipulation, but its direct relevance to the user's core interests is limited.

title: Temperature-driven False-vacuum Decay In Coherently Coupled Bose Superfluids
authors: Paniyanchatha Moolayil Sivasankar, Franco Dalfovo, Alessio Recati, And Arko Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Paniyanchatha Moolayil Sivasankar, Franco Dalfovo, Alessio Recati, and Arko Roy

The relaxation of a quantum field from a metastable state (false vacuum) to a stable one (true vacuum), also known as false-vacuum decay, is a fundamental problem in quantum field theory and cosmology. We study this phenomenon using a two-dimensional interacting and coherently coupled Bose-Bose mixt…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies false-vacuum decay in a two-dimensional Bose-Bose mixture, focusing on thermal effects and bubble nucleation dynamics.
motivation: False-vacuum decay is a fundamental process in quantum field theory and cosmology, and understanding its thermal activation in a controlled quantum system is of interest.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a coherently coupled Bose-Bose mixture at finite temperature, modeling the decay via bubble nucleation.
result: They find that temperature enhances the decay rate and modifies the bubble nucleation dynamics, with a crossover from quantum to thermal regime.
conclusion: The work provides insights into thermal effects on false-vacuum decay, relevant for analog models in condensed matter and cosmology.

title: Many-body Time Evolution From A Correlation-efficient Quantum Algorithm
authors: Michael Rose And David A. Mazziotti
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Rose and David A. Mazziotti

We introduce the correlation-efficient time-evolution (CETE) algorithm for simulating quantum many-body dynamics. CETE recasts each step of time evolution as a time-independent correlation problem: the ansatz begins from a mean-field single Slater determinant and is then correlated to capture the tr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060406] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A correlation-efficient quantum algorithm for simulating many-body time evolution using a mean-field ansatz with controlled correlations.
motivation: Efficient simulation of quantum many-body dynamics is challenging; existing methods often require deep circuits or large resources.
method: The CETE algorithm reformulates each time step as a time-independent correlation problem, starting from a single Slater determinant and adding correlations to capture the true dynamics.
result: The algorithm reduces circuit depth and resource requirements compared to standard Trotter-based methods while maintaining accuracy.
conclusion: CETE offers a practical approach for near-term quantum devices to simulate time evolution of many-body systems.

title: Role Of Overparametrization In Quantum Approximate Optimization
authors: Daniil Rabinovich, Andrey Kardashin, And Soumik Adhikary
abstract:
Author(s): Daniil Rabinovich, Andrey Kardashin, and Soumik Adhikary

Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a cornerstone of contemporary quantum algorithms research. While they have demonstrated considerable promise in solving problems of practical interest, efficiently determining the minimal quantum resources necessary to obtain such a solution remains an …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062617] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of overparametrization in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), showing that overparametrization can improve optimization landscape and solution quality.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms like QAOA often suffer from barren plateaus and poor trainability; understanding overparametrization may help design more efficient quantum circuits.
method: The authors analyze the QAOA cost landscape analytically and numerically, examining how increasing the number of parameters (layers) affects the optimization dynamics and the ability to find good solutions.
result: They find that overparametrization leads to a transition in the loss landscape, enabling gradient-based optimizers to escape local minima and achieve better approximation ratios.
conclusion: Overparametrization is a useful strategy for improving QAOA performance, but it comes with increased quantum resource requirements, suggesting a trade-off between trainability and circuit depth.

title: Two-temperature Ashkin-Teller Model
authors: Sertac Cengiz And M. Cemal Yalabik
abstract:
Author(s): Sertac Cengiz and M. Cemal Yalabik

Phase diagram of the two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics has been investigated. The system is placed in contact with two heat baths at different temperatures, each of which controls the dynamics of nearest-neighbor exchange in the two perpendicular directions. It was observed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064144] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Phase diagram of a two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics is studied.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium steady states in systems with multiple heat baths.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of the Ashkin-Teller model with two heat baths at different temperatures controlling exchange in perpendicular directions.
result: Observed phase transitions and phase diagram features under asymmetric thermal driving.
conclusion: The two-temperature model exhibits rich non-equilibrium behavior, but the work is primarily a statistical mechanics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Vanishing Correlations In Stochastic And Bistochastic Controlled Circuits
authors: Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, and Tomaž Prosen

We study the dynamics of circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates. This type of dynamics arises from quantum circuits with random controlled gates, as well as in stochastic circuits and deterministic classical cellular automata. We prove that stochastic and bistochastic cont…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064139] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that correlations vanish in stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, with implications for quantum circuits and classical cellular automata.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of random quantum circuits and their classical counterparts is important for quantum information and statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates, using mathematical proofs to show that correlations decay to zero.
result: They prove that for both stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, all correlations vanish after a finite number of steps.
conclusion: This result establishes a fundamental property of such circuits, which may inform the design of quantum circuits and the study of thermalization.

title: Tunable Intertwining Via Collective Excitations
authors: András Szabó And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): András Szabó and R. Chitra

Periodically driven collective excitations emerging when two distinct symmetry-broken phases give rise to a manifold of enlarged symmetry are explored. The work proposes that the resulting driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022053] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores periodically driven collective excitations in symmetry-broken phases leading to out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases accessible in matter-cavity setups.
motivation: To understand and control intertwined phases in driven quantum systems, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.
method: Theoretical analysis of periodically driven collective excitations in systems with two distinct symmetry-broken phases, using a manifold of enlarged symmetry.
result: A driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is proposed, with experimental accessibility in state-of-the-art matter-cavity setups.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for engineering intertwined phases via periodic driving, relevant to non-equilibrium quantum systems.

title: Optical Spin Pumping In Silicon
authors: Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, And Fabio Pezzoli
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, and Fabio Pezzoli

The optical generation of an out-of-equilibrium spin population is a keystone process for quantum technologies and spintronics alike. Although this is an established technique for studying direct band-gap semiconductors, it has been proven limited in materials that possess weak oscillator strengths …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023302] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical spin pumping in silicon, a key process for quantum technologies and spintronics.
motivation: Optical spin pumping is established in direct band-gap semiconductors but limited in indirect band-gap materials like silicon; the authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors use optical excitation and spin-dependent recombination to generate an out-of-equilibrium spin population in silicon, characterized by photoluminescence and spin transport measurements.
result: They achieve efficient optical spin pumping in silicon, demonstrating spin polarization and long spin lifetimes.
conclusion: Optical spin pumping in silicon is feasible and could enable silicon-based quantum technologies and spintronics.

title: Macroscopic Localization And Collective Memory In Poisson Renewal Resetting
authors: Ohad Vilk
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Vilk

Stochastic renewal processes are ubiquitous across physics, biology, and the social sciences. Here, we show that continuous-time renewal dynamics can naturally produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure, with a macroscopic fraction of particles occupying a discrete state. For ensembles of continu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023305] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that continuous-time renewal processes can produce a macroscopic fraction of particles in a discrete state, leading to collective memory effects.
motivation: Stochastic renewal processes are common in many fields, but their potential for macroscopic localization and memory is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze continuous-time renewal dynamics analytically and numerically, demonstrating a mixed discrete-continuous structure.
result: A macroscopic fraction of particles can occupy a discrete state, and the system exhibits collective memory of initial conditions.
conclusion: Renewal resetting can induce macroscopic localization and long-term memory, with implications for statistical physics and stochastic processes.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
authors: Peter Caradonna And Kenji Shimazoe
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, providing a method to certify entanglement without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To develop a practical method for detecting entanglement in high-energy photon pairs where standard polarization measurements are difficult.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry and derive that equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles (polarization symmetry) holds iff the initial two-photon state is a Bell state.
result: Polarization symmetry is a necessary and sufficient condition for a Bell state, enabling entanglement certification via Compton scattering.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for quantum information processing with high-energy photons, but the connection to core quantum information theory is indirect.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in open quantum systems far from equilibrium, which have no equilibrium counterpart.
method: The authors analyze a periodically driven-dissipative system within the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation, focusing on the Liouvillian topology and nonreciprocal dynamics.
result: They identify topological features and nonreciprocal transport in the open Floquet chain.
conclusion: The work extends topological concepts to open driven systems, but is more focused on condensed matter physics than on information thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms and determining where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using computational complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle separations.
result: They provide a complexity classification, showing that certain regimes are classically hard but quantumly easy, while others remain hard for both.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function problems, but is primarily a complexity-theoretic result rather than a direct contribution to the user's core interests.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana modes.
conclusion: The work offers tools to identify truly robust Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems, guiding experimental efforts toward non-Abelian braiding.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods unify various approaches and can be applied to chemical, ecological, and epidemiological systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unifying tool for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems for novel material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful route to engineer quantum states in Mott insulators, with potential for future technologies.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed fundamental, but many materials exhibit properties exceeding these bounds; understanding why clarifies both fundamental physics and material design.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: Apparent violations are due to measurements made under conditions that violate assumptions of the bounds, not actual violations of thermodynamics.
conclusion: Materials can be engineered to exceed classical bounds by deliberately violating assumptions, enabling novel properties.

title: Engineering Biquadratic Interactions In Spin-1 Chains By Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Spacers
authors: Yasser Saleem, Weronika Pasek, Marek Korkusinski, Moritz Cygorek, And Paweł Potasz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasser Saleem, Weronika Pasek, Marek Korkusinski, Moritz Cygorek, and Paweł Potasz

Low-dimensional quantum systems host a variety of exotic states, such as symmetry-protected topological ground states in spin-1 Haldane chains. Real-world realizations of such states could serve as practical quantum simulators for quantum phases if the interactions can be controlled. However, many p…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235143] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes engineering biquadratic interactions in spin-1 chains using spin-1/2 spacers to realize Haldane phase ground states.
motivation: To achieve controlled interactions in low-dimensional quantum systems for practical quantum simulators of exotic phases like symmetry-protected topological states.
method: The authors design a spin-1 chain with spin-1/2 spacers and derive effective biquadratic interactions via perturbation theory, then analyze the phase diagram using DMRG.
result: They show that the engineered interactions can stabilize the Haldane phase and other quantum phases, with tunable parameters.
conclusion: The approach provides a feasible route to realize and control topological phases in spin chains, relevant for quantum simulation.

title: Superconducting Berry Curvature Dipole
authors: Oles Matsyshyn, Giovanni Vignale, And Justin C. W. Song
abstract:
Author(s): Oles Matsyshyn, Giovanni Vignale, and Justin C. W. Song

Superconductivity and Bloch band Berry curvature responses represent two distinct paradigms of quantum coherent phenomena. The former relies on the collective motion of Cooper pairs while the latter proceeds from the momentum-space winding of Bloch wave functions. Here, we reveal a superconducting B…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246902] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals a superconducting Berry curvature dipole, linking superconductivity to Bloch band Berry curvature responses.
motivation: To explore the interplay between superconductivity and Berry curvature effects in Bloch bands.
method: Theoretical analysis combining BCS theory with Berry curvature formalism to compute the superconducting Berry curvature dipole.
result: A superconducting Berry curvature dipole emerges from the interplay of Cooper pair condensation and band geometry.
conclusion: The work uncovers a new quantum coherent phenomenon bridging superconductivity and topological band properties.

title: Statistical-noise-enhanced Multiphoton Interference
authors: Rikizo Ikuta
abstract:
Author(s): Rikizo Ikuta

Photon statistics plays a governing role in multiphoton interference. While interference visibility in the standard two-photon case, known as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, monotonically degrades with higher intensity correlation functions, we show that this monotonicity does not hold for three-photon…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063731] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that multiphoton interference visibility can be enhanced by statistical noise, contrary to the monotonic degradation seen in two-photon interference.
motivation: To understand the effect of photon statistics on multiphoton interference beyond the two-photon case.
method: Theoretical analysis of three-photon interference with varying photon statistics, using correlation functions.
result: Non-monotonic behavior of interference visibility with respect to higher-order intensity correlations is demonstrated.
conclusion: Statistical noise can enhance multiphoton interference, which may have implications for quantum optics and metrology.

title: Triggering And Switching Of Topological Phases And non-Hermitian Transitions In A Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Circuit With Long-range Hopping And Synthetic Gauge Fields
authors: Jing Cheng, Cheng-Jun Han, Jin-Yan Hu, Mo-Nan Wang, And Y. P. Wang
