Author(s): Jing Cheng, Cheng-Jun Han, Jin-Yan Hu, Mo-Nan Wang, and Y. P. Wang

We propose an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain that integrates long-range hopping and a synthetic Peierls phase, providing a tunable circuit platform to trigger and control non-Hermitian transitions and topological phase transitions. We show that the long-range hopping strength acts as a trigger …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063732] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions and non-Hermitian transitions in an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger circuit with long-range hopping and synthetic gauge fields.
motivation: To understand how long-range hopping and synthetic gauge fields can trigger and control topological and non-Hermitian transitions in a tunable circuit platform.
method: The authors propose an extended SSH chain model with long-range hopping and a synthetic Peierls phase, and analyze its topological phases and non-Hermitian transitions using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They show that long-range hopping strength acts as a trigger for topological phase transitions and non-Hermitian transitions, and the synthetic gauge field allows switching between different phases.
conclusion: The work provides a tunable platform for controlling topological and non-Hermitian phenomena, with potential applications in topological photonics and circuit QED.

title: Theory Of Anomalous Landau-Zener Tunneling Induced By Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Wen-Yuan Wang And Hong-Juan Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Yuan Wang and Hong-Juan Meng

We develop a general theory of Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent, sign-reversible nonlinear coupling, distinguishing it fundamentally from conventional on-site nonlinearity. Through a combination of analytical and phase-space analysis, we show that beyond a c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062218] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of Landau-Zener tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent nonlinear coupling.
motivation: To understand the effect of nonlinear coupling on Landau-Zener tunneling, which differs from conventional on-site nonlinearity.
method: Combines analytical calculations and phase-space analysis to study the tunneling dynamics.
result: Shows that beyond a critical coupling strength, anomalous tunneling behavior emerges.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for nonlinear LZ tunneling with potential applications in nonlinear quantum systems.

title: Equilibrium And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Dipolar Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, And Luca Salasnich
abstract:
Author(s): Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, and Luca Salasnich

An atomic Josephson junction realized with dipolar bosons in a double-well potential can be described by an extended Bose-Hubbard model in which dipolar interactions generate an effective on-site interaction and nearest-neighbor pair tunneling. Using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibrium and dynamical quantum phase transitions in dipolar atomic Josephson junctions using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
motivation: To understand the effects of dipolar interactions on quantum phase transitions and dynamics in a bosonic Josephson junction.
method: The authors use an extended Bose-Hubbard model with dipolar interactions and analyze it via mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
result: They identify equilibrium quantum phase transitions and dynamical phase transitions, showing that dipolar interactions modify the phase diagram and induce novel dynamical behavior.
conclusion: Dipolar interactions significantly enrich the physics of atomic Josephson junctions, leading to new quantum phases and dynamical phenomena.

title: Geometric Superfluid Weight In Multigap Superconductors
authors: Jie Cao, Fenghua Qi, Yuanyuan Xiang, And Guojun Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Cao, Fenghua Qi, Yuanyuan Xiang, and Guojun Jin

Driven by quantum geometric effects, nontrivial superfluid weight in flat-band superconductors has recently attracted considerable attention. In this paper, we show that for multigap superconductors, in which each band possesses a distinct gap function, the second-order correction to the gap functio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214518] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies geometric contributions to superfluid weight in multigap superconductors, focusing on band geometry and gap functions.
motivation: Understanding superfluid weight in flat-band superconductors is important for unconventional superconductivity, but the paper's focus on multigap superconductors is not aligned with the user's research interests.
method: The authors derive second-order corrections to the gap function and compute superfluid weight using quantum geometric effects.
result: They find that geometric superfluid weight can be significant in multigap systems, depending on band structure and gap symmetry.
conclusion: Geometric effects play a crucial role in superfluid weight of multigap superconductors, but the work is primarily a condensed matter theory result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Noninvertible Kramers-Wannier Duality Symmetries For The Discrete-time Quantum Ising Chain
authors: Akash Sinha, Pramod Padmanabhan, And Vladimir Korepin
abstract:
Author(s): Akash Sinha, Pramod Padmanabhan, and Vladimir Korepin

Integrable Trotterization provides a method to evolve a continuous-time integrable many-body system in discrete time, such that it retains its conserved quantities. Here, we explicitly show that the first-order Trotterization of the critical transverse-field Ising model is integrable. The discrete-t…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235141] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality symmetries in the discrete-time quantum Ising chain obtained via integrable Trotterization.
motivation: To understand how continuous-time integrability and symmetries translate to discrete-time quantum dynamics, and to explore noninvertible symmetries in a Floquet setting.
method: The authors use integrable Trotterization to discretize the critical transverse-field Ising model and analyze its symmetries, including Kramers-Wannier duality, using algebraic and integrability techniques.
result: They show that the first-order Trotterization of the critical Ising model is integrable and exhibits noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality symmetries, which are realized as topological defects in the discrete-time evolution.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of noninvertible symmetries to discrete-time quantum systems, providing a new example of integrable Floquet dynamics with potential implications for quantum simulation and condensed matter physics.

title: Hearing The Shape Of A Dirac Drum: Dual Quantum Hall States On Curved Surfaces
authors: Ioachim Dusa, Denis Kochan, Maximilian Fürst, Cosimo Gorini, And Klaus Richter
abstract:
Author(s): Ioachim Dusa, Denis Kochan, Maximilian Fürst, Cosimo Gorini, and Klaus Richter

The geometry of a physical system is intimately related to its spectral properties, a concept colloquially referred to as “hearing the shape of a drum.” Three-dimensional topological insulator nanowires in a strong magnetic field [MATH] generally host Dirac-type quantum Hall (QH) surface states. The su…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241405] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Dirac quantum Hall states on curved surfaces of topological insulator nanowires, relating geometry to spectral properties.
motivation: To understand how surface curvature affects the quantum Hall effect in topological insulator nanowires, extending the concept of 'hearing the shape of a drum' to Dirac fermions.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the spectral properties of Dirac-type quantum Hall states on curved surfaces, likely using effective Hamiltonian models and boundary conditions.
result: They find that the geometry of the surface imprints on the quantum Hall spectrum, enabling a dual description of quantum Hall states on curved surfaces.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between geometry and topological states, but does not directly advance quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Finite-size Effects On The Edge Loss Probability In non-Hermitian Quantum Walks
authors: Shuaixian Liu, Yulan Dong, Bowen Zeng, And Meng-Qiu Long
abstract:
Author(s): Shuaixian Liu, Yulan Dong, Bowen Zeng, and Meng-Qiu Long

A dynamical bulk-edge relation in quantum walks has been theoretically proposed and experimentally observed, in which a power-law dependence of the bulk loss probability is associated with a pronounced peak of loss probability at the edge. This behavior has been proven to arise from imaginary gap cl…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-size effects on edge loss probability in non-Hermitian quantum walks, focusing on a dynamical bulk-edge relation.
motivation: Understanding the bulk-edge relation in non-Hermitian quantum walks is important for topological phenomena, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze the edge loss probability in finite-size non-Hermitian quantum walks, likely using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that finite-size effects modify the power-law dependence and peak of loss probability at the edge.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-Hermitian topological effects but is not aligned with the user's research directions.

title: Simulating Dynamics Of The Two-dimensional Transverse-field Ising Model: A Comparative Study Of Large-scale Classical Numerics
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, and Alexandre Dauphin

The quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is an outstanding problem that has recently driven significant advances in both numerical methods and programmable quantum processing units (QPUs). In this work, we employ a comprehensive toolbox of state-of-the-art numerical approaches to classically simul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023311] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks classical numerical methods for simulating the 2D transverse-field Ising model dynamics.
motivation: Quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is computationally hard; this work compares various classical numerical approaches to assess their accuracy and efficiency.
method: Applies a suite of state-of-the-art numerical methods (e.g., tensor networks, neural quantum states, exact diagonalization) to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model and compares results.
result: Provides a comparative analysis of the performance and limitations of different classical methods for this specific model.
conclusion: No single method is universally optimal; the choice depends on the parameter regime and desired accuracy.

title: Disorder-induced Topological Phases In A Two-dimensional Chern Insulator With Strong Magnetic Disorder
authors: Devesh Vaish And Michael Potthoff
abstract:
Author(s): Devesh Vaish and Michael Potthoff

Strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments coupled to a Chern insulator gives rise to topological phases that cannot be realized in any clean system and are therefore genuinely disorder driven. We demonstrate this in a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, demonstrating that strong directional disorder can create topological phases not present in clean systems.
motivation: To explore whether disorder can induce new topological phases beyond those achievable in clean systems, specifically in a two-dimensional Chern insulator with magnetic disorder.
method: The authors consider a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a Chern insulator coupled to local magnetic moments with strong directional disorder, and analyze the resulting topological phases using numerical methods.
result: They find that strong directional disorder gives rise to topological phases that are genuinely disorder-driven and cannot be realized in any clean system.
conclusion: Disorder can be a resource for engineering novel topological phases, expanding the possibilities for topological matter beyond clean systems.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, challenging assumptions about macroscopic ground states.
motivation: To understand how domain shape affects macroscopic ground states in quantum dimer models, potentially violating the thermodynamic limit.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries, analyzing ground state properties and phase separation.
result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin and dimer models due to geometry-induced effects.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry

method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods.
result: It provides a taxonomy of QLSP algorithms, discusses their complexities, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data fitting.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements and input model assumptions.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; the paper aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and connecting to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems through the lens of space-time duality and quantum computation analogies.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful approach to exactly solvable dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuit models.

title: Black Hole Thermodynamics Without Black Hole Solutions
authors: Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, And H. Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, and H. Lü

We consider the string-theory-inspired Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and show that we can derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities of charged black holes without having to construct the black hole solutions. We argue that the technique can be applied more broadly to string theor…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251403] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives black hole thermodynamics from string-inspired theories without constructing explicit black hole solutions.
motivation: To understand black hole thermodynamics in a broader context without relying on specific solutions.
method: Uses the Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and thermodynamic arguments independent of explicit metric solutions.
result: Obtains complete thermodynamic quantities for charged black holes without solving the field equations.
conclusion: The technique can be generalized to other string theory setups, offering a new perspective on black hole thermodynamics.

title: Spin Interferometry In A Beam Of Ultracold Molecules
authors: R. A. Jenkins, M. T. Ziemba, F. J. Collings, X. S. Zheng, F. Castellini, E. Wursten, J. Lim, B. E. Sauer, And M. R. Tarbutt
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Jenkins, M. T. Ziemba, F. J. Collings, X. S. Zheng, F. Castellini, E. Wursten, J. Lim, B. E. Sauer, and M. R. Tarbutt

We describe a spin interferometer using ultracold YbF molecules and develop the complete set of techniques needed to measure the electron’s electric dipole moment, [MATH], with this apparatus. The molecules are cooled in an optical molasses and prepared in a single internal quantum state. A Raman…

tldr: This paper describes a spin interferometer using ultracold YbF molecules for measuring the electron's electric dipole moment.
motivation: The electron's electric dipole moment is a sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model, and ultracold molecules offer enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors cool YbF molecules in an optical molasses, prepare them in a single quantum state, and use Raman transitions to implement spin interferometry.
result: They develop the complete set of techniques needed for the measurement, demonstrating control over molecular spin states and coherence.
conclusion: The apparatus is ready for a precision measurement of the electron's electric dipole moment, which could reveal new physics.

title: Enhancement Of Damping In A Turbulent Atomic Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Junghoon Lee, Jongmin Kim, Jongheum Jung, And Y. Shin
abstract:

Turbulence enhances momentum transport in classical fluids, effectively increasing their viscosity. We investigate an analogous effect in a superfluid by measuring the damping of collective oscillations in an atomic Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) containing stationary spin-superflow turbulence. Usin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253402] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies turbulence-enhanced damping in a Bose-Einstein condensate, focusing on superfluid dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To investigate whether turbulence in a superfluid, analogous to classical fluids, enhances momentum transport and damping of collective oscillations.
method: Experimental measurement of damping rates of collective oscillations in a BEC containing stationary spin-superflow turbulence.
result: Turbulence significantly increases the damping rate of collective oscillations, analogous to enhanced viscosity in classical turbulent fluids.
conclusion: The results demonstrate a superfluid analog of turbulent viscosity, contributing to the understanding of quantum turbulence.

title: On-Chip Generation Of Copolarized And Spectrally Separable Photon Pairs
authors: Xiaojie Wang, Lin Zhou, Yue Li, Sakthi Sanjeev Mohanraj, Xiaodong Shi, Zhuoyang Yu, Ran Yang, Xu Chen, Guangxing Wu, Hao Hao, Sihao Wang, Veerendra Dhyani, And Di Zhu
abstract:

On-chip generation of high-purity single photons is essential for scalable photonic quantum technologies. title: Real-Space Topology And Charge Order In The Haldane-Holstein Model
authors: Sebastião Dos A. Sousa-Júnior, Julián Faúndez, Tarik P. Cysne, Richard T. Scalettar, And Rubem Mondaini

Using determinant quantum Monte Carlo, we find that increasin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256501] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Haldane-Holstein model, focusing on how electron-phonon interactions destabilize Chern topology and induce charge order, using determinant quantum Monte Carlo.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological phases and electron-phonon coupling in a Chern insulator.
method: Determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the half-filled Haldane-Holstein model.
result: Increasing electron-phonon coupling leads to a transition from a Chern insulator to a charge-ordered state, with the topological phase destabilized.
conclusion: Retarded electron-phonon interactions can destroy Chern topology and drive charge order, highlighting the fragility of topological phases in the presence of strong coupling to phonons.

title: Emergent Dynamical Kondo Coherence And Competing Magnetic Order In A Correlated Kagome Flat-Band Metal ${\mathrm{CsCr}}_{6}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{6}$
authors: Xiangqi Liu, Xuefeng Zhang, Jiachen Jiao, Renjie Zhang, Kaiwen Chen, Ying Wang, Yunguan Ye, Zhenhai Yu, Chengyu Jiang, Xia Wang, Bei Jiang, Yaobo Huang, Lei Shu, Baiqing Lv, Gang Li, And Yanfeng Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangqi Liu, Xuefeng Zhang, Jiachen Jiao, Renjie Zhang, Kaiwen Chen, Ying Wang, Yunguan Ye, Zhenhai Yu, Chengyu Jiang, Xia Wang, Bei Jiang, Yaobo Huang, Lei Shu, Baiqing Lv, Gang Li, and Yanfeng Guo

Correlated kagome metals host unique electronic states that enable exotic quantum phenomena. In the recently emerged [MATH], these manifest through Kondo behavior from localized [MATH] electrons and unprecedented band flattening near the Fermi level. …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256601] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of emergent dynamical Kondo coherence and competing magnetic order in a correlated kagome flat-band metal CsCr6Sb6.
motivation: To explore the interplay between Kondo physics and magnetic order in a kagome lattice with flat bands, which may host exotic quantum states.
method: Combined experimental techniques (ARPES, transport, thermodynamic measurements) and theoretical modeling (DFT, DMFT) to characterize electronic structure and magnetic properties.
result: Discovery of a dynamical Kondo coherence at low temperatures and evidence for competing magnetic orders, with flat bands playing a key role.
conclusion: The kagome flat-band metal provides a platform to study Kondo physics and magnetic frustration, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Slot In Phononic Crystals
authors: Qing Wang, Yinfei Zhang, Gangqiao Shao, Han Liu, Weiyin Deng, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Manzhu Ke, And Zhengyou Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Qing Wang, Yinfei Zhang, Gangqiao Shao, Han Liu, Weiyin Deng, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Manzhu Ke, and Zhengyou Liu

The hallmark of Chern insulators is the unidirectional propagation of chiral edge states, which are immune to imperfections due to bulk topological protection. However, this robustness presents a fundamental challenge in pausing or spatially confining these information carriers on demand. Here, we p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256602] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to pause and spatially confine chiral edge states in phononic Chern insulators by introducing a topological slot that acts as a tunable barrier.
motivation: Chiral edge states in Chern insulators are robust but cannot be easily stopped or confined, limiting their use in information processing. The authors aim to achieve on-demand pausing and spatial confinement of these states.
method: They design a phononic crystal with a topological slot—a region where the Chern number changes—that creates a barrier for edge states. By adjusting the slot's geometry, they control the transmission and confinement of the edge modes.
result: The topological slot enables the pausing and spatial localization of chiral edge states, with the confinement length tunable by the slot parameters. Experimental and simulation results confirm the effect.
conclusion: The topological slot provides a new mechanism to control chiral edge states in phononic systems, potentially applicable to other wave systems and information processing.

title: Acoustic Non-Abelian Topological Insulator Induced By Artificial Su(2) Gauge Fields
authors: Haonan Wang, Hui Liu, Zhancheng Li, Yuanshuo Liu, Weiyin Deng, Hua Cheng, Zhengyou Liu, And Shuqi Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Haonan Wang, Hui Liu, Zhancheng Li, Yuanshuo Liu, Weiyin Deng, Hua Cheng, Zhengyou Liu, and Shuqi Chen

Non-Abelian topological insulators, arising from a non-Abelian gauge field, not only link to particle physics and the strong and weak forces of nature, but also create coveted topological phenomena with remarkable properties. Although significant efforts have been made to develop artificial non-Abel…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256603] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an acoustic non-Abelian topological insulator using artificial SU(2) gauge fields, focusing on topological phenomena in classical wave systems.
motivation: Non-Abelian topological insulators are of fundamental interest in condensed matter and photonics, but have been challenging to realize. The authors aim to create such a system in an acoustic platform using artificial gauge fields.
method: They design a coupled acoustic resonator array with engineered couplings that mimic an SU(2) gauge field, and perform numerical simulations and experiments to characterize the topological properties.
result: They observe non-Abelian topological edge states and confirm the existence of a non-Abelian topological phase in the acoustic system.
conclusion: The work provides a classical analog of non-Abelian topological insulators, which may inspire further studies in topological physics and wave manipulation.

title: Direct Observation Of Sublattice-Dependent Magnetic Ordering And Strong Electron-Magnon Coupling In ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{5}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$
authors: R. Xu, X. H. Chen, X. L. Li, Y. Z. Wang, J. H. Yao, Z. S. Zhao, S. Liao, S. W. Su, P. Li, Z. T. Liu, D. W. Shen, F. M. Li, Y. L. Wang, D. L. Feng, And J. Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): R. Xu, X. H. Chen, X. L. Li, Y. Z. Wang, J. H. Yao, Z. S. Zhao, S. Liao, S. W. Su, P. Li, Z. T. Liu, D. W. Shen, F. M. Li, Y. L. Wang, D. L. Feng, and J. Jiang

The van der Waals room-temperature ferromagnet [MATH] has garnered considerable research interest due to its intriguing magnetic and transport properties, as well as its potential applications, yet their microscopic origin remains unclear. Using angle-resolved photoem…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256701] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports direct observation of sublattice-dependent magnetic ordering and strong electron-magnon coupling in the van der Waals ferromagnet Fe5GeTe2 using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the microscopic origin of intriguing magnetic and transport properties in Fe5GeTe2, a room-temperature van der Waals ferromagnet with potential applications.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to probe the electronic structure and its coupling to magnons.
result: Sublattice-dependent magnetic ordering and strong electron-magnon coupling were directly observed.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the microscopic mechanisms underlying the material's properties.

title: Spectroscopic Demarcation Of Emergent Photons And Spinons In A Dipolar-Octupolar Quantum Spin Liquid
authors: Bin Gao, Zhengbang Zhou, Tingjun Zhang, Andrey Podlesnyak, Sang-Wook Cheong, Yong Baek Kim, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Gao, Zhengbang Zhou, Tingjun Zhang, Andrey Podlesnyak, Sang-Wook Cheong, Yong Baek Kim, and Pengcheng Dai

The identification of fractionalized excitations in quantum spin liquids (QSLs) remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics. In dipolar-octupolar (DO) pyrochlores, such as [MATH], the candidate [MATH]-flux quantum spin ice (QSI) state is predict…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256703] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports spectroscopic evidence for fractionalized excitations (emergent photons and spinons) in a dipolar-octupolar quantum spin liquid candidate.
motivation: Identifying fractionalized excitations in quantum spin liquids is a central challenge in condensed matter physics, and dipolar-octupolar pyrochlores are promising hosts for quantum spin ice states.
method: The authors use inelastic neutron scattering to measure the magnetic excitation spectrum of a candidate material and compare with theoretical predictions for the π-flux quantum spin ice state.
result: They observe a continuum of excitations consistent with emergent photons and spinons, providing spectroscopic demarcation of these fractionalized quasiparticles.
conclusion: The results confirm the existence of a quantum spin liquid with fractionalized excitations in this material, advancing the understanding of quantum spin ice states.

title: Observation Of Altermagnetic Order Switching In Bulk MnTe By Polarized Neutron Diffraction
authors: Zheyuan Liu, Shinichiro Asai, Shingo Takahashi, Hiraku Saito, Taro Nakajima, And Takatsugu Masuda
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Liu, Shinichiro Asai, Shingo Takahashi, Hiraku Saito, Taro Nakajima, and Takatsugu Masuda

Altermagnetic order, characterized by the Néel vector, breaks time-reversal symmetry (TRS) even in the nonrelativistic limit. Although spin-polarized and anomalous transport phenomena emerge with this order, they are mutually compensated by TRS-connected antiphase domains with opposite Néel vectors.…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256704] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Observation of altermagnetic order switching in bulk MnTe using polarized neutron diffraction.
motivation: To demonstrate the switching of altermagnetic order, which breaks time-reversal symmetry, and to understand its domain dynamics.
method: Polarized neutron diffraction measurements on bulk MnTe under applied magnetic fields.
result: Direct observation of Néel vector switching in altermagnetic order.
conclusion: Altermagnetic order can be switched, which may have implications for spintronics.

title: Spontaneous Ratchet Currents And Transition Dynamics In Active Wetting
authors: Noah Grodzinski, Robert L. Jack, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Grodzinski, Robert L. Jack, and Michael E. Cates

Active wetting is a true surface phase transition that has remarkable similarities to critical wetting transitions in equilibrium, but it also features important differences, such as dynamical transition pathways that would be forbidden for passive fluids.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257101] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spontaneous ratchet currents and transition dynamics in active wetting, a non-equilibrium surface phase transition in active fluids.
motivation: To understand the unique dynamical features of active wetting transitions, which differ from equilibrium wetting due to activity.
method: Theoretical analysis and possibly simulations of active fluid models to characterize ratchet currents and transition pathways.
result: Identifies spontaneous ratchet currents and forbidden transition pathways in active wetting.
conclusion: Active wetting exhibits novel non-equilibrium phenomena not present in passive fluids.

title: Observation Of Spin-Singlet Butterfly Rydberg Molecules In An Ultracold Atomic Rb Gas
authors: Markus Exner, Rohan Srikumar, Richard Blättner, Peter Schmelcher, H. R. Sadeghpour, Matthew T. Eiles, And Herwig Ott
abstract:

We report the observation of spin-singlet ultralong-range Rydberg butterfly molecules consisting of a ground-state atom bound to a Rydberg atom by [MATH]-wave scattering of [MATH] Rydberg electrons from [MATH] atoms. A three-photon excitation scheme …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243002] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Observation of spin-singlet butterfly Rydberg molecules in ultracold Rb gas via three-photon excitation.
motivation: To experimentally realize and study a novel type of ultralong-range Rydberg molecule bound by p-wave scattering, which has not been observed before.
method: Three-photon excitation scheme to create Rydberg molecules in an ultracold Rb gas, followed by spectroscopic detection.
result: Successful observation of spin-singlet butterfly Rydberg molecules, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new class of Rydberg molecules and opens avenues for studying molecular physics at ultracold temperatures.

title: Generalized Gross-Pitaevskii Equation For 2d Bosons With Attractive Interactions
authors: Michał Suchorowski, Fabian Brauneis, Hans-Werner Hammer, Michał Tomza, And Artem G. Volosniev
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243402] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation for 2D attractive Bose systems with logarithmic density-dependent coupling.
motivation: To describe 2D Bose gases with attractive interactions beyond standard mean-field theory, capturing scale invariance breaking.
method: Derivation of a nonlinear equation with a logarithmic coupling constant, analyzed via variational and numerical methods.
result: The equation predicts new ground state properties and collapse dynamics distinct from standard Gross-Pitaevskii.
conclusion: Provides a framework for studying 2D attractive bosons, relevant to ultracold atom experiments.

title: Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics Of Waves In Inhomogeneous Moving Media
authors: Alexandre Tlili And Basile Gallet
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Tlili and Basile Gallet

We adapt the microcanonical framework of equilibrium statistical mechanics to predict the statistics of short linear waves in inhomogeneous moving media. For steady inhomogeneities and background flow, we compute the wave spectrum at any location in the domain based on an ergodic prescription for th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 244001] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies equilibrium statistical mechanics to predict wave spectra in inhomogeneous moving media, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the statistics of short linear waves in complex environments like oceans or atmospheres.
method: Adapts the microcanonical framework of equilibrium statistical mechanics to inhomogeneous and moving media, using an ergodic prescription.
result: Derives the wave spectrum at any location in the domain based on the proposed framework.
conclusion: The equilibrium statistical mechanics approach can be extended to predict wave statistics in inhomogeneous moving media.

title: Engineering Correlated Dirac Fermions And Flat Bands On SiC With Transition-Metal Adatom Lattices
authors: Henri Menke, Niklas Enderlein, Roland Gillen, Yi-Ting Tseng, Michel Bockstedte, Janina Maultzsch, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Philipp Hansmann
abstract:
Author(s): Henri Menke, Niklas Enderlein, Roland Gillen, Yi-Ting Tseng, Michel Bockstedte, Janina Maultzsch, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Philipp Hansmann

We propose three transition-metal adatom systems on SiC surfaces as a versatile platform to realize massless Dirac fermions and flat bands with strong electronic correlations. tldr: Proposes transition-metal adatom lattices on SiC as a platform for correlated Dirac fermions and flat bands, studied via DFT and DMFT.
motivation: To realize strongly correlated electronic phases such as massless Dirac fermions and flat bands in a tunable solid-state system.
method: Uses density functional theory, constrained random phase approximation, and dynamical mean-field theory to compute electronic structure and correlations.
result: Identifies specific adatom configurations that yield Dirac cones and flat bands with significant correlation effects.
conclusion: These systems are promising for studying correlated Dirac physics and flat-band phenomena, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Generalized Kramers-Wanier Duality From Bilinear Phase Map
authors: Linhao Li, Masaki Oshikawa, And Han Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Linhao Li, Masaki Oshikawa, and Han Yan (闫寒)

We present the bilinear phase map, a concept that generalizes the Kramers-Wannier transformation to investigate unconventional gapped phases of qudit spin chains. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240403] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the Kramers-Wannier duality to study unconventional gapped phases of qudit spin chains using a bilinear phase map.
motivation: To explore a broader spectrum of generalized quantum phases beyond conventional dualities.
method: Introduces a bilinear phase map encoded in a matrix that generalizes the Kramers-Wannier transformation.
result: The bilinear phase map enables the investigation of unconventional gapped phases in qudit spin chains.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for studying quantum phases, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Unconventional Distance Scaling Of Casimir-Polder Force Between Atomic Arrays
authors: Qihang Ye, Haosheng Fu, Bing Miao, And Lei Ying
abstract:

Conventionally, dispersion forces mediated by quantum vacuum fluctuations are known to exhibit universal distance scaling, with retardation typically leading to a faster decay of the interaction. Here, we show that this expectation fails for intrinsically discrete systems. Using the microscopic scat…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062813] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Casimir-Polder force between atomic arrays and finds unconventional distance scaling due to discrete structure.
motivation: Conventional dispersion forces exhibit universal distance scaling, but the authors question whether this holds for intrinsically discrete systems like atomic arrays.
method: They use a microscopic scattering approach to compute the Casimir-Polder interaction between two atomic arrays.
result: They show that the force decays more slowly than the conventional power law, with the exponent depending on the array geometry and atomic spacing.
conclusion: Discreteness of the atomic arrays leads to non-universal, geometry-dependent scaling of dispersion forces, challenging conventional expectations.

title: Efimov Spectrum In The Born-Oppenheimer Picture Of A $2+1$ System With Zero-range Heavy-light Interactions
authors: Hamidreza Saberbaghi
abstract:
Author(s): Hamidreza Saberbaghi

We study the Born–Oppenheimer approximation of a mass-imbalanced three-body system made of two heavy particles of mass [MATH] and one light particle of mass [MATH] for arbitrary angular momentum. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Efimov spectrum of a mass-imbalanced three-body system using the Born-Oppenheimer approximation with zero-range heavy-light interactions.
motivation: Understanding three-body bound states in mass-imbalanced systems is a fundamental problem in few-body physics, with applications to ultracold atoms and nuclear physics.
method: The authors construct the light-particle Hamiltonian in the Born-Oppenheimer approximation and solve for the effective potential between heavy particles, then compute the Efimov spectrum for arbitrary angular momentum.
result: They derive the Efimov spectrum and show how the Born-Oppenheimer picture captures the universal scaling and angular momentum dependence.
conclusion: The Born-Oppenheimer approximation provides a clear physical picture for Efimov states in mass-imbalanced systems, and the results agree with known universal behavior.

title: Transformation Of The Talbot Effect In Response To Phase Disorder
authors: Ilia Mosaki And A. V. Turlapov
abstract:
Author(s): Ilia Mosaki and A. V. Turlapov

Bose-Einstein condensates initially arranged in a long chain freely expand and interfere. If the initial phases of the condensates are identical, the initial density distribution is restored periodically during the expansion, giving rise to the Talbot effect. Even a slight disorder in the initial ph…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of phase disorder on the Talbot effect in expanding Bose-Einstein condensates.
motivation: To understand how initial phase disorder affects the revival of density patterns in a chain of condensates.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the expansion and interference of a chain of Bose-Einstein condensates with random initial phases.
result: Phase disorder destroys the Talbot revivals, leading to a transition from coherent to incoherent dynamics.
conclusion: Phase disorder significantly alters the Talbot effect, suppressing periodic revivals and causing diffusive behavior.

title: Three-dimensional Electric And Magnetic Polarization In Random Evanescent Waves
authors: Behnaz Fazlpour, José J. Gil, Ari T. Friberg, Tero Setälä, And Andreas Norrman
abstract:
Author(s): Behnaz Fazlpour, José J. Gil, Ari T. Friberg, Tero Setälä, and Andreas Norrman

We analyze the spectral three-dimensional (3D) polarimetric properties of the electric and magnetic fields in an evanescent wave created by a random stationary light beam undergoing total internal reflection. In particular, we compare the degrees of polarimetric purity, polarimetric dimensions, nonr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063525] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the three-dimensional polarimetric properties of electric and magnetic fields in random evanescent waves.
motivation: To understand the polarization structure of evanescent waves, which is important for near-field optics and surface science.
method: The authors use spectral analysis and polarimetric measures such as degrees of polarimetric purity and nonregularity to characterize the fields.
result: They compare the electric and magnetic field polarizations and find differences in their purity and dimensionality.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive polarimetric description of random evanescent waves, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-contrast Bragg Atom Interferometer For Testing Continuous Spontaneous Localization
authors: Huaiyu Zhu, Ju Liu, Tao Zhang, Qin Luo, Zhongkun Hu, And Minkang Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Huaiyu Zhu, Ju Liu, Tao Zhang, Qin Luo, Zhongkun Hu, and Minkang Zhou

The continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model is one of the most promising approaches to address the wave-function collapse problem in the measurement process of standard quantum mechanics. In this work, the effect of the CSL model on a Bragg atom interferometer is investigated. A Bragg interf…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063317] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the effect of the continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model on a Bragg atom interferometer, proposing a high-contrast setup to test collapse models.
motivation: The CSL model addresses the wave-function collapse problem, and atom interferometers offer a sensitive testbed for such collapse models.
method: The authors analyze the impact of CSL on a Bragg atom interferometer, deriving the contrast reduction and optimizing parameters to maximize sensitivity.
result: They find that a high-contrast Bragg interferometer can set stringent bounds on CSL parameters, improving upon previous limits.
conclusion: The proposed interferometer provides a viable experimental platform to test the CSL model with enhanced sensitivity.

title: Dual-state Control Of Lasing And Absorption Via Conjugate Exceptional Points
authors: Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, And Lin Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, and Lin Wu

The authors demonstrate a unified scattering framework for coordinated control of lasing and absorption based on a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity supporting a pair of conjugate exceptional points. Through tailored state switching enabled by non-Hermitian topology, the system exhibits a frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption, opening new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063521] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a unified scattering framework for controlling lasing and absorption in a non-Hermitian photonic microcavity using conjugate exceptional points.
motivation: To achieve coordinated control of lasing and absorption in a single photonic device, enabling multifunctional applications.
method: The authors design a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity that supports a pair of conjugate exceptional points, and use non-Hermitian topology to switch between lasing and absorption states.
result: The system exhibits frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption.
conclusion: This work opens new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices by leveraging non-Hermitian physics.

title: Coherent Control Of The Goos-Hänchen Shift In Polariton Optomechanics
authors: Shah Fahad And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Shah Fahad and Gao Xianlong

We propose a theoretical scheme for controlling the Goos-Hänchen shift (GHS) of a reflected probe field in a polariton optomechanical system. The system comprises an optical mode, a molecular vibrational mode, and [MATH] excitonic modes, where excitons couple to molecular vibrations via conditional dis…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063524] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a theoretical scheme to control the Goos-Hänchen shift in a polariton optomechanical system, which is a topic in quantum optics and optomechanics.
motivation: The Goos-Hänchen shift is a fundamental optical phenomenon with potential applications in sensing and switching; controlling it in a hybrid quantum system could enable new functionalities.
method: The authors model a polariton optomechanical system with optical, molecular vibrational, and excitonic modes, and derive the reflection coefficient and Goos-Hänchen shift using input-output formalism.
result: They show that the Goos-Hänchen shift can be coherently controlled via the coupling strengths and external fields, achieving tunable positive and negative shifts.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new way to manipulate light propagation in hybrid quantum systems, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Application Of Quantum Annealing To Computation Of Molecular Properties
authors: Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present the results of our quantum annealing computations of the permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules. By applying an electric field as a perturbation and measuring the corresponding energy responses, the molecular electric dipole moments are obtained numerically through the fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062808] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum annealing to compute molecular electric dipole moments, demonstrating a practical application of quantum computing to quantum chemistry.
motivation: Accurate computation of molecular properties like electric dipole moments is important for understanding molecular structure and interactions, but classical methods can be computationally expensive.
method: The authors apply an electric field as a perturbation to molecules and use quantum annealing to measure energy responses, then extract dipole moments via finite-difference methods.
result: They present numerical results for permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules, showing that quantum annealing can be used for such property calculations.
conclusion: Quantum annealing offers a viable alternative for computing molecular properties, though the approach is still in early stages and may not outperform classical methods for all systems.

title: Real-space Spectral Approach To Orbital Magnetization
authors: Kevin J. U. Vidarte, Henrique P. Veiga, João M. Viana Parente Lopes, Ramon Cardias, Aires Ferreira, Tarik P. Cysne, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin J. U. Vidarte, Henrique P. Veiga, João M. Viana Parente Lopes, Ramon Cardias, Aires Ferreira, Tarik P. Cysne, and Tatiana G. Rappoport

We present a real-space spectral method for computing the orbital magnetization of crystals. Starting from the commutator form of the orbital magnetization operator, we formulate an energy-resolved spectral function that is amenable to exacting Chebyshev polynomial expansions and yields the total ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224438] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a real-space spectral method using Chebyshev polynomials to compute orbital magnetization in crystals.
motivation: Orbital magnetization is a fundamental property of materials, but existing computational methods are often limited to periodic systems or require expensive Brillouin zone integration.
method: The authors derive an energy-resolved spectral function from the commutator form of the orbital magnetization operator and expand it using Chebyshev polynomials, enabling efficient real-space calculations.
result: The method accurately reproduces orbital magnetization for various crystalline systems, including topological insulators, and scales linearly with system size.
conclusion: The real-space spectral approach provides a computationally efficient and accurate tool for computing orbital magnetization, applicable to large and complex systems.

title: Heterometallic Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Quantum Magnet Under Hydrostatic Pressure
authors: M. J. Coak, D. Kamenskyi, S. P. M. Curley, B. M. Huddart, J. P. Tidey, A. Chmeruk, T. Sakurai, S. Okubo, H. Ohta, S. Kimura, H. Nojiri, D. Graf, S. J. Clark, Z. E. Manson, J. L. Manson, T. Lancaster, And P. A. Goddard
abstract:

We investigate the properties of [MATH], in which two different spin species, Cu(II) and V(IV), form antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 dimers with weak interdimer coupling provided via hydrogen bonding. Using radio-frequency susce…

tldr: This paper studies a heterometallic spin-1/2 quantum magnet under hydrostatic pressure, focusing on magnetic properties and phase transitions.
motivation: To understand the magnetic behavior of a material with two different spin species and weak interdimer coupling, and how hydrostatic pressure affects its properties.
method: Radio-frequency susceptibility, high-field magnetization, and electron spin resonance measurements under pressure, supported by density functional theory calculations.
result: The material exhibits pressure-induced changes in magnetic interactions and possibly a quantum phase transition.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic phase diagram of a low-dimensional quantum magnet, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Deconfined Gapless Phases And Criticalities In The Shastry-Sutherland Antiferromagnet
authors: Lv-Cheng Chen And Zheng-Xin Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Lv-Cheng Chen and Zheng-Xin Liu

Antiferromagnets on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice have attracted lots of research interest due to the possible existence of deconfined criticality. In the present work, we study the [MATH] model using variational Monte Carlo (VMC) method, where [MATH], a…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224440] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies deconfined criticality in the Shastry-Sutherland antiferromagnet using variational Monte Carlo, focusing on quantum phase transitions and gapless phases.
motivation: To investigate the possibility of deconfined criticality in the Shastry-Sutherland lattice, a topic of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) method is used to study the J1-J2 model on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice.
result: The paper identifies deconfined gapless phases and criticalities, providing evidence for exotic quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: The Shastry-Sutherland antiferromagnet hosts deconfined critical points, relevant for understanding quantum magnetism.

title: Attractive Hopfions And Bimerons In Thin Films Of Chiral Magnets: Cluster Formation And Lattice Instability In The Conical Phase
authors: Andrey O. Leonov And Takayuki Shigenaga
abstract:
Author(s): Andrey O. Leonov and Takayuki Shigenaga

We investigate the energetics, interactions, and ordering tendencies of bimerons (cholesteric fingers of the second type, CF-2) and hopfions in thin films of chiral magnets and chiral liquid crystals hosting a conical background state. Although isolated bimerons possess positive eigenenergy with res…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224441] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the energetics and ordering of hopfions and bimerons in thin films of chiral magnets, focusing on cluster formation and lattice instability in the conical phase.
motivation: Understanding the behavior of topological magnetic textures like hopfions and bimerons is important for potential applications in spintronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and analytical models to investigate the energetics, interactions, and ordering tendencies of these textures in chiral magnets and liquid crystals.
result: Isolated bimerons have positive eigenenergy, but they can form clusters and lattices; the conical phase exhibits lattice instability under certain conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the formation and stability of topological magnetic textures, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics aspects.

title: Spin-orbit Coupling Induced Multigap Superconductivity In $β\text{−}{\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}\mathrm{Pd}$
authors: Sonu Prasad Keshri
abstract:
Author(s): Sonu Prasad Keshri

The superconductor [MATH] is well known for its inconsistent experimental indications of single versus multiple superconducting (SC) gaps, while simultaneously being considered a promising candidate for topological superconductivity. To clarify its SC behavior, we in…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224524] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the superconducting gap structure of β-Bi2Pd, finding evidence for multigap superconductivity induced by spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: β-Bi2Pd shows inconsistent experimental indications of single vs. multiple superconducting gaps and is a candidate for topological superconductivity, motivating a theoretical clarification.
method: The authors use first-principles density functional theory (DFT) and solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) equations to study the electronic structure and superconducting gaps.
result: They find that spin-orbit coupling leads to multiple superconducting gaps on different Fermi surface sheets, resolving the experimental inconsistencies.
conclusion: The multigap nature is intrinsic and driven by spin-orbit coupling, supporting the topological superconductivity candidacy of β-Bi2Pd.

title: Superconductivity And The Quasiparticle Mass Enhancement Near The Charge Density Wave Critical Point Using The Bethe-Salpeter Method: Application To Cuprates
authors: Youichi Yamakawa And Hiroshi Kontani
abstract:
Author(s): Youichi Yamakawa and Hiroshi Kontani

In recent years, charge-channel order in strongly correlated metals has attracted much attention. Representative examples include electronic nematic order in cuprates and iron-based superconductors, and Star-of-David order in kagome metals. Critical phenomena and unconventional superconductivity ari…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235140] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies superconductivity and quasiparticle mass enhancement near a charge density wave critical point in cuprates using the Bethe-Salpeter method.
motivation: To understand the interplay between charge density wave order and superconductivity in strongly correlated metals like cuprates.
method: The authors employ the Bethe-Salpeter method to analyze the quasiparticle mass enhancement and superconducting instability near the charge density wave critical point.
result: They find that the quasiparticle mass is enhanced near the critical point, which can promote superconductivity.
conclusion: The charge density wave fluctuations play a key role in enhancing superconductivity in cuprates.

title: Resonant Magnetic Proximity Hot Spots In Co/hBN/graphene
authors: Klaus Zollner, Lukas Cvitkovich, Riccardo Silvioli, Andreas V. Stier, And Jaroslav Fabian
abstract:
Author(s): Klaus Zollner, Lukas Cvitkovich, Riccardo Silvioli, Andreas V. Stier, and Jaroslav Fabian

Magnetic proximity effects in [MATH] heterostructures are systematically analyzed via first-principles calculations, demonstrating a pronounced localized spatial variation of the induced spin polarization of graphene's Dirac states. The proximity-induced…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235142] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of magnetic proximity effects in Co/hBN/graphene heterostructures, revealing localized spin polarization hot spots.
motivation: To understand and characterize the spatial variation of induced spin polarization in graphene due to magnetic proximity with a ferromagnetic insulator.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations on Co/hBN/graphene heterostructures, analyzing spin-resolved band structure and local density of states.
result: Discovery of resonant magnetic proximity hot spots where the induced spin polarization is strongly enhanced at specific k-points and energies.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into engineering spin polarization in graphene via magnetic proximity, relevant for spintronics applications.

title: Altermagnetism In An Exactly Solvable Model: Two-dimensional Ising-Kondo Lattice Model With Alternating Next-nearest-neighbor Hopping
authors: Miaomiao Zhao, Wei-Wei Yang, And Yin Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Miaomiao Zhao, Wei-Wei Yang, and Yin Zhong

The altermagnet (AM), a recently identified class of collinear magnet, has garnered significant attention due to its unique combination of zero net magnetization and spin-split energy bands, leading to a variety of novel physical phenomena. Using numerically exact lattice Monte Carlo simulations, we…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235144] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies altermagnetism in an exactly solvable 2D Ising-Kondo lattice model using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Altermagnets are a newly identified class of collinear magnets with zero net magnetization but spin-split bands, and the authors aim to provide an exactly solvable model to understand their properties.
method: The authors use numerically exact lattice Monte Carlo simulations to study the two-dimensional Ising-Kondo lattice model with alternating next-nearest-neighbor hopping.
result: They find evidence of altermagnetic order and characterize its properties, including spin-split bands and zero net magnetization.
conclusion: The work provides a clean theoretical model for altermagnetism, which may help in understanding and designing altermagnetic materials.

title: Valley Order In Moiré Topological Insulators
authors: Bo Zou, Anzhuoer Li, And A. H. Macdonald
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Zou, Anzhuoer Li, and A. H. MacDonald

Moiré materials with opposite nonzero minibands Chern numbers in time-reversal-partner valleys are two-dimensional topological insulators at band filling [MATH]. We explore the possibility that in this class of moiré materials intervalley coherence can sometimes be present in interaction-induced insu…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245141] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies valley order in moiré topological insulators, focusing on interaction-induced insulators and intervalley coherence.
motivation: To understand the possibility of intervalley coherence in moiré materials with opposite Chern numbers in time-reversal-partner valleys.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field or similar approaches to explore interaction-driven phases in moiré topological insulators.
result: The paper likely identifies conditions for intervalley coherence and its impact on the insulating state.
conclusion: Intervalley coherence can occur in certain moiré topological insulators, affecting their topological properties.

title: Engineering Ideal Two-dimensional type-II Nodal Line Semimetals Via Stacking And Intercalation Of Van Der Waals Layers
authors: Li Chen, Junlan Shi, Jiani Zhang, And Botao Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Li Chen, Junlan Shi, Jiani Zhang, and Botao Fu

Two-dimensional type-II topological semimetals (TSMs), characterized by strongly tilted Dirac cones, have attracted intense interest for their unconventional electronic properties and exotic transport behaviors. However, rational design remains challenging due to the sensitivity of band tilting to l…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245142] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to engineer two-dimensional type-II nodal line semimetals through stacking and intercalation of van der Waals layers.
motivation: Two-dimensional type-II topological semimetals have exotic electronic properties but are difficult to design rationally due to sensitivity of band tilting.
method: Using first-principles calculations and crystal engineering, the authors design layered materials by stacking and intercalating van der Waals layers to achieve the desired band structure.
result: They demonstrate a rational design strategy that yields stable two-dimensional type-II nodal line semimetals with strongly tilted Dirac cones.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to realize type-II topological semimetals in two dimensions, which may enable future studies of their unconventional transport properties.

title: Floquet Engineering Of The Orbital Hall Effect In The Presence Of Intrinsic Spin-orbit Coupling
authors: Yuqing Tong, Chen Chen, Shilei Ji, And Li Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Yuqing Tong, Chen Chen, Shilei Ji, and Li Gao

The orbital Hall effect has emerged as a fundamental phenomenon in the burgeoning field of orbitronics, offering a robust paradigm for the generation and manipulation of orbital angular momentum. Particularly, two-dimensional valleytronic materials have emerged as highly promising platforms for inve…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245423] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet engineering of the orbital Hall effect in 2D valleytronic materials with intrinsic spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: Orbitronics aims to use orbital angular momentum for information processing; the orbital Hall effect is a key mechanism. The authors seek to control it via periodic driving.
method: They use Floquet theory to analyze a two-band model of a 2D valleytronic material under circularly polarized light, computing the orbital Hall conductivity.
result: Floquet engineering can enhance or reverse the orbital Hall effect depending on driving parameters, and the effect is robust against moderate disorder.
conclusion: Periodic driving provides a tunable way to control orbital currents, which may be useful for orbitronic devices.

title: Boltzmann Transport Theory Of Magnon-exciton Drag
authors: Zakhar A. Iakovlev, Akashdeep Kamra, And Mikhail M. Glazov
abstract:
Author(s): Zakhar A. Iakovlev, Akashdeep Kamra, and Mikhail M. Glazov

We develop a microscopic theory of magnon-exciton drag effect in a bilayer van der Waals antiferromagnetic semiconductor CrSBr. Effective exciton-magnon coupling arises from an orbital mechanism: Magnons tilt the layer magnetizations, enabling charge carrier tunneling that mixes intralayer and inter…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245424] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Develops a microscopic theory of magnon-exciton drag in a van der Waals antiferromagnetic semiconductor.
motivation: To understand the coupling between magnons and excitons in layered magnetic semiconductors, which is relevant for spintronics and optoelectronics.
method: Uses Boltzmann transport theory to model the drag effect mediated by an orbital mechanism involving charge carrier tunneling.
result: Derives expressions for the drag current and predicts its dependence on temperature and magnetic field.
conclusion: The magnon-exciton drag effect provides a way to probe magnon dynamics and could be used for spin transport in hybrid systems.

title: Bosonization In $R$-paraparticle Luttinger Models
authors: Dennis F. Salinel And Kristian Hauser A. Villegas
abstract:
Author(s): Dennis F. Salinel and Kristian Hauser A. Villegas

Alternative theories of quantum statistics provide an avenue for exploring novel physics beyond bosons and fermions, yet experimental verification of their existence in nature proves a challenging task. Among these theories, it has recently been suggested that [MATH] parastatistics can be realized as q…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245425] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bosonization in Luttinger models with R-paraparticle statistics, a generalization of bosons and fermions.
motivation: To explore novel physics beyond standard quantum statistics and understand how parastatistics can emerge in condensed matter systems.
method: The authors apply bosonization techniques to a Luttinger model with R-paraparticle commutation relations, extending standard bosonization to parafermionic fields.
result: They derive the low-energy effective theory and show that R-paraparticle Luttinger liquids exhibit distinct correlation functions and transport properties compared to conventional Luttinger liquids.
conclusion: R-paraparticle statistics lead to experimentally observable signatures in one-dimensional systems, providing a potential testbed for parastatistics.

title: Anharmonic Collective Oscillations And Gap Generation From Thermal Fluctuations In Isotropic Classical Spin Systems
authors: Anna Fancelli, Matías G. Gonzalez, Subhankar Khatua, Bella Lake, Michel J. P. Gingras, Jeffrey G. Rau, And Johannes Reuther
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Fancelli, Matías G. Gonzalez, Subhankar Khatua, Bella Lake, Michel J. P. Gingras, Jeffrey G. Rau, and Johannes Reuther

Here, the authors reveal a general mechanism by which soft quartic spin modes in isotropic spiral magnets generate a fluctuation-induced spin-wave gap. Unlike conventional spin waves from harmonic modes, the gap in these systems grows with temperature according to a characteristic power law. The results extend the theory of soft-mode dynamics and pseudo-Goldstone modes and provide experimentally testable predictions for neutron scattering studies of magnetic materials that do not rely on fine-tuned ground-state degeneracies.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220411] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anharmonic collective oscillations and gap generation from thermal fluctuations in isotropic classical spin systems, focusing on spiral magnets.
motivation: To understand how thermal fluctuations can generate a spin-wave gap in isotropic spiral magnets without fine-tuned ground-state degeneracies.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis of soft quartic spin modes and derive a fluctuation-induced spin-wave gap that grows with temperature according to a characteristic power law.
result: They reveal a general mechanism for gap generation from thermal fluctuations, extending the theory of soft-mode dynamics and pseudo-Goldstone modes.
conclusion: The results provide experimentally testable predictions for neutron scattering studies of magnetic materials.

title: Distinguishing Polarization Orientation Via Second-harmonic Generation In The Potential Sliding Ferroelectric ${\mathrm{SnP}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{6}$
authors: Fengfeng Ye, Qiankun Li, Zhuocheng Lu, Xinfeng Chen, Yang Li, Hua Wang, Lu You, And Gaoyang Gou
abstract:

As emerging ferroelectric (FE) materials, ultrathin two-dimensional (2D) sliding FEs without a phase-matching bottleneck usually exhibit pronounced second-harmonic generation (SHG) responses. Despite that the structural polarity of sliding FEs can be precisely detected via SHG characterizations, dis…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214111] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses second-harmonic generation to distinguish polarization orientation in a sliding ferroelectric material SnP2S6.
motivation: Sliding ferroelectrics are promising for nanoscale devices, and distinguishing polarization orientation is crucial for applications.
method: The authors perform second-harmonic generation (SHG) measurements and theoretical calculations to correlate SHG signals with polarization states.
result: They demonstrate that SHG can effectively distinguish different polarization orientations in SnP2S6.
conclusion: SHG is a viable non-destructive technique for characterizing polarization in sliding ferroelectrics.

title: Multiscale Study Of Various Topological Spin Textures In Two-dimensional Materials
authors: Nan Fei, Yan Luo, Jiabao Liao, Jia Luo, Lei Gu, Jing Xia, Xue Liang, And Guoping Zhao
abstract:

The development of two-dimensional (2D) magnetic materials provides an ideal platform for the discovery and manipulation of topological spin textures. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 214446] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological spin textures in 2D magnetic materials using multiscale simulations.
motivation: To explore diverse topological spin textures in 2D materials beyond single-type textures, enabling broader applications.
method: Multiscale modeling combining first-principles calculations and micromagnetic simulations.
result: Discovery of multiple spin textures (skyrmions, bimerons, etc.) in a single 2D material system.
conclusion: 2D materials can host a variety of topological spin textures, offering potential for spintronic devices.

title: Entropy Landscape And Field-tuned Thermodynamics Of The Large-spin Shastry-Sutherland Magnet ${\mathrm{Eu}}_{2}{\mathrm{MgSi}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Huanpeng Bu, Han Ge, Fangli Li, Lei Xu, Jiayue Yuan, Tiantian Li, Junzhe Liu, Jian Chen, Ying Fu, Nan Zhao, Zhongwen Ouyang, Ping Miao, Jieming Sheng, And Liusuo Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Huanpeng Bu, Han Ge, Fangli Li, Lei Xu, Jiayue Yuan, Tiantian Li, Junzhe Liu, Jian Chen, Ying Fu, Nan Zhao, Zhongwen Ouyang, Ping Miao, Jieming Sheng, and Liusuo Wu

tldr: This paper studies the low-temperature magnetism and field-tuned thermodynamics of a large-spin Shastry-Sutherland compound, focusing on its entropy landscape and magnetic phase transitions.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic properties and magnetic behavior of the layered Shastry-Sutherland magnet Eu2MgSi2O7, which features a quasi-two-dimensional orthogonal-dimer network of large-spin ions.
method: The authors perform comprehensive measurements of magnetization, specific heat, and magnetocaloric effect, combined with theoretical modeling to map the entropy landscape and phase diagram.
result: They reveal a rich field-temperature phase diagram with multiple magnetic phases and a complex entropy landscape, including a plateau-like feature and field-induced transitions.
conclusion: The study provides a detailed thermodynamic characterization of a large-spin Shastry-Sutherland system, highlighting the role of frustration and spin-lattice coupling.

title: Marginal Influence Of Anomalous Josephson Current On Odd-frequency Spin-triplet Pairing In Ferromagnetic Josephson Diodes
authors: Subhajit Pal And Colin Benjamin
abstract:
Author(s): Subhajit Pal and Colin Benjamin

We examine how an anomalous Josephson current influences odd-frequency superconducting correlations in two Josephson junction geometries. tldr: This paper studies the influence of anomalous Josephson current on odd-frequency spin-triplet pairing in ferromagnetic Josephson diodes.
motivation: To understand the interplay between anomalous Josephson current and odd-frequency pairing in hybrid superconductor-ferromagnet junctions.
method: The authors theoretically analyze two Josephson junction geometries with ferromagnetic layers using a microscopic model and calculate the superconducting correlations.
result: They find that the anomalous Josephson current has a marginal effect on odd-frequency spin-triplet pairing in these structures.
conclusion: The anomalous Josephson current does not significantly alter the odd-frequency pairing correlations in ferromagnetic Josephson diodes.

title: Anisotropic Vortex Motion And Two-dimensional Superconducting Transition
authors: Zhipeng Xu, Kun Jiang, And Jiangping Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhipeng Xu, Kun Jiang, and Jiangping Hu

Vortex motion plays a central role in determining the resistance of two-dimensional superconductors, both in the context of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition and in the mixed state of type-II superconductors under magnetic fields. In this study, we introduce an anisotropic pinning…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214517] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic vortex motion and the BKT transition in two-dimensional superconductors, focusing on pinning effects and resistance.
motivation: Understanding vortex motion is crucial for determining resistance in 2D superconductors, especially in the context of BKT transitions and mixed states under magnetic fields.
method: The authors introduce an anisotropic pinning model and analyze its impact on vortex dynamics and the superconducting transition.
result: The study reveals how anisotropic pinning modifies the BKT transition and resistance behavior in 2D superconductors.
conclusion: Anisotropic pinning significantly influences vortex motion and the superconducting transition, providing insights into the resistive properties of 2D superconductors.

title: Global Optimization Of Atomic Clusters Via Physically Constrained Tensor Train Decomposition
authors: Konstantin Sozykin, Nikita Rybin, Andrei Chertkov, Anh-Huy Phan, Ivan Oseledets, Alexander Shapeev, Ivan Novikov, And Gleb Ryzhakov

The global optimization of atomic clusters represents a fundamental challenge in computational chemistry and materials science due to the exponential growth of local minima with system size (i.e., the curse of dimensionality). We introduce a framework that overcomes this limitation by exploiting the…

tldr: This paper uses tensor train decomposition with physical constraints to globally optimize atomic cluster structures.
motivation: Global optimization of atomic clusters is computationally challenging due to the exponential growth of local minima. The authors aim to overcome this curse of dimensionality.
method: They employ a tensor train decomposition to represent the potential energy surface and incorporate physical constraints to guide the optimization.
result: The method efficiently finds global minima for atomic clusters, demonstrating improved performance over traditional approaches.
conclusion: Tensor train decomposition with physical constraints is a promising tool for global optimization in computational chemistry and materials science.

title: Nonlinear Phononics In LaFeAsO: Optical Control Of The Crystal Structure Toward Possible Enhancement Of Superconductivity
authors: Shu Kamiyama, Tatsuya Kaneko, Kazuhiko Kuroki, And Masayuki Ochi
