Nonlinear phononics provides a route to control crystal structures through light-induced phonon excitation. In this study, we apply nonlinear phononics to an iron-based superconductor, LaFeAsO, with the aim of tuning its crystal structure toward the ideal one to enhance superconductivity. We simulat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224315] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses nonlinear phononics to optically control the crystal structure of LaFeAsO to enhance superconductivity.
motivation: To tune the crystal structure of an iron-based superconductor toward an ideal configuration that may enhance superconductivity.
method: Simulations of nonlinear phononics in LaFeAsO, modeling light-induced phonon excitation and resulting structural changes.
result: The simulations show that specific light excitations can modify the crystal structure, potentially improving superconducting properties.
conclusion: Nonlinear phononics offers a promising route to optically control superconductivity in iron-based superconductors.

title: Steady-state Equilibrium And Nonequilibrium Noisy Network Dynamics
authors: Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

The fluctuating dynamics of a network about its stable, noise-free steady state are theoretically investigated. Various causes of nonequilibrium dynamics are identified in terms of the properties and symmetry of the network connections and the noise covariance matrices. Several equivalent conditions…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064148] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies steady-state fluctuations in noisy networks, focusing on equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics from a classical stochastic perspective.
motivation: To understand how network connectivity and noise properties drive nonequilibrium dynamics in complex systems.
method: Theoretical analysis using Langevin equations and covariance matrices to characterize fluctuations around stable steady states.
result: Identifies conditions for equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics based on network symmetry and noise correlations.
conclusion: The framework provides a general classification of network dynamics but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Search With Space-dependent Diffusivity
authors: Hwai-Ray Tung And Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Hwai-Ray Tung and Sean D. Lawley

The canonical model of stochastic search tracks a randomly diffusing “searcher” until it finds a “target.” Owing to its many applications across science and engineering, this perennially popular problem has been thoroughly investigated in a variety of models. However, aside from some exactly solvabl…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064149] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic search with space-dependent diffusivity, a problem in statistical physics and applied mathematics.
motivation: Stochastic search models are widely used in science and engineering, but space-dependent diffusivity introduces complexity that is not fully understood.
method: The authors develop analytical and numerical methods to compute first-passage time statistics for a diffusing searcher with spatially varying diffusion coefficient.
result: They derive exact results for certain diffusivity profiles and characterize how space-dependent diffusivity affects search efficiency.
conclusion: Space-dependent diffusivity can significantly alter search times, with implications for biological and technological search processes.

title: Nonreciprocal Blume-Capel Model With Antisymmetric Single-ion Anisotropies
authors: Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, And A. V. Anil Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, and A. V. Anil Kumar

We investigate the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model. Combining a systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions, we map the model's dynamical…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064140] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model with antisymmetric single-ion anisotropies using mean-field analysis and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species spin model.
method: Combines systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions.
result: Maps the model's dynamical phase diagram and identifies nonreciprocal effects.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal interactions lead to novel dynamical phases not present in the equilibrium Blume-Capel model.

title: Collective Coordinate Descriptions Of A Kink In A Driven-damped ${ϕ}^{4}$ Model
authors: Jacek Gatlik, Tomasz Dobrowolski, Jean-Guy Caputo, And Panayotis G. Kevrekidis
abstract:

Extending a recent effective theory formulation for the dynamics of kinks in the sine-Gordon model [T. Dobrowolski et al.,
tldr: This paper develops effective collective coordinate models for kink dynamics in a driven-damped φ^4 model, extending previous work on sine-Gordon kinks.
motivation: To provide a reduced description of kink motion in the φ^4 model under driving and damping, which is important for understanding nonlinear wave propagation in classical field theories.
method: The authors propose three reduced models based on collective coordinates (position, width, internal mode) and compare their predictions with full numerical simulations of the partial differential equation.
result: The reduced models capture key features of kink dynamics, including resonance phenomena and energy transfer, with varying accuracy depending on the driving and damping parameters.
conclusion: The collective coordinate approach is effective for modeling kink dynamics in the φ^4 model, offering a computationally efficient alternative to full simulations.

title: Relationship Between Heider Links And Ising Spins
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Maciej Wołoszyn, Krzysztof Malarz, And Krzysztof Kułakowski
abstract:

tldr: The paper establishes an equivalence between the Heider model of social balance and the Ising model, showing that structurally balanced Heider triads correspond to Ising ground states.
motivation: To connect sociological balance theory (Heider) to statistical physics (Ising model), potentially allowing insights from one field to inform the other.
method: The authors analyze the Heider model with an external field and show that in the limit of structural balance, it reduces to the Ising model with nearest-neighbor interactions and no external field.
result: The signs of Heider relations that maintain structural equilibrium are equivalent to Ising spin configurations at zero temperature.
conclusion: The Heider model and Ising model are mathematically equivalent under the condition of structural balance, bridging social dynamics and condensed matter physics.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, and Deok-Sun Lee

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth-gradient transitions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation despite defection being individually beneficial.
method: A game-theoretic model on a lattice where interaction payoffs are scaled by minimum wealth, analyzed via simulations and analytical methods.
result: A discontinuous wealth-gradient transition drives cooperation.
conclusion: Wealth inequality can promote cooperation under certain conditions.

title: Universality And Ambiguity In Extremes Of Anomalous Diffusion
authors: Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Sean D. Lawley

Many biophysical processes begin when the fastest searcher finds a target out of many random searchers, which is called an extreme or fastest first passage time (fFPT). In some models (i) the fFPT vanishes logarithmically as the number of searchers grows and (ii) the fFPT can be faster for subdiffus…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064135] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the extreme first passage time for anomalous diffusion processes, showing universal logarithmic scaling and ambiguity in the definition of subdiffusion.
motivation: Many biophysical processes depend on the fastest searcher among many, but the behavior of extreme first passage times for anomalous diffusion was not well understood.
method: The author derives asymptotic formulas for the fastest first passage time in models of subdiffusion and superdiffusion, analyzing the dependence on the number of searchers.
result: The fastest first passage time vanishes logarithmically with the number of searchers for a wide class of anomalous diffusion processes, but the scaling depends on the definition of subdiffusion.
conclusion: The results highlight universal features and ambiguities in extreme statistics of anomalous diffusion, relevant to biophysical search processes.

title: Angular Anisotropy Landscape Of Vortex Ensembles In Polarized Small-angle Neutron Scattering
authors: Michael P. Adams, Elizabeth M. Jefremovas, And Andreas Michels
abstract:

We present a symmetry-resolved classification of two-dimensional spin-flip small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) patterns arising from dilute ensembles of spherical nanoparticles hosting magnetic vortex states. Based on a linear vortex ansatz with an axially symmetric distribution of vortex axes and…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023328] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper classifies spin-flip small-angle neutron scattering patterns from magnetic vortex ensembles in spherical nanoparticles.
motivation: To understand the angular anisotropy of magnetic vortex structures in nanoparticle assemblies, which is relevant to condensed matter physics and materials science.
method: The authors use a linear vortex ansatz with axially symmetric vortex axis distribution and compute symmetry-resolved SANS patterns.
result: They provide a classification of two-dimensional spin-flip SANS patterns based on the symmetry of the vortex ensemble.
conclusion: The work offers a theoretical framework for interpreting SANS experiments on magnetic vortex systems, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: One-particle Density Matrix Framework For Mode-shell Correspondence: Characterizing Topology In Amorphous Higher-order Topological Insulators
authors: Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, And Julia D. Hannukainen
abstract:
Author(s): Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, and Julia D. Hannukainen

We present a framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases directly from the one-particle density matrix, without any reference to an underlying Hamiltonian. Our approach extends the mode-shell correspondence, originally formulated for single-particle Hamiltonians, to Gaussian states …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases in amorphous systems using the one-particle density matrix.
motivation: To extend topological characterization to amorphous materials where traditional band-structure methods fail.
method: Extends the mode-shell correspondence to Gaussian states via the one-particle density matrix, without requiring a Hamiltonian.
result: Demonstrates that higher-order topological invariants can be computed from the density matrix, applicable to amorphous higher-order topological insulators.
conclusion: Provides a general method to identify topological phases in disordered systems, broadening the scope of topological classification.

title: Ligand-mediated Magnetic Coupling Across Metamagnetic Transitions In ${\mathrm{CrPS}}_{4}$
authors: Giuseppe Buccoliero, Rachel Nickel, Roberto Sant, Marli Dos Reis Cantarino, Andrei Rogalev, Nathan J. Yutronkie, Tristan Riccardi, Daniel A. Chaney, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, And Nicholas B. Brookes
abstract:
Author(s): Giuseppe Buccoliero, Rachel Nickel, Roberto Sant, Marli dos Reis Cantarino, Andrei Rogalev, Nathan J. Yutronkie, Tristan Riccardi, Daniel A. Chaney, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, and Nicholas B. Brookes

Chromium thiophosphate ([MATH]) is a long-known material: A layered semiconducting antiferromagnet. Its recently discovered gate-tunable metamagnetic phase transitions, the remarkable positive and oscillating magnetoresistance as a tunnel barrier, and its Fano-resonance luminescence, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates ligand-mediated magnetic coupling and metamagnetic transitions in CrPS4 using X-ray absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory.
motivation: To understand the microscopic origin of metamagnetic transitions and magnetic coupling in CrPS4, a layered antiferromagnet with potential for spintronic applications.
method: Combined X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) experiments with first-principles DFT calculations.
result: Identified that magnetic coupling is mediated by sulfur ligands and that the metamagnetic transition involves a change in the Cr-S-Cr bond angle, altering the superexchange interaction.
conclusion: The study provides a detailed microscopic picture of the metamagnetic transition in CrPS4, highlighting the role of ligand-mediated exchange.

title: Excited Eigenstates From A Two-species Random Walk
authors: Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, And Alexandre Melanson
abstract:
Author(s): Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, and Alexandre Melanson

Macroscopically, the population density function of random walk models can satisfy self-contained dynamics and exhibit unexpected order. Here, we show how a two-species random walk model that includes diffusion, probabilistic absorption of walkers mediated by a potential function, cross-species anni…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023324] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A two-species random walk model with diffusion, absorption, and cross-species annihilation is studied, showing emergent order in population density.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic order can arise from microscopic random walk dynamics with multiple species.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a two-species random walk model including diffusion, potential-mediated absorption, and cross-species annihilation.
result: The population density function satisfies self-contained dynamics and exhibits unexpected order.
conclusion: The model demonstrates that complex interactions in random walks can lead to emergent macroscopic behavior.

title: Theory Of High-harmonic Generation With Quantum Light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, And Jianmin Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, and Jianmin Yuan

High-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by intense quantum light has recently emerged as a new frontier in strong-field physics. Yet, the mechanism underlying HHG with nonclassical fields such as bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) light—characterized by a vanishing mean electric field—remains elusive. In th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023326] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of high-harmonic generation driven by quantum light, specifically bright squeezed vacuum, revealing a new mechanism distinct from classical HHG.
motivation: High-harmonic generation with nonclassical light (e.g., bright squeezed vacuum) is a new frontier, but the underlying mechanism is not understood because the mean electric field vanishes.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework combining quantum optics and strong-field physics, likely using a time-dependent Schrödinger equation or quantum trajectory approach to model HHG with squeezed vacuum.
result: They identify a mechanism where quantum fluctuations of the field drive HHG, leading to distinct spectral features compared to classical HHG.
conclusion: Quantum light enables a new regime of HHG with unique properties, opening avenues for attosecond science and quantum optics.

title: Before The Cycle Is Over: Subcycle Time Refraction At Optical Frequencies
authors: Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, And Mordechai Segev
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, and Mordechai Segev

This work demonstrates subcycle order-unity variations in the refractive index at optical frequencies and measures the time-refraction of a probe wave propagating in the modulated medium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022054] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates subcycle time refraction at optical frequencies by modulating refractive index on ultrafast timescales.
motivation: To achieve and measure order-unity refractive index changes within an optical cycle, enabling new regimes of light-matter interaction.
method: Experimental setup using ultrafast optical modulation to induce subcycle refractive index variations and probe wave time-refraction.
result: Observation of subcycle time refraction with order-unity index changes at optical frequencies.
conclusion: Subcycle refractive index modulation is feasible and can be measured, opening possibilities for ultrafast optical control.

title: Formation Of Bosonic $^{23}\mathrm{Na}^{41}\mathrm{K}$ Feshbach Molecules
authors: Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, And Jee Woo Park
abstract:
Author(s): Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, and Jee Woo Park

Ultracold Feshbach molecules are a crucial intermediate step for the creation of quantum degenerate gases of strongly dipolar molecules. After coherent transfer to the rovibrational ground state, these dimers can realize stable dipolar gases with strong, tunable long-range interactions. Here, we rep…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023307] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the formation of ultracold 23Na41K Feshbach molecules, a step toward creating quantum degenerate dipolar gases.
motivation: Ultracold Feshbach molecules are essential for producing strongly dipolar quantum gases with tunable long-range interactions, enabling studies of novel quantum phases.
method: The authors use magnetoassociation across a Feshbach resonance in a mixture of 23Na and 41K atoms, followed by coherent transfer to the rovibrational ground state.
result: They successfully create Feshbach molecules and characterize their properties, demonstrating a pathway to ground-state molecules.
conclusion: This work provides a crucial intermediate step for realizing quantum degenerate gases of dipolar molecules, with implications for quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
Author(s): Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, and Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda

We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports antiferromagnetic resonance measurements in the topological insulator EuSn2As2, observing surface ferromagnons in the axion-insulating phase.
motivation: To study spin dynamics and surface magnetic excitations in a topological insulator with antiferromagnetic order, which is relevant for understanding axion electrodynamics in condensed matter.
method: Electron spin resonance (ESR) at 9.34 GHz was used to measure antiferromagnetic resonance modes below the Néel temperature.
result: Two resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and a surface ferromagnon mode, indicating surface magnetic order.
conclusion: The observation of surface ferromagnons provides evidence for the axion-insulating phase and highlights the role of surface magnetism in topological insulators.

title: Most Probable Path And Invariant Sets In Noise-induced Transition To Turbulence
authors: Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, and Kenta Ishimoto

Turbulence transition often arises from a subcritical transition between bistable states characterized by invariant sets of deterministic dynamical systems, and such transitions can be triggered by system noise as rare events. In this study, we employ the Onsager-Machlup (OM) formulation of stochast…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023303] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noise-induced transitions to turbulence using the Onsager-Machlup formulation to find most probable paths and invariant sets.
motivation: Understanding turbulence transition from bistable states triggered by noise is a fundamental problem in fluid dynamics.
method: The authors apply the Onsager-Machlup functional to stochastic dynamical systems to compute most probable transition paths and identify invariant sets.
result: They characterize the most probable paths and invariant sets associated with the subcritical transition to turbulence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into noise-induced transitions in turbulent flows, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Manifold-based Transformation Of Probability Distributions: Application To The Inverse Problem Of Reconstructing Distributions From Experimental Data
authors: Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, And Masaaki Sugiyama
abstract:
Author(s): Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, and Masaaki Sugiyama

Information geometry is a mathematical framework that elucidates the manifold structure of the probability distribution space (p space), providing a systematic approach to transforming probability distributions (PDs). In this study, we utilized information geometry to address the inverse problems as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023291] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses information geometry to transform probability distributions for solving inverse problems in experimental data reconstruction.
motivation: The authors aim to address the inverse problem of reconstructing probability distributions from experimental data, which is a common challenge in data analysis.
method: They apply information geometry, specifically the manifold structure of probability distribution spaces, to systematically transform distributions and solve the inverse problem.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the manifold-based transformation approach for reconstructing distributions from experimental data.
conclusion: Information geometry provides a powerful framework for inverse problems involving probability distributions, with potential applications in various experimental fields.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive.
method: Analytical effective nonlinear response theory combined with complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes.
result: An analytical threshold for dynamical phase transitions is derived and mapped across the two regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear resonators.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
authors: M. Sumetsky
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies inelastic transparency in time-modulated resonant photonic circuits, focusing on frequency conversion and power amplification.
motivation: To understand and exploit the effects of time modulation on light propagation in photonic circuits, particularly for frequency conversion and amplification.
method: Theoretical analysis using coupled-mode theory and transfer matrix methods for time-modulated resonant structures.
result: Demonstrates that under certain conditions, time-modulated photonic circuits can achieve complete inelastic transparency, converting input light to different frequencies without loss.
conclusion: Time-modulated resonant photonic circuits offer a new mechanism for frequency conversion and amplification, with potential applications in photonic signal processing.

title: General Spin Models From Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory And Spin-cluster Expansion
authors: Tomonori Tanaka And Yoshihiro Gohda
abstract:
Author(s): Tomonori Tanaka and Yoshihiro Gohda

We present a data-efficient framework for constructing general classical spin Hamiltonians by combining the spin-cluster expansion (SCE) with fully self-consistent noncollinear spin density functional theory (DFT). The key idea is to fit the SCE model to magnetic torques rather than to total energie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023300] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A data-efficient framework for constructing classical spin Hamiltonians from noncollinear spin DFT using spin-cluster expansion.
motivation: To enable accurate and efficient modeling of magnetic materials with general spin interactions beyond simple Heisenberg models.
method: Combines noncollinear spin DFT with spin-cluster expansion, fitting the model to magnetic torques instead of total energies.
result: Demonstrates that the torque-based fitting yields accurate spin Hamiltonians with fewer DFT calculations compared to energy-based methods.
conclusion: The proposed framework is a practical tool for deriving classical spin models from first principles, applicable to complex magnetic systems.

title: Current-induced Successive Structural Phase Transitions Beyond Thermal Equilibrium In Single-crystal ${\mathrm{VO}}_{2}$
authors: Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-Hisa Arima, And Ichiro Terasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-hisa Arima, and Ichiro Terasaki

Using synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy, current-induced structural phase transitions in single-crystal vanadium dioxide are investigated. Successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases are observed, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion inaccessible under thermal equilibrium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022050] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates current-induced structural phase transitions in VO2 single crystals, revealing nonequilibrium metallic phases not accessible under thermal equilibrium.
motivation: To understand how electric current can drive structural phase transitions beyond thermal equilibrium, potentially enabling new pathways to control material properties.
method: Combined synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy to characterize structural changes in VO2 single crystals under applied current.
result: Observation of successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion.
conclusion: Current can induce structural phase transitions that are inaccessible under thermal equilibrium, offering a new route to engineer material phases.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates quantum computational advantage by simulating driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a utilizable quantum computational advantage using a programmable ultracold-atom processor.
method: The processor simulates the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely using a Rydberg atom array or similar platform.
result: The experiment shows a quantum advantage in simulating the dynamics, outperforming classical simulations.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can achieve quantum computational advantage for simulating many-body physics.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and become detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to condensed matter physics.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is applied to chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and can be detected via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of quantum chiral solitons and their experimental signatures, advancing the understanding of topological excitations in spin chains.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs, analyzing spectra and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study 3D fermionic CFTs, revealing emergent symmetries.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: Spin moiré superstructures are of interest for manipulating information via spin textures, but a general theoretical framework for solving such structures is lacking.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering experiments with theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phases of EuAg4Sb2 under varying temperature and magnetic field.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are identified, including a spin moiré superstructure, and a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices is established.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures, which could enable new ways to manipulate information using spin textures.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: To understand the stability of topological magnon gaps near the Curie point for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail, which is relevant for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial but challenging; the paper aims to leverage physical principles to improve link prediction.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical constraints and dynamics to infer causal links from observational data.
result: The framework demonstrates improved accuracy in predicting physical links across various networked systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed approaches can enhance causal inference in networks, with potential applications in diverse fields.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers, a topological condensed matter phenomenon.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers driven by topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches.
result: Topological criticality enables anyonic exciton superfluidity with robust properties.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a platform for engineering anyonic superfluids, advancing topological quantum matter.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré systems.
method: Attractive polaron spectroscopy is employed as a probe to detect the quantum anomalous Hall state, with magneto-optical measurements under varying electric fields.
result: The experiments reveal a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and show that electric fields can switch between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism, relevant for future quantum devices.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in statistical physics and soft matter.
motivation: To understand the unusual behavior of hyperuniform fluids at the liquid-vapor critical point, where density fluctuations are suppressed yet susceptibility is high.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to characterize the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit suppressed density fluctuations but enhanced susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new class of critical behavior in hyperuniform fluids, with implications for understanding phase transitions in systems with constrained fluctuations.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, focusing on residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments reveal unexpected scattering that needs to be understood.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize the scattering behavior.
result: Residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and provide insights into wave transport in disordered media.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin valve behavior in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, a condensed matter physics experiment with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling spin-based devices.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene heterostructures to probe ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for spin-dependent electron optics, but the work is primarily a condensed matter transport study.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state may clarify their behavior.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical methods to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: A dipolar nematic state is identified and analyzed in relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: The nematic ordering is key to relaxor behavior, but the work is purely condensed matter physics.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
motivation: To understand the nature of long-lived hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems, which may have implications for novel electronic phases.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation combined with resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe excitations in the equilibrium and hidden phases of Pr0.67Ca0.33MnO3.
result: The hidden phase exhibits unique polaronic and phononic excitations not present in equilibrium, indicating a distinct metastable state.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can induce hidden phases with different lattice and electronic properties, offering a route to control material properties optically.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: Increasing microscopic activity in a sparse active solid can counterintuitively reduce its macroscopic active response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how the density of active units affects the collective mechanical response in active solids.
method: Combined experiments with robotic metamaterials and theoretical modeling.
result: When active units are too sparse, increasing activity does not percolate and the solid's active response vanishes.
conclusion: More activity can lead to less macroscopic effect in unpercolated active solids.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to compute persistence diagrams efficiently.
result: They prove a provable exponential quantum speedup over classical algorithms for certain instances of the problem.
conclusion: The work suggests that quantum computers could enable practical applications in topological data analysis, though it remains theoretical.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap for bridging the gap between current quantum computing capabilities and real-world applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of the field's progress.
result: A five-stage framework detailing milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path for the quantum computing community to focus efforts on achieving practical quantum advantage.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial evaluation to a quantum circuit, including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on small knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and highlighting resource requirements for scaling.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and provides insights into the potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: To provide a systematic and experimentally feasible approach for generating complex multimode multi-photon quantum states.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose target states into a sequence of elementary operations, including photon catalysis and linear optics.
result: They show that any photonic state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a general and efficient recipe for photonic state preparation, advancing quantum optics experiments.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has seen rapid progress since 2016.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: Covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving and opening new directions for applications.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on wave-matter interactions and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles, with applications in trapping, sorting, and pulling.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental demonstrations of optical and acoustic radiation forces and torques.
result: It summarizes key mechanisms and applications, including trapping of atoms and nanoparticles, cell sorting, and pulling forces.
conclusion: The review highlights the rich physics and practical potential of radiation forces and torques across optics and acoustics.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new electronic states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses are a paradigmatic model for complex systems, and understanding their dynamics is important for many fields.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical developments, and large-scale numerical simulations.
result: It tracks progress in spin-glass dynamics and highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich area for future research, with implications for diverse physical systems.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic and topological properties.
result: Highlights key candidate materials and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new results.
conclusion: The review serves as a resource for researchers in quantum spin liquids, but is not directly aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central problem in neuroscience, and statistical physics offers powerful tools for analyzing such complex systems.
method: The paper reviews the use of maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze simultaneous recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations, demonstrating that abstract theoretical principles can achieve predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a quantitative bridge between neural data and theory, revealing emergent properties of neural networks.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a fundamental photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models used to describe internal conversion, including nonradiative decay mechanisms and computational approaches.
result: The review summarizes the current state of theoretical methods and identifies key challenges and opportunities for future research.
conclusion: The authors provide an outlook on how these theoretical models can be incorporated into studies relevant to photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering formation interactions and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including quantum tunneling and entanglement.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum depinning and superposition states.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmionics is an emerging field with open questions and potential for future quantum technologies.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models of spin-dependent exotic interactions mediated by hypothetical bosons and surveys experimental techniques used to search for such interactions.
result: The review summarizes the current status of experimental constraints on various spin-dependent exotic interactions and outlines future directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential connections to dark matter and dark energy, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum simulation.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions using atomic, photonic, and electronic platforms.
result: Summarizes progress in engineering exotic geometries and discusses potential for simulating topological phases and gravitational models.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a promising avenue for quantum simulation, but the paper is a broad review without deep technical contributions to the user's specific research directions.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, focusing on how active units align their orientation with their velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: To understand and unify the phenomenon of self-alignment in active systems, which can produce unique single-particle and collective dynamics not captured by standard alignment models.
method: The paper reviews existing theoretical models and experimental systems of self-alignment, presenting a unified mathematical framework and categorizing different types of self-alignment.
result: Self-alignment enables behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, with potential applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental mechanism in active matter that reshapes motion emergence, and its study opens new avenues for designing active materials and understanding biological systems.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects like decoherence and entanglement.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts to detect gravity-induced decoherence, collapse, and entanglement between massive particles.
result: Summarizes current state-of-the-art experiments and theoretical models for testing quantum gravity with massive quantum systems.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity effects, but further experimental and theoretical work is needed.

title: Critical Phenomenon Inside Asymptotically Flat Black Holes With Spontaneous Scalarization
authors: Li Li, Ze Sun, And Fu-Guo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Li Li, Ze Sun, and Fu-Guo Yang

We study the nonlinear interior dynamics of spontaneously scalarized black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with zero cosmological constant, revealing novel critical phenomena. We demonstrate that, for a wide range of scalar-electromagnetic couplings, scalarized black holes possess no smooth …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251402] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies critical phenomena inside spontaneously scalarized black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory.
motivation: To understand the nonlinear interior dynamics and critical behavior of scalarized black holes beyond the event horizon.
method: Numerical simulations of the Einstein-Maxwell-scalar field equations with zero cosmological constant, exploring a range of scalar-electromagnetic couplings.
result: Scalarized black holes exhibit novel critical phenomena inside the horizon, with no smooth interior solutions for certain couplings.
conclusion: The interior dynamics of scalarized black holes show rich critical behavior, which may have implications for the strong cosmic censorship conjecture.

title: Dynamical Spreading And Memory Retention Of Particle Suspensions Under Power Law Potential
authors: Ido Fanto, Yuval Rosenblum, Ori Harel, Matan Yah Ben Zion, And Naomi Oppenheimer
abstract:
Author(s): Ido Fanto, Yuval Rosenblum, Ori Harel, Matan Yah Ben Zion, and Naomi Oppenheimer

We study the overdamped dynamic spreading of a suspension of particles under a repulsive power law potential. We predict that the suspension spreads in a self-similar form, with its radius growing in time with a power independent of the dimension. We confirm this prediction experimentally using magn…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248202] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the overdamped dynamic spreading of particle suspensions under a repulsive power law potential, predicting and experimentally confirming self-similar spreading with a dimension-independent power law.
motivation: Understanding the spreading dynamics of particle suspensions is important for soft matter physics and industrial applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors derive a theoretical prediction for self-similar spreading under a power law potential and validate it with experiments using magnetic particles.
result: The suspension radius grows as a power law in time, with an exponent independent of spatial dimension, confirmed experimentally.
conclusion: The work provides a universal scaling law for spreading of repulsive particle suspensions, but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Resolution Of The Hyperfine Puzzle And Its Significance For Two-fermion Dirac Atoms
authors: Gordon Baym And Glennys R. Farrar
abstract:
Author(s): Gordon Baym and Glennys R. Farrar

If we could shrink the ground-state wave function of a hydrogen atom to a size [MATH], at fixed electron mass and charge, the singlet hyperfine attraction in a spin singlet state would scale as [MATH]—faster than the increase in kinetic energy—raising the question of why the hyperfine interaction …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062219] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper resolves a hyperfine puzzle in two-fermion Dirac atoms by analyzing the scaling of hyperfine attraction relative to kinetic energy.
motivation: To understand why the hyperfine interaction does not cause collapse in hydrogen-like atoms despite its rapid scaling with wavefunction compression.
method: The authors use relativistic Dirac theory and scaling arguments to analyze the hyperfine splitting in two-fermion systems.
result: They show that the hyperfine attraction scales faster than kinetic energy, but the puzzle is resolved by considering the finite size of the nucleus and relativistic effects.
conclusion: The hyperfine puzzle is resolved within standard quantum electrodynamics, with implications for precision spectroscopy and bound-state QED.

title: Ellipticity- And Wavelength-dependent Rydberg-state Excitation Induced By Strong Laser Fields
authors: Chun Kang, Yang Liu, Qi Chen, Hang Lv, And Haifeng Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun Kang, Yang Liu, Qi Chen, Hang Lv, and Haifeng Xu

We perform a joint experimental and theoretical study on Rydberg-state excitation (RSE) of argon in elliptically polarized strong laser fields with different wavelengths in the range of 800–1500 nm.
