method: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the equation of state and density profiles, benchmarked against analytical theories.
result: Quantifies the effects of confinement and finite range on the equation of state and density profiles, showing deviations from idealized models.

abstract:

Enhanced atomic vibrations have previously been observed near edges of two-dimensional materials with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM). Here this observation is accounted for by localized phonon edge modes by including correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022049] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses HR-TEM image simulations to show that enhanced atomic vibrations near edges of MoS2 are due to localized phonon edge modes.
motivation: Enhanced atomic vibrations observed near edges of 2D materials in HR-TEM lacked a clear explanation; the authors aimed to account for this by including correlated atom vibrations in simulations.
method: The authors performed HR-TEM image simulations that incorporate correlated atom vibrations to model phonon edge modes on molybdenum disulfide.
result: The simulations reproduced the enhanced vibrations, confirming that localized phonon edge modes are responsible.
conclusion: Phonon edge modes explain the observed enhanced atomic vibrations at edges of 2D materials, providing a deeper understanding of edge effects.

tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and training instabilities.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in neural networks can improve training stability and efficiency.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of recurrent networks, identifying ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks that cause abrupt learning.
result: The ghost mechanism is shown to underlie abrupt learning, and methods to overcome training instabilities are identified.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical framework for abrupt learning in recurrent networks, with implications for training dynamics.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper reviews the theoretical background of Wannier functions and describes the interoperable software ecosystem, including codes for maximally localized Wannier functions and their applications.
result: It highlights the widespread use of Wannier functions in computing topological invariants, Berry phases, and other material properties.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community, enabling accurate and insightful materials simulations.

tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of Bianchi I universe in loop quantum cosmology, finding that quantum effects suppress shear after the bounce, leading to isotropization.
motivation: To understand the isotropization mechanism in the early universe within the framework of loop quantum cosmology, addressing the shear problem in Bianchi I models.
method: The authors analyze the modified loop quantum cosmology (mLQC-I) model for Bianchi I universe, deriving the effective dynamics and studying the evolution of shear numerically.
result: They find that shear is dynamically suppressed after the bounce and decays rapidly in the quantum postbounce regime, independent of the equation of state.
conclusion: Loop quantum cosmology provides a robust mechanism for isotropization, which is a new prediction of the theory.

title: Predicting Instantaneous Friction From Friction Damping Coefficients In Underdamped Sliding
authors: Chengdong Sun, Yi Tao, Zaoqi Duan, Kai Chen, Quan Han, Yajing Kan, Zhonghua Ni, Zhiyong Wei, Yan Zhang, And Yunfei Chen

motivation: Friction accounts for nearly one-third of global energy consumption, and the coefficient of friction's dependence on sliding velocity limits its predictive power for instantaneous friction forces.
method: The authors develop a model that uses friction damping coefficients to predict instantaneous friction in underdamped sliding contacts.
result: The model provides a method to estimate instantaneous friction forces more accurately than traditional coefficient-based approaches.
conclusion: The proposed approach improves prediction of friction-induced energy dissipation, which could aid in designing more efficient mechanical systems.

title: Unsteady Phase Waves In The One-dimensional Swarmalator Model With Inertia
authors: Kevin O'keeffe
abstract:

We study a one-dimensional swarmalator model with inertia. Previous studies have focused almost exclusively on the overdamped limit. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064210] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a one-dimensional swarmalator model with inertia, discovering a new unsteady collective state called 'thrashing' phase waves.
motivation: Previous studies of swarmalators focused on the overdamped limit; this work introduces inertia to explore new collective dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional swarmalator model with inertia using analytical and numerical methods, examining the bifurcation of rainbow order parameters.
result: Inertia leads to multiharmonic oscillations in the rainbow order parameters, giving rise to a 'thrashing' phase wave state.
conclusion: Inertia fundamentally alters the collective behavior of swarmalators, producing unsteady dynamics not seen in the overdamped regime.

title: Fractional Degree Centrality For Directed Networks

When [MATH], the fractional centrality reduces to the out-degree centrality. …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064310] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a fractional version of degree centrality for directed networks using the fractional directed Laplacian.
motivation: Degree centrality is a fundamental measure in network analysis, but its fractional generalization may capture non-local influences in directed networks.

title: Emergence Of A Fluctuation-driven Cooperative Solidlike Phase In Potts Model Monolayers
authors: Alexander J. Devanny And Laura J. Kaufman

Cellular Potts model (CPM) simulations display significant variation in dynamics, structural ordering, and observed phase transitions. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064410] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in cellular Potts model monolayers, focusing on a fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase.
motivation: To understand the variability in dynamics and phase transitions observed in cellular Potts model simulations due to differences in implementation.
method: The authors perform cellular Potts model simulations with varying definitions of cell perimeter and area constraints, analyzing structural ordering and dynamics.
result: They identify a fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase that emerges under certain conditions, distinct from conventional solid phases.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of implementation details in CPM simulations and reveal a new type of phase behavior in monolayer systems.

title: Characterizing Emergent Multiscale Dynamics In Colloidal Nanoparticle Gels
authors: William D. Brackett, Zachary M. Sherman, Felix Lehmkühler, Thomas M. Truskett, And Delia J. Milliron
abstract:

Characterizing the dynamics of nanoparticle gel networks demands a spatiotemporal resolution that no single technique can provide. This Perspective describes the opportunities to address this challenge using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy at fourth-generation light sources combined with complementary experimental and simulation tools. This should move the field beyond descriptive fundamental studies toward mechanistic understanding and design of nanoparticle gels with adaptive and programmable behaviors.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 061001] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This perspective discusses using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy at fourth-generation light sources to study multiscale dynamics in colloidal nanoparticle gels.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of nanoparticle gel networks requires spatiotemporal resolution beyond any single technique, motivating a combined experimental and simulation approach.
method: The paper proposes using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy at advanced light sources, complemented by other experimental methods and simulations.
result: No new results are presented; it is a perspective outlining opportunities for future research.
conclusion: The field can move from descriptive studies to mechanistic understanding and design of adaptive nanoparticle gels.

authors: D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, And G. Franchetti

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: To summarize the scientific contributions of the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research over its 50-year operation.
method: The paper reviews incoherent scatter radar theory and presents key results from Arecibo's radar, lidar, and optical instruments in studies of plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
result: The review highlights advances in understanding ionospheric dynamics, metal layers, and coupling processes, enabled by Arecibo's unique capabilities.
conclusion: Arecibo's legacy includes foundational contributions to geospace science, but the paper does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium on multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and future detectors.
motivation: To discuss detection prospects for continuous gravitational waves and their implications for astrophysics and condensed matter physics.
method: Review of current and future gravitational-wave detectors and simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: Highlights the potential for multimessenger observations to probe dense environments of neutron stars.
conclusion: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier for multimessenger astronomy, with strong connections to other fields.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties provide crucial tests of nuclear physics under extreme conditions.
method: The paper reviews recent observational constraints from gravitational-wave signals (binary neutron star mergers) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to theoretical predictions of the nuclear equation of state.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and discusses how they inform the equation of state at and beyond nuclear densities.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of dense matter, but the paper does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, highlighting cases where techniques are combined.
result: The review demonstrates how these techniques provide direct access to atomic-scale disorder information in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Combining multiple real-space probes yields a more complete picture of defects, which is important for understanding material properties.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonance phenomena.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for astrophysics but difficult to measure directly.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches including tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: Provides an overview of the state-of-the-art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory.
conclusion: New experimental and theoretical methods are needed to study these reactions on Earth.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: To provide a self-consistent set of fundamental constants for use in physics and chemistry, updated with the latest experimental data.
method: A least-squares adjustment of data from various experiments, incorporating uncertainties and correlations.
result: A new set of recommended values for fundamental constants such as the Planck constant, elementary charge, and Boltzmann constant.
conclusion: The updated constants are essential for accurate scientific measurements and theoretical calculations.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of buckling instabilities in growing soft matter using nonlinear elasticity theory.
motivation: Understanding creases and cusps in soft materials is important for morphogenesis and materials science.
method: The review integrates bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and nonlinear elasticity to analyze the Biot instability.
result: Provides a modern treatment of buckling patterns in growing soft matter.
conclusion: Nonlinear elasticity is essential to fully describe the observed instabilities.

title: Flexible Gravitational-Wave Parameter Estimation With Transformers
authors: Annalena Kofler, Maximilian Dax, Stephen R. Green, Jonas Wildberger, Nihar Gupte, Jakob H. Macke, Jonathan Gair, Alessandra Buonanno, And Bernhard Schölkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Annalena Kofler, Maximilian Dax, Stephen R. Green, Jonas Wildberger, Nihar Gupte, Jakob H. Macke, Jonathan Gair, Alessandra Buonanno, and Bernhard Schölkopf

Gravitational-wave data analysis relies on accurate and efficient methods to extract physical information from noisy detector signals, yet the increasing rate and complexity of observations represent a growing challenge. Deep learning provides a powerful alternative to traditional inference, but exi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies transformer neural networks to gravitational-wave parameter estimation, a topic in astrophysics and deep learning.
motivation: Gravitational-wave data analysis requires accurate and efficient parameter estimation from noisy signals, and traditional methods are computationally expensive.
method: The authors develop a transformer-based deep learning model to perform flexible and fast parameter estimation from gravitational-wave data.
result: The transformer model achieves competitive accuracy and significantly faster inference compared to traditional methods.
conclusion: Deep learning, specifically transformers, offers a promising alternative for gravitational-wave parameter estimation, enabling real-time analysis.

title: Proposal For Direct Detection Of Ultralight Dark Matter Via Charged Lepton Flavor Violation
authors: Innes Bigaran, Patrick J. Fox, Yann Gouttenoire, Roni Harnik, Gordan Krnjaic, Tony Menzo, And Jure Zupan
abstract:
Author(s): Innes Bigaran, Patrick J. Fox, Yann Gouttenoire, Roni Harnik, Gordan Krnjaic, Tony Menzo, and Jure Zupan

We propose a dark matter direct-detection strategy using charged particle decays at accelerator-based experiments. If ultralight [MATH] dark matter has a misalignment abundance, its local field oscillates in time at a frequency set by its mass. If it also couples to flavor-changing …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251801] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using charged lepton flavor violation at accelerator experiments to detect ultralight dark matter.
motivation: Ultralight dark matter with misalignment abundance oscillates and may couple to flavor-changing processes, offering a new detection channel.
method: Theoretical proposal analyzing how dark matter oscillations induce charged lepton flavor violation in particle decays, detectable at accelerator-based experiments.
result: Derives sensitivity estimates for existing and future experiments, showing potential to probe new parameter space.
conclusion: Charged lepton flavor violation provides a promising direct detection strategy for ultralight dark matter.

title: Test Of $cp$ Symmetry In The Neutral Decays Of $\mathrm{Λ}$ Via $J/ψ→\mathrm{Λ}\overline{\mathrm{Λ}}$
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Using [MATH] events collected with the BESIII detector, a full angular analysis is carried out on the process [MATH]. The decay parameters [MATH] for [MATH] an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper tests CP symmetry in neutral decays of Λ hyperons using J/ψ→ΛΛ¯ events from BESIII.
motivation: CP violation is a key phenomenon in particle physics, and testing it in hyperon decays provides a sensitive probe of the Standard Model and potential new physics.
method: A full angular analysis of the decay J/ψ→ΛΛ¯ is performed using 10 billion J/ψ events collected by the BESIII detector, extracting decay parameters for Λ and Λ¯.
result: The decay parameters are measured with high precision, and CP symmetry is tested by comparing the parameters for Λ and Λ¯.
conclusion: The results are consistent with CP conservation within uncertainties, placing constraints on CP-violating effects in hyperon decays.

title: Four-Jet Rate In Electron-Positron Annihilation At Order ${α}_{s}^{4}$
authors: Xuan Chen, Dmitry Chicherin, Elliot Fox, Nigel Glover, Matteo Marcoli, Vasily Sotnikov, Huiting Sun, Hantian Zhang, And Simone Zoia
abstract:
Author(s): Xuan Chen, Dmitry Chicherin, Elliot Fox, Nigel Glover, Matteo Marcoli, Vasily Sotnikov, Huiting Sun, Hantian Zhang, and Simone Zoia

We compute for the first time the production rate for four jets in electron-positron annihilation at next-to-next-to-leading order. Our calculation exhibits the highest final-state jet multiplicity considered at this perturbative accuracy to date. The cancellation of infrared singularities is achiev…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251901] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes the four-jet production rate in electron-positron annihilation at next-to-next-to-leading order in QCD.
motivation: To achieve higher precision in jet production rates at colliders, testing perturbative QCD and improving event shape predictions.
method: Uses perturbative QCD calculations at order α_s^4, handling infrared singularities via subtraction methods.
result: First calculation of four-jet rate at NNLO accuracy, demonstrating cancellation of infrared divergences.
conclusion: Provides a new benchmark for jet multiplicity at high perturbative order, relevant for precision tests of the Standard Model.

title: Search For The $y(2175)$ In The Photoproduction Cross Section Measurement Of $γp→ϕ{π}^{+}{π}^{−}p$ At GlueX
authors: F. Afzal et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): F. Afzal et al. (The GlueX Collaboration)

Based on [MATH] of photoproduction data collected with the GlueX detector at Jefferson Lab, we have measured for the first time the cross section of the exclusive reaction [MATH] by reconstructing the final state [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251902] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first measurement of the photoproduction cross section for γp→ϕπ+π−p, searching for the Y(2175) resonance.
motivation: The Y(2175) is a suspected exotic meson; its photoproduction cross section has not been measured before, and this measurement can help clarify its nature.
method: The GlueX detector at Jefferson Lab collected photoproduction data, and the exclusive reaction γp→ϕπ+π−p was reconstructed to extract the cross section.
result: The cross section for the reaction was measured for the first time, providing new data on the Y(2175) resonance.
conclusion: The measurement contributes to understanding the Y(2175) state, but no definitive conclusion on its exotic nature is drawn.

title: Precise Qcd Predictions For Hadron-in-Jet Production In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Collisions
authors: Leonardo Bonino, Aude Gehrmann-De Ridder, Thomas Gehrmann, Alexander Huss, Francesco Merlotti, And Giovanni Stagnitto
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Bonino, Aude Gehrmann-De Ridder, Thomas Gehrmann, Alexander Huss, Francesco Merlotti, and Giovanni Stagnitto

The production of identified hadrons inside jets in [MATH] annihilation allows for detailed studies of parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions in a clean environment. We compute hadron-in-jets production cross sections for [MATH] and ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}→…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251903] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents precise QCD predictions for hadron-in-jet production in e+e- collisions, focusing on fragmentation functions.
motivation: To improve understanding of parton-to-hadron fragmentation in a clean environment and provide theoretical predictions for comparison with experimental data.
method: The authors compute next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD corrections to hadron-in-jet production cross sections in e+e- annihilation.
result: They obtain precise theoretical predictions for hadron-in-jet production, including detailed distributions and comparisons to experimental data.
conclusion: The results provide a benchmark for testing fragmentation functions and improve the accuracy of QCD predictions for jet substructure observables.

title: Low-Energy Dipole Strength Distribution In $^{102}\mathrm{Ru}$: Coexistence Of Scissors And Octupole Resonances
authors: A. Saracino, A. D. Ayangeakaa, Q. B. Chen, S. Frauendorf, S. R. Johnson, R. V. F. Janssens, E. Churchman, S. W. Finch, D. Gribble, F. E. Idoko, X. K.-H. James, T. M. Kowalewski, M. Lee, A. Psaltis, And K. Song

The dipole response of [MATH] has been investigated for the first time using nuclear resonance fluorescence, providing comprehensive and detailed information about the nucleus. The [MATH] strength, concentrated in the 3–4 MeV region, is consistent with a scissors resonance. As a surprisin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 252501] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dipole response of 102Ru using nuclear resonance fluorescence, revealing a scissors resonance and an octupole resonance.
motivation: To investigate the low-energy dipole strength distribution in 102Ru, which provides insights into nuclear structure and collective modes.
method: Nuclear resonance fluorescence (NRF) experiment to measure the dipole response.
result: The dipole strength in the 3–4 MeV region is consistent with a scissors resonance, and an unexpected octupole resonance is observed.
conclusion: The coexistence of scissors and octupole resonances in 102Ru reveals new aspects of nuclear structure.

authors: C. Cousins, G. Lotay, D. T. Doherty, D. Seweryniak, C. Sarma, C. M. Campbell, L. Canete, M. P. Carpenter, W. N. Catford, K. A. Chipps, J. Henderson, A. R. L. Kennington, T. Lauritsen, J. The observation of active [MATH] in supernova remnants offers the potential to solve one of the most debated questions in modern astrophysics, the exact underlying explosion mechanism of core collapse supernovae (CCSNe). In particular, a comparison between the predicted synthesized yield…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 252701] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nuclear reaction rates in the 45V(p,γ)46Cr process to understand 44Ti production in supernovae.
motivation: The yield of 44Ti in supernova remnants is a key observable for testing explosion models, but uncertainties in nuclear reaction rates limit its predictive power.
method: The authors identified resonant states in 46Cr via gamma-ray spectroscopy and used them to calculate the astrophysical reaction rate for 45V(p,γ)46Cr.
result: New resonances were found that significantly increase the reaction rate, affecting the predicted 44Ti yield from core-collapse supernovae.
conclusion: The updated reaction rate reduces uncertainties in 44Ti production, improving the use of 44Ti as a diagnostic for supernova explosion mechanisms.

title: Memories Of Amplitude And Direction Coexist And Compete In Non-Brownian Suspensions
authors: Surendra Padamata And Nathan C. Keim
abstract:
Author(s): Surendra Padamata and Nathan C. Keim

A new experiment elucidates the ability of some particle–fluid mixtures to behave in ways that depend on their previous flow.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 258201] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies memory effects in non-Brownian suspensions, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: Understanding how particle-fluid mixtures remember their flow history is important for predicting material behavior.
method: Experimental rheology and imaging of non-Brownian suspensions under controlled flow protocols.
result: The system exhibits coexisting and competing memories of both amplitude and direction of previous flow.
conclusion: Memory in non-Brownian suspensions is more complex than previously thought, with multiple memory types interacting.

title: Standard Model Baryon Number Violation At Zero Temperature From Higgs Bubble Collisions
authors: Nabeen Bhusal, Simone Blasi, Martina Cataldi, Aleksandr Chatrchyan, Marco Gorghetto, And Géraldine Servant
abstract:
Author(s): Nabeen Bhusal, Simone Blasi, Martina Cataldi, Aleksandr Chatrchyan, Marco Gorghetto, and Géraldine Servant

We compute for the first time baryon number violation at zero temperature from Higgs bubble collisions and find that it can be of the same order as that from thermal sphalerons in the symmetric phase at electroweak temperatures. We study the dependence of the rate of Chern-Simons number transitions …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241803] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes baryon number violation from Higgs bubble collisions at zero temperature, relevant to electroweak baryogenesis.
motivation: To understand baryon number violation mechanisms beyond thermal sphalerons, which are important for explaining the matter-antimatter asymmetry.
method: The authors compute Chern-Simons number transition rates during Higgs bubble collisions using numerical simulations and analytical estimates.
result: They find that baryon number violation from bubble collisions can be comparable to that from thermal sphalerons at electroweak temperatures.
conclusion: Higgs bubble collisions provide a new source of baryon number violation that should be considered in models of electroweak baryogenesis.

title: First Observation Of Deuteron-$\mathrm{Λ}$ Correlations At Rhic
authors: B. E. Aboona et Al.

Author(s): B. E. Aboona et al. (STAR Collaboration)

Precise experimental information on hyperon-nucleon interactions is scarce but of paramount importance to our understanding of the inner structure of compact stars. In this Letter, we report the first experimental results of correlation functions between deuterons ([MATH]) and [MATH] hyperons in …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 242303] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: First experimental observation of deuteron-Λ correlations at RHIC, providing data on hyperon-nucleon interactions.
motivation: Hyperon-nucleon interactions are poorly understood but crucial for understanding compact stars.
method: Measured correlation functions between deuterons and Λ hyperons in high-energy collisions at RHIC.
result: Reported the first experimental results of deuteron-Λ correlations.
conclusion: Provides new experimental constraints on hyperon-nucleon interactions.

title: Periodic Fracture Of Active Tissues
authors: Yue Qian, Yue Li, And Bo Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Qian, Yue Li, and Bo Li

Fracture typically signifies mechanical failure in engineering materials, whereas controlled cracking may actively sculpt tissues through precise biological regulation. Here, we establish a multiscale nonlinear peridynamic theory that accounts for cellular mechanosensing to decipher the spontaneous …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248402] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A multiscale peridynamic theory for periodic fracture in active tissues, driven by cellular mechanosensing.
motivation: Understanding how controlled cracking sculpts tissues through biological regulation, as opposed to being a sign of mechanical failure.
method: Develops a nonlinear peridynamic model incorporating cellular mechanosensing at multiple scales.
result: The model predicts spontaneous periodic fracture patterns in active tissues.
conclusion: Periodic fracture can be a biologically regulated process, not just a failure mechanism.

title: Universal Approach To Saddle-point Methods In Attosecond Science
authors: Anne Weber, Job Feldbrugge, And Emilio Pisanty
abstract:
Author(s): Anne Weber, Job Feldbrugge, and Emilio Pisanty

Light-matter interactions within the strong-field regime, where intense laser fields can ionize a target via tunneling, give rise to fascinating phenomena such as the generation of high-order harmonic radiation (HHG) and, correspondingly, light pulses of attosecond duration. On the atomic scale, the…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063111] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a universal saddle-point method for attosecond science, focusing on strong-field light-matter interactions and high-harmonic generation.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for saddle-point methods used in attosecond physics, which are important for understanding strong-field phenomena like tunneling ionization and high-harmonic generation.
method: The authors generalize saddle-point techniques to handle complex trajectories and multi-dimensional integrals arising in attosecond science, likely using analytic continuation and numerical integration.
result: A universal approach that improves accuracy and applicability of saddle-point methods for attosecond phenomena, enabling better modeling of strong-field processes.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a robust tool for theoretical and computational studies in attosecond science, with potential to advance understanding of ultrafast light-matter interactions.

title: Stark Effect In Molecular Rydberg States: Calculation Of Rydberg-Stark Manifolds Of ${\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}$ Including Fine And Hyperfine Structures
authors: I. Doran, L. Jeckel, M. Beyer, Ch. Jungen, And F. Merkt
abstract:
Author(s): I. Doran, L. Jeckel, M. Beyer, Ch. Jungen, and F. Merkt

We present a general theoretical treatment and calculations of the fine and hyperfine structures in the spectra of high-[MATH] molecular Rydberg states in static uniform electric fields. The treatment combines (i) multichannel quantum-defect theory and long-range polarization models to determine the fi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062812] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a theoretical treatment and calculations of fine and hyperfine structures in molecular Rydberg states under static electric fields.
motivation: Understanding Stark effects in molecular Rydberg states is important for spectroscopy and molecular physics.
method: The authors combine multichannel quantum-defect theory with long-range polarization models to compute Stark manifolds including fine and hyperfine structures.
result: They provide detailed calculations for H2 and D2 molecules, showing how Stark shifts and splittings depend on quantum numbers and field strength.
conclusion: The work advances theoretical modeling of high-lying molecular Rydberg states in electric fields, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

We develop a theoretical framework for time-modulated acoustic metasurfaces comprising a line array of modulated cavities, and show that bound acoustic surface waves can undergo temporal diffraction from bound states localized at an interface into bulk waves. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 224317] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for time-modulated acoustic metasurfaces, demonstrating that bound acoustic surface waves can diffract into bulk waves via temporal modulation.
motivation: To understand and control the conversion of bound surface waves into propagating bulk waves using time-varying acoustic metasurfaces.
method: The authors derive the dispersion relation for a line array of modulated cavities and analyze temporal diffraction of bound states into the continuum.
result: They show that time modulation enables bound acoustic surface waves to couple to bulk waves, effectively radiating into the continuum.
conclusion: Time-varying acoustic metasurfaces provide a mechanism for controlling wave radiation from surface-bound states, with potential applications in acoustic wave manipulation.

title: Effects Of Electric Field Rising Time On Polarization Switching In Ferroelectrics
authors: Bowen Li, Jinhong Li, Wenpeng Zhu, Haohua Wen, And Yue Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Bowen Li, Jinhong Li, Wenpeng Zhu, Haohua Wen, and Yue Zheng

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224112] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of electric field rising time on polarization switching in ferroelectrics using stochastic phase-field simulations.
motivation: The electric field rising time is often overlooked in ultrafast ferroelectric switching studies, but it critically influences switching dynamics and mechanism discrimination.
method: Stochastic phase-field simulations are used to systematically investigate the effects of rising time on polarization switching.
result: The rising time significantly affects the switching behavior and can alter the dominant switching mechanism.
conclusion: Rising time must be considered in ultrafast ferroelectric switching experiments to correctly interpret dynamics.

title: Nonlinear Bubble Resonance: Geometric Mechanisms And Onset Scaling
authors: Shilin Yu, Wenbao Zheng, Chao Zeng, And Wen Deng

The oscillatory dynamics of trapped nonwetting fluids in pore constrictions influence multiphase flow and transient fluid mobility in geologic media. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 065109] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear bubble resonance in pore constrictions, focusing on geometric mechanisms and onset scaling.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear oscillatory dynamics of trapped nonwetting fluids is important for multiphase flow in geologic media, but the mechanism for finite-amplitude nonlinear behavior is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the oscillatory dynamics theoretically and/or numerically, identifying geometric mechanisms that lead to nonlinear resonance and deriving scaling laws for the onset of nonlinearity.
result: They reveal the geometric mechanisms responsible for nonlinear bubble resonance and characterize the scaling of the onset amplitude.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into nonlinear fluid behavior in porous media, which may have implications for multiphase flow and fluid mobility.

title: From Spark To Conflagration: A Multiscale Thermodynamic-percolation Framework For Wildland-fire Spread
authors: Xiaoping Shi, Mir Faizal, Arshid Shabir, And Behnam Pourhassan
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoping Shi, Mir Faizal, Arshid Shabir, and Behnam Pourhassan

Wildland fire operates across multiple spatial and temporal scales, linking local combustion chemistry and turbulent heat transport to continental patterns of burned area. A quantitative bridge between microscale ignition physics and macroscale propagation has remained elusive because operational si…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064143] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a multiscale thermodynamic-percolation framework for wildland-fire spread, bridging microscale ignition to macroscale propagation.
motivation: A quantitative bridge between microscale ignition physics and macroscale fire propagation has been missing in operational models.
method: The authors combine thermodynamic principles with percolation theory across multiple spatial and temporal scales.
result: The framework successfully links local combustion and heat transport to large-scale burned area patterns.
conclusion: The multiscale model provides a new quantitative tool for understanding and predicting wildland-fire spread.

title: Evolution Of Localized Pulses In The Defocusing Modified Korteweg–de Vries Equation Theory
authors: L. F. Calazans de Brito, A. Gammal, And A. M. Kamchatnov

In this work, we develop, in the Gurevich-Pitaevskii framework, an analytic theory for the evolution of localized pulses in the defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation theory for situations when a dispersive shock does not eventually transform into a sequence of well-separated solitons. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064208] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytic theory for the evolution of localized pulses in the defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation, focusing on dispersive shock waves and soliton dynamics.
motivation: To understand the evolution of localized pulses in nonlinear wave systems where dispersive shocks do not break into solitons.
method: Uses the Gurevich-Pitaevskii framework to derive analytic solutions for pulse evolution.
result: Provides analytic descriptions of pulse dynamics and dispersive shock formation in the defocusing mKdV equation.
conclusion: The theory successfully describes pulse evolution in regimes where soliton formation is suppressed.

title: Effect Of Temporary Lockdowns On Disease Extinction Risk In Assortative Networks
authors: Elad Korngut And Michael Assaf
abstract:
Author(s): Elad Korngut and Michael Assaf

Changing environmental conditions can significantly affect the dynamics of disease spread. These changes may arise naturally or result from human interventions; in the latter case, lockdown measures that lead to abrupt but temporary reductions in transmission rates are used to combat disease spread.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064309] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of temporary lockdowns on disease extinction in assortative networks using stochastic modeling.
motivation: Understanding how temporary lockdowns affect disease extinction risk is crucial for public health policy, especially in structured populations.
method: The authors develop a stochastic model of disease spread on assortative networks and analyze the probability of extinction under temporary lockdowns using branching process approximations and simulations.
result: Temporary lockdowns can significantly increase extinction probability, but the effect depends on network assortativity and timing of interventions.
conclusion: Optimal lockdown strategies should consider network structure to maximize extinction probability while minimizing duration.

title: Dynamic Stabilization Of The Isolated Internal Defect In The Presence Of A Temporally Modulated Laser Prepulse
authors: Y. Z. Han, K. G. Zhao, Z. Y. Li, Y. X. Liu, C. Xue, J. W. Li, Z. Chen, J. Q. Dong, J. F. Wu, L. F. Wang, And W. Y. Zhang

tldr: This paper studies dynamic stabilization of hydrodynamic instabilities seeded by internal defects in inertial confinement fusion using temporally modulated laser prepulses.
motivation: Hydrodynamic instabilities from isolated internal defects limit performance in inertial confinement fusion experiments.
method: The authors extend the concept of dynamic stabilization via temporally modulated laser pulses from the main drive to the prepulse regime.
result: The modulated prepulse can stabilize the growth of perturbations seeded by internal defects.
conclusion: Dynamic stabilization using modulated laser prepulses is a promising approach to mitigate defect-seeded instabilities in fusion experiments.

title: Self-propelled Droplet Dynamics On Superhydrophobic Surfaces Under Low-pressure Conditions

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065506] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of self-propelled droplets on superhydrophobic surfaces under low pressure, focusing on fluid mechanics and surface engineering.
motivation: Understanding droplet self-removal under low pressure is important for extreme-environment surface engineering applications.
method: High-speed photography and quantitative analysis are used to observe ethylene glycol-water solution droplets on irregular micro-nanostructured superhydrophobic surfaces.
result: The study reveals unique droplet dynamics under low-pressure conditions, including self-propelled motion.
conclusion: The findings provide insights for designing surfaces that promote droplet removal in low-pressure environments.

title: Plume Stretching In The Trapped Region Of A Reoriented Potential Mixer
authors: Roseanna M. Neupauer, James D. Meiss, And Tomás G. Dabove
abstract:
Author(s): Roseanna M. Neupauer, James D. Meiss, and Tomás G. Dabove

The reoriented potential mixer (RPM) can enhance mixing and reaction during in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater, in which a chemical or biological amendment is introduced into a contaminant plume to react with and degrade the contaminant. tldr: This paper studies fluid mixing in a reoriented potential mixer for groundwater remediation, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Enhance in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater by improving mixing and reaction between introduced amendments and contaminant plumes.
method: Analyzes plume stretching in the trapped region of a reoriented potential mixer using dipole flow and numerical simulations.
result: Quantifies stretching dynamics and mixing efficiency in the trapped region under reoriented potential mixing.
conclusion: The reoriented potential mixer can improve mixing in trapped regions, aiding remediation efforts.

authors: Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, And James E. Sprittles

This work investigates the oscillatory dynamics and subsequent sustained bouncing behavior of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a phenomenon that has received little theoretical attention to date. Building on previous approaches toward drop impacts and Leidenfrost drops, a computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing.

result: The model reveals an elastic surface-wave instability that sustains bouncing.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for a previously unexplored bouncing regime in Leidenfrost hydrogels.

This work aims to study the resynchronization of CR flagella after a high light intensity stimulus, known as photoshock. The synchronization is estimated thanks to a qu…

title: When Surface Dynamics Fakes Symmetry: Oxygen On Rh(100) Revisited
authors: Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, And M. Alexander Schneider

Heating a long-range ordered adsorbate phase beyond its stability temperature does not necessarily result in a disordered phase; it can also break up into heavily fluctuating ordered domains. Temporal and/or spatial averaging over these fluctuations may give the impression of both a wrong periodicit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023296] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oxygen adsorption on Rh(100) surface, revealing that fluctuating ordered domains can mimic a wrong surface symmetry under thermal averaging.
motivation: To understand the behavior of adsorbate phases beyond their stability temperature and correct misinterpretations of surface symmetry from diffraction patterns.
method: Combined experimental techniques (STM, LEED, XRD) and theoretical modeling to analyze the structure and dynamics of oxygen on Rh(100).
result: Heating the ordered phase leads to heavily fluctuating domains that, upon averaging, produce a diffraction pattern suggesting a different symmetry than the true local structure.
conclusion: Surface dynamics can fake symmetry, emphasizing the need for careful analysis of fluctuating systems in surface science.

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023287] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.

motivation: To understand and control the formation of microjets from laser-driven shock waves in droplets, which is relevant for industrial applications like EUV light sources.
method: Experimental: two laser pulses create interfering shock waves in a tin microdroplet, and high-speed imaging captures the resulting jet dynamics.
result: The interference of two shock waves can be tuned to control the direction and velocity of the microjet.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein

tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically demonstrate super-resonance in a system of coupled resonators, showing that a broadband out-of-phase response can be maintained beyond the usual bandwidth.
result: Super-resonance achieves a broadband response that significantly exceeds the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling effective flow stabilization.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems with potential applications in flow control and other areas requiring broadband response.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electric fields, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism can improve reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: A detailed model emerges where tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights can guide the design of more robust accelerator structures and other high-power technologies.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A review of hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction physics.
motivation: To understand strong interaction mechanisms such as quark confinement and gluon binding through the study of charmonium decays and searches for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BABAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on hadron production in e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: Summarizes current progress and highlights recent advances from BESIII, which has become the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: The study of open-charm meson pairs provides crucial insights into QCD and hadron spectroscopy, with BESIII playing a key role.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz

motivation: To honor the Arecibo Observatory's contributions and impact on various scientific fields.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: To document the contributions of the Arecibo planetary radar system to planetary science and its role in supporting space exploration.
method: The paper is a colloquium-style review summarizing radar techniques and key observational results for Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: It highlights unique subsurface and surface insights provided by radar, which complemented other observational methods and guided in situ missions.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary science, and its loss leaves a gap in capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the scientific legacy of the Arecibo Observatory after its collapse.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Highlights Arecibo's major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's unique capabilities and upgrades enabled groundbreaking discoveries across multiple fields.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The paper synthesizes experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud microphysics.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can generate turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising platform to address the long-standing bottleneck in cloud physics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare events that provide unique insights into stellar physics and neutron star formation; detecting gravitational waves alongside photons and neutrinos is a key goal.
method: The paper summarizes recent supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents the latest progress in modeling and detection strategies for gravitational waves from core collapse supernovae.
conclusion: The review highlights the potential of multimessenger observations to reveal the supernova central engine and neutron star physics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a cosmological observation that challenges the standard ΛCDM model, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale matter distribution with the cosmic microwave background dipole.
method: Analysis of radio galaxy and quasar catalogs to measure the dipole anisotropy and compare it to the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, challenging the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require new physics beyond ΛCDM.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their observational signatures.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test beyond-standard-model physics through astrophysical observations.
method: Review of theoretical models of self-interacting dark matter and comparison with observational data from galaxies to large-scale structures.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, but more precise astrophysical tests are needed to distinguish it from other models.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard Model physics, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a review of viable models and future discovery potential.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery prospects for the HL-LHC across multiple search channels and well-motivated scenarios.
result: The review identifies remaining viable supersymmetric models and estimates the HL-LHC's sensitivity to them.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains a compelling framework, but its discovery at the HL-LHC depends on the specific model and requires dedicated searches.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions and their astrophysical implications.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting solar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models and experimental data from the last decade on nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and atomic effects in the solar interior.
result: Updated reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic observations.
conclusion: The review consolidates recent advances in nuclear astrophysics of hydrogen burning, providing a benchmark for solar modeling.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: A review of gas bubble dynamics in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and surfactants.
motivation: Gas bubbles are important in many natural and industrial processes, but their dynamics are complex due to deformability and interactions.
method: The paper reviews recent advances in experimental and theoretical studies of bubble motion, including effects of turbulence, rheology, and surfactants.
result: Key advances over the past 20 years are summarized, highlighting the influence of liquid properties and flow conditions on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The review provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers deep-tissue optical contrast with high resolution.
method: The paper reviews the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, where short laser pulses cause temperature rise and generate ultrasound waves detected externally.
result: The technique enables noninvasive imaging millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, and multimodal combinations with optical microscopy are discussed.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical research, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of using gravitational waves to probe the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: Gravitational waves can penetrate the early universe's opaque plasma, offering a unique window into the first second after the Big Bang.
method: The paper reviews theoretical signals from cosmological sources like phase transitions and topological defects, and discusses detection strategies for stochastic gravitational waves.
result: It summarizes possible gravitational wave signatures from early universe events and outlines detection methods.
conclusion: Gravitational waves provide a promising tool to study the earliest moments of the universe, complementing electromagnetic observations.
